description: Two teams play a cross-ice 2-on-2 between two nets. When the defending team gains possession, it must make an outlet to its waiting line at the blue line; the previous offensive pair immediately tracks and backchecks as the new attackers go the other direction.
coaching_points: Transition immediately when possession changes.
Outlet players present a clear target and attack on receipt instead of standing still.
The previous attackers sprint back through the middle and identify coverage early.
Run it as 2-on-2 or 3-on-3 while keeping shifts short and fast.

title: Offense then Backcheck to DZC
description: A five-player unit attacks in one end until the whistle, then immediately backchecks the full length into its defensive zone where a fresh offensive five is waiting. The sequence continues end to end to rehearse offensive-zone habits, tracking, and defensive-zone coverage.
coaching_points: First player back pressures the puck; second protects the front of the net.
Third player supports the corner battle, fourth protects the middle slot, and the last fills the strong-side wing area.
Backcheck in direct lines toward defensive responsibilities instead of drifting toward the puck.
On offense, find the puck, provide close support, and attack the net.

title: Alternate 1 on 1 x 3
description: Players attack three consecutive 1-on-1 situations from different parts of the offensive zone. A second progression uses the same setup to build from 1-on-1 into 2-on-1 and then 2-on-2 as players join the next phase after each rep.
coaching_points: Defenders keep sticks in lanes and angle attackers toward the outside.
Forwards protect the puck and work off the wall to create a lane to the net.
Attack with speed instead of settling for a low-percentage outside shot.
Progress to the 2-on-1 and 2-on-2 version once the individual angling reads are clean.

title: 4 v 3 Pass Between 2 Players
description: Four attackers play against three defenders in-zone. The offense earns the right to shoot only after completing a pass between two defenders to a teammate who is moving, forcing timing, deception, support, and constant off-puck movement.
coaching_points: Offensive players keep moving and communicate before the passing lane opens.
Players without the puck time cuts through or behind defenders instead of standing in space.
Defenders keep sticks on the ice and protect the middle.
Reward both successful seam passes and goals to reinforce the intended read.

title: Triangle Passing Progression with 3 Players
description: Three players form a triangle and progress through one-touch passing patterns. Start with one puck, emphasize quiet controlled receptions and forehand targets, then advance to two and three pucks to increase scanning and timing demands.
coaching_points: Keep sticks on the ice as clear targets.
Pass to the receiver's forehand whenever possible to set up the next one-touch play.
Make each reception quiet and controlled rather than stabbing at the puck.
Add multiple pucks only after the group can maintain rhythm with one.

title: Designated Shooters Umbrella Power Play Game
description: Two teams battle 2-on-2 or 3-on-3 around back-to-back nets while each side has designated umbrella point players. The team in possession can use the point players for give-and-go plays, one-timers, shots through traffic, and tips.
coaching_points: Use the point players, then move immediately to open ice for the return option.
Point players move the puck quickly and look for one-timers or tip passes.
Defenders box out, eliminate sticks, and let the goalie see the puck.
Keep defensive sticks in lanes and force the puck toward the outside.

title: Red Baron Game
description: Teams play 3-on-3 cross-ice with one neutral Red Baron who always joins the team in possession, creating a continuous 4-on-3 offensive advantage whenever the puck changes hands.
coaching_points: Offense spreads out and uses the extra player instead of forcing plays through pressure.
Support the puck carrier on both sides so the 4-on-3 advantage stays usable.
Defenders keep sticks in lanes and protect the middle.
Transition quickly when possession changes because the neutral player switches sides immediately.

title: Cross Fire Possession Game
description: Two players from each team compete inside a square while teammates are positioned on opposite outside edges. A team scores by moving the puck from one outside player, through support inside the box, to its teammate on the far side.
coaching_points: Protect the puck until a clean play is available.
Move immediately after passing to create the next support lane.
Use give-and-go plays instead of standing after the pass.
Adjust the square size to match the players' skill level.

title: Seven Pass 2 on 1
description: A high-tempo full-ice sequence uses at least seven passes before two forwards attack the defenseman who started the rep. The defenseman also receives a cross-zone pass for a quick shot, recovers ice, and then defends the returning 2-on-1.
coaching_points: Communicate throughout the passing sequence and present clear targets.
Headman the puck so the lead forward stays ahead of the play.
Defenseman gets the shot off quickly, then recovers gap before the rush arrives.
Enter the final 2-on-1 with speed and force the defender to make a decision.

title: 6 Pass Shooting Drill
description: A half-ice sequence creates six passes before the final shot. Players work one-touch exchanges, pivots, handling the puck while moving backward, changing passing angles, and receiving the final pass high in the zone for a shot.
coaching_points: Keep the feet moving through the entire rep, including the shot.
Show a clear target and communicate for each pass.
Use one-touch passes when the lane and timing are available.
The corner player opens up on the breakout-style pass instead of firing blindly up the wall.

title: Continuous One Touch Shooting Drill
description: A player from the blue-line line exchanges repeated one-touch passes with a stationary goal-line player while skating down, transitioning up the wall, and curling into the slot. The final reception becomes a quick shot, and both players drive the net before rotating.
coaching_points: Make flat passes with soft hands instead of slapping at the puck.
Transition while facing the puck throughout the route.
Receive and shoot in one motion in the slot.
Both players follow the shot to the net for rebounds.

title: Four Corners Possession Game
description: Two players from each team compete in the middle while one teammate from each side is fixed inside designated corner boxes. Teams score points by completing clean passes to their corner players while maintaining possession.
coaching_points: Play with the head up to identify the next scoring option before receiving.
Protect the puck first when pressure removes the immediate pass.
Use both verbal and non-verbal communication with teammates.
Rotate inside and corner players every short shift to keep pace high.

title: Shoot Around The Traffic!
description: A three-part shooting progression teaches players to move the puck around traffic before releasing. Players push or pull around an obstacle, add escape moves while moving backward or forward, and then time a jump into open ice for the shot.
coaching_points: Keep the head up while moving the puck around traffic.
Receive, move, shoot—avoid unnecessary stickhandling before release.
When moving backward, pull the puck toward the toe caps to clear the obstacle sooner.
Communicate for passes and shoot to a target rather than simply throwing the puck at the net.

title: Cloverleaf - Cutting Hands
description: Players work through a cloverleaf pattern around four markers, first without a puck, then with a puck, and finally with passive pressure. The progression emphasizes hand position, blade control, and foot placement through tight control turns.
coaching_points: Close the blade through each turn so the puck stays connected to the stick.
Keep the inside leg in front to help shield the puck.
Separate the hands enough to control forehand and backhand turns.
Master the footwork first, then add the puck and passive pressure.

title: Quick 2 vs 1 Attack Situational Drill
description: A passer starts the rep to one of two forwards, who cross and attack immediately in a tight 2-on-1. The drill recreates an offensive-zone turnover where the attacking team must transition to the net before the defender can reset.
coaching_points: Puck carrier attacks quickly and uses width, drop options, or deception to create a lane.
Off-puck forward reads the play, communicates, and jumps into available space.
Defender protects the middle and forces a poor-angle shot when possible.
Defender keeps the blade flat in the lane instead of sweeping the stick.

title: Deceptive Point Shooting Progression
description: Defensemen work three point-shooting progressions designed to move the puck around pressure and find a clean lane. Reps include pulling from backhand to forehand, changing the release point around a coach, and using a shot fake before escaping to a new lane.
coaching_points: Keep the head up while receiving and moving laterally.
Explode after the puck move to create separation from the shot blocker.
Get the shot off quickly once the lane opens.
Add tips, screens, or a net-driving forward once the shooting movement is clean.

title: Give & Go Rover
description: Two players compete inside a small box with one neutral rover. After gaining possession, a player earns a point by passing to the rover, moving into open space, and receiving the return pass.
coaching_points: Protect the puck until the passing lane is available.
Pass and immediately move to new space for the return.
Keep every player moving—no standing after the puck changes hands.
Adjust the box size to increase or reduce pressure.

title: Eagles Half Ice 2 on 1
description: Two forwards begin with separate pass-and-shot touches, then work into a breakout and timed middle-support route. The pair exits the zone, regroups through the neutral area and attacks back 2-on-1 against the defenseman.
coaching_points: Time the middle support route so the breakout receiver has a clean second option.
Move the puck before pressure closes and attack the return rush with speed.
Defenseman recovers through the middle, establishes gap and protects the passing lane.
Both forwards finish at the net after the 2-on-1.

title: Quarter Ice 3 vs. 3
description: Three players per side compete in a tight quarter-ice game with the two nets set on opposite sides of a faceoff circle. One player from each team is restricted to the defensive half of the circle while two teammates work the offensive side.
coaching_points: Use quick puck movement because time and space disappear fast.
Off-puck players create passing lanes instead of standing beside the puck carrier.
Defenders stay goal-side and communicate through switches.
Keep shifts short and competitive to maintain pace.

title: Ring It 1 on 1
description: A forward rims the puck around the boards to a teammate on the opposite side. The receiver transitions inside-out to collect it in motion and attacks up ice while the defenseman times the route, closes gap and defends the zone entry.
coaching_points: Receiver times the route so the puck is collected with speed rather than from a standstill.
Use the wall cleanly and accelerate immediately after possession.
Defenseman keeps inside positioning and closes the gap before the blue line.
Forward attacks the defender's feet and uses speed or deception to gain the zone.

title: Cross, Poke, Shoot
description: Defensemen work lateral footwork and poke checks on two loose pucks, transition backward around a marker, then receive a coach pass while moving backward before controlling the puck and getting a hard shot through from the blue line.
coaching_points: Stay balanced through the lateral crossover and poke-check movements.
Recover quickly to backward skating after each puck touch.
Receive the pass under control while moving backward, then walk toward the middle when possible.
Get the shot off quickly and through the shooting lane.

title: 3 v 2 Backside Ice Balance
description: Three attackers play against two defenders and continually rotate through puck-carrier, support, and backside roles as the puck changes sides. The goal is to keep a weak-side option available and preserve offensive ice balance.
coaching_points: Keep a player available on the weak side of the ice.
Rotate roles as the puck changes sides rather than following the puck.
Support underneath and beside the puck carrier with useful spacing.
Use the backside option to stretch defenders and create the next attack.

title: 1 v 2 with Backside Presence
description: Two players work together to win a puck from one opponent along the wall. Once possession is established, they immediately find a third player positioned on the backside for a shot before rotating into the next rep.
coaching_points: Win the wall battle in tandem instead of both players attacking independently.
First secure possession, then immediately scan away from pressure.
Move the puck to the weak side before the defense can recover.
Rotate quickly so the next battle begins without delay.

title: 3 v 2 Improve the Advantage
description: A three-player offensive group begins with a numerical advantage against two defenders and must create an additional advantage through speed, spacing, routes, or getting behind coverage before attacking.
coaching_points: Do more than simply use the extra player—create another advantage inside the 3-on-2.
Generate speed away from the puck so receivers attack with momentum.
Use routes and positioning to manipulate defenders.
Recognize opportunities to get behind coverage rather than staying in front of it.

title: 3 v 3 Using the Weak Side for Possession
description: Two players per team compete for possession while a third teammate remains available on the weak side. The offense uses the backside player to escape pressure, spread the defense, and keep possession moving across the available space.
coaching_points: Avoid bunching around the puck.
Find the weak-side teammate before forcing a puck into pressure.
Move after every pass so the next support option is already forming.
Use patience and multiple sides of the ice to keep possession.

title: Utah Surf Transition
description: A multi-part full-ice transition sequence develops defensive surfing, tracking, retrievals, and immediate counterattack. It progresses from an angled takeaway into an outlet and shot, then a tracked 2-on-1, and finishes with a full-ice 3-on-2.
coaching_points: Defenders surf from inside position and dictate the route instead of backing in passively.
Tracking forwards reload above the puck and stay connected from behind.
Retrieve loose pucks under control and transition them immediately to an outlet.
Protect the dots, match speed through the gap, and attack quickly when possession changes.

title: 1 v 1 Skate Touch Battle to 2 v 1
description: Two players race to a loose puck and battle 1-on-1, with the first touch required to be made with a skate. The winner moves the puck back to a teammate and immediately joins that player to create a 2-on-1 entry.
coaching_points: Win body position before reaching for the puck.
Use the skate deliberately on the first touch to control the loose puck.
After winning possession, move the puck and join the attack immediately.
Turn the skill win into a fast 2-on-1 before the defender can reset.

title: Skate Touch Warm Up
description: Players work inside a circle and must make their first touch on every puck with a skate. Once the puck is controlled, they transition into normal puck play and look to create a shot.
coaching_points: Make the first touch intentionally with a skate instead of letting the puck simply hit the foot.
Work both feet and different receiving angles.
Transition from skate control to the stick quickly.
After control is established, move immediately into an offensive play.

title: Buffalo 4 v 3 Continuous D Activation
description: Three forwards per team play between two repositioned nets with defensemen stationed behind each attack. A team must move the puck to its defense before attacking; one defenseman then activates to create a continuous 4-on-3.
coaching_points: Defensemen read controlled possession before committing to the rush.
Use D-to-D movement to change the activation lane.
The activating defender arrives as a useful second wave instead of following directly behind the puck.
Transition immediately when possession changes and maintain four-player spacing.

title: Alberni Valley Power Play Game
description: A power-play group works against an outnumbered penalty kill in a transition game built around possession-based entries. Attackers retrieve below the repositioned net, create support around the puck, enter against pressure, and then play live in the attacking space.
coaching_points: Give the puck carrier multiple support options during the entry.
Use the numerical advantage to possess instead of forcing the first available lane.
Penalty killers pressure with active sticks while maintaining a connected wedge or triangle.
Once inside, spread the attack and stay creative with puck movement.

title: 2v1 4v2
description: The sequence begins with two forwards attacking one defenseman, then immediately flips into a four-player rush against two new defenders. The high forward from the 4-on-2 tracks back to pressure the next 2-on-1, creating a continuous offense-to-defense transition drill.
coaching_points: Attack the opening 2-on-1 with speed and force the defender to make a decision.
Defenseman manages gap and protects the most dangerous lane.
React immediately when the whistle changes the situation into a 4-on-2.
The high forward tracks hard through the middle and applies back pressure on the next rush.

title: 1, 2, 3 Bumper Game
description: Two teams battle 2-on-2 for possession while each team has an offensive-only bumper across the top of the zone. The team that wins the puck can attack after carrying below the goal line or using its bumper to create a give-and-go or weak-side scoring chance.
coaching_points: Use the bumper to relieve pressure and create a new attack lane.
Move immediately after passing so the give-and-go stays available.
Defenders protect the middle with active sticks and recover loose pucks quickly.
Transition to offense immediately after winning possession.

title: Wrap Puck Protection Progression
description: A wall-retrieval progression that starts with a rimmed puck and a direct attack to the net, then adds a support pass to a teammate arriving from the point. Light pressure can be added so the retriever must scan, protect the puck and find the open option.
coaching_points: Shoulder-check before arriving at the puck.
Get the puck off the wall and into protected space quickly.
The support player communicates and arrives as a clear passing option.
Progress from a direct net attack to a quick pass-and-shot under pressure.

title: Big Man Cycle 2 on 1
description: A three-part sequence that begins with a pressured corner retrieval, becomes a low 2-on-1 using the wall and net for protection, and then expands into a full-ice 2-on-1. The drill links puck protection, support and defensive gap control.
coaching_points: Use the boards and net to shield the puck and create separation.
Support underneath the puck before attacking the scoring lane.
The defender keeps the stick in the passing lane and protects the middle.
On the full-ice rush, gap up early, pivot under control and match the attackers' speed.

title: Alternating 4 V 3 Power Play Game
description: A cross-ice 4-on-3 special-teams game where the numerical advantage flips to the other team on each whistle. The extra-player group works on spacing and support while the short-handed group protects the middle and looks to counter quickly.
coaching_points: The power-play group spreads the area and gives the puck carrier multiple support options.
The penalty-kill group keeps sticks in lanes and forces play outside.
Change roles immediately when the whistle flips the advantage.
Reward possession decisions and quick puck movement instead of forcing low-percentage shots.

title: Horseshoe Defensive Gap Progression
description: A two-part full-ice gap progression that teaches defenders to match an attacker's speed and influence the rush toward the outside. The second progression changes the defender's route and adds an inside pivot before the angle.
coaching_points: Defenders match speed before trying to close space.
Maintain inside position and steer the attacker away from middle ice.
Forwards change pace and route instead of skating a predictable straight line.
Begin without sticks if needed, then add stick positioning once the footwork is clean.

title: Defend the Bucket
description: A no-stick body-positioning game inside a faceoff circle. The offensive player uses changes of direction and deception to reach a bucket in the middle while the defender shadows, maintains gap and protects the inside lane.
coaching_points: Defend with feet and positioning instead of reaching or grabbing.
Stay square and avoid crossing the feet when the attacker changes direction.
Maintain a workable gap without backing directly into the target.
The attacker uses deception and direction changes rather than trying to run through the defender.

title: 2 on 2 Box Out
description: A two-part drill that starts with a net-front 2-on-2 battle off a point shot and then sends the same forwards up ice against the point defenders in a 2-on-2 rush. An optional regroup can be added before the rush.
coaching_points: Defenders establish inside position, eliminate sticks and clear rebounds.
Forwards fight for net-front leverage and find soft areas for tips and rebounds.
On the rush, attackers use width, pace changes and passing instead of skating directly at defenders.
Defensemen maintain a tight gap, keep sticks in lanes and angle the attack outside.

title: Dinks Warm Up
description: A full-ice warm-up built around a defenseman retrieval and a controlled bump pass off the wall. The breakout continues through middle ice into a wide entry before the defenseman joins late for a shot with traffic at the net.
coaching_points: The retrieving defenseman shoulder-checks before collecting the puck.
The center communicates the wall-bump option and presents a clear target.
The puck carrier works to gain middle ice before moving the puck wide.
Everyone follows the play to the net for a tip, screen or rebound.

title: D Scissor to 2 on 1
description: A three-part full-ice progression that combines low-zone support, low-to-high puck movement and a defenseman scissor before finishing with a 2-on-1 rush. The sequence forces players to create support quickly and transition from zone play into the rush.
coaching_points: Communicate early and present sticks as clear passing targets.
Create support below the puck before moving it low-to-high.
Defensemen time the scissor so the puck carrier has a useful second option.
On the final 2-on-1, attack with pace while the defender protects the middle and manages gap.

title: 3 v 3 Neutral Zone Rush Attack Game
description: A full-ice 3-on-3 transition game where one group begins the rush from behind its net while three defenders step up through the neutral zone. Both groups play live after the entry, creating repeated rush-attack, gap and transition decisions.
coaching_points: Attack with pace and width before the defense can establish a comfortable gap.
Defenders keep sticks in lanes and angle the rush toward the outside.
Communicate through the neutral zone so support stays connected.
On turnovers, transition immediately instead of drifting out of the play.

title: Continuous In Zone 3 vs. 3 Game
description: A continuous in-zone 3-on-3 where the defending trio stays for the next shift after possession changes. The format creates fatigue and forces players to maintain defensive habits, communicate and protect possession under pressure.
coaching_points: Defenders stay connected and keep sticks in useful lanes even when tired.
Protect the puck until a real play is available instead of forcing possession away.
Communicate through every change of possession.
Transition quickly because the former attacking group immediately becomes the next defending group.

title: Thread The Needle Passing Game
description: A keep-away passing game played around a faceoff circle with a small target gate in the middle. The offensive group must move the puck and create a lane through the center gate while one or two defenders protect the interior.
coaching_points: Scan before receiving so the next pass is already identified.
Move after every pass to create a new angle around the circle.
Use eyes, stick and body position to sell false passing lanes.
Defenders keep sticks on the ice and protect the middle without chasing outside the area.

title: Neutral Zone Angle 2 V 2 to 3 V 2
description: A neutral-zone attack and angling drill that begins 2-on-2 and can progress to 3-on-2. Attackers must make a play instead of dumping the puck while defenders step up, manage gap and try to end the rush before the offensive blue line.
coaching_points: Defenders match speed, maintain inside position and angle toward the wall.
Keep defensive sticks in lanes and close through the hands when the gap is right.
Attackers use width, cutbacks and give-and-go support instead of skating straight at defenders.
Keep the drill continuous so players repeatedly transition between attack and defend reads.

title: Neutral Zone Bump Back 1 vs. 1
description: A full-ice 1-on-1 flow drill where the forward exchanges a bump-back pass with a stationary player at the red line before attacking the defender from the opposite end. The defender advances into the neutral zone, then transitions backward to establish gap.
coaching_points: Start with firm tape-to-tape passes.
The attacking forward gets off the wall to create more options through the neutral zone.
The defender retakes ice before pivoting rather than backing up too early.
Transition through the middle and match the attacker's speed before closing the gap.

title: 3 Part Wrist Shot Progression
description: A three-step wrist-shot teaching progression that moves from stationary mechanics to shooting in motion and then to shooting after receiving a pass. The sequence lets players establish clean mechanics before adding timing and movement.
coaching_points: Keep the hands away from the body so the stick can load and release cleanly.
Keep the puck in a usable shooting position rather than too far ahead or behind the feet.
Transfer weight through the shot and finish the follow-through toward the target.
When adding a pass, present a clear target and prepare the puck for a quick release.

title: Stick Lift to Attack Drill
description: A neutral-zone skill sequence that combines passing, a quick stick lift, puck recovery and an immediate attack. After winning the puck, the player exchanges passes, swings into support and finishes by protecting the puck around pressure before shooting.
coaching_points: Show a clear target and communicate on every pass.
Make the stick lift quick and controlled, then secure the puck immediately.
Move the feet through the support route instead of gliding into the pass.
Use hips and body position to protect the puck on the final attack.

title: Continuous 1 vs. 1 Battle Game
description: A continuous 1-on-1 game where each attacking forward becomes the next defender. The format creates repeated puck-protection battles while the defender works under fatigue to angle the puck outside and end the shift with a clean recovery or exit.
coaching_points: Forwards protect the puck until a real scoring lane opens.
Defenders keep the stick down and angle the attacker away from the middle.
Finish every battle through the rebound or puck recovery.
Transition immediately from offense to defense when the rep changes.

title: Wallee 2 vs. 2 Scoring & Defending Game
description: A continuous narrow-ice 2-on-2 game with an offense-to-defense-to-rest rotation. A defensive recovery and outlet launches the next pair down ice while the previous attackers must immediately backcheck and defend at the opposite end.
coaching_points: Attackers isolate a tired defender and create a 2-on-1 whenever possible.
Defenders communicate, stay between the puck and net, and finish loose-puck battles.
The previous offensive pair reloads hard through the middle on the transition.
Possession and shots on net should extend offensive-zone time rather than forcing low-percentage plays.

title: KP 2 vs. 2 Neutral Zone Scoring Game
description: Two teams attack opposite nets inside the neutral zone. Each pair must continuously decide whether the off-puck player should defend the opponent or join the puck carrier to create an offensive advantage.
coaching_points: The player without the puck reads offense versus defense before committing.
The puck carrier identifies whether the situation is 1-on-0, 1-on-1 or 2-on-1.
Communicate constantly because the advantage changes quickly.
React immediately when a puck leaves the area and a new attacking opportunity appears.

title: 3 V 3 Keep Away With Team Bumpers
description: A center-ice 3-on-3 possession game with three teammates positioned as moving bumpers on the blue line. Teams score through completed passes while the outside players create support angles and rotate into the game on each change.
coaching_points: Outside bumpers stay alert and move laterally to remain available.
Players without the puck scan, communicate and create a passing lane.
Use give-and-go movement and deception to keep possession away from pressure.
On a turnover, transition immediately from pressure to support.

title: Four Zone 1 on 1
description: One defender handles four consecutive 1-on-1 attacks from four different corner starting points. The coach calls the next attacker, forcing the defender to recover quickly, identify the new threat and close time and space from changing angles.
coaching_points: React to the coach's call and establish inside position immediately.
Close space under control instead of lunging at the puck carrier.
Keep the stick in a useful lane and steer the attacker away from the middle.
Recover quickly between reps and maintain defensive habits under fatigue.

title: The Ottawa Drill
description: A two-part transition drill that begins with a live 3-on-2 below the tops of the circles. On the whistle, a second 3-on-2 attacks the other direction and the original five players recover into the play, turning the sequence into a full-ice 5-on-5.
coaching_points: In the initial 3-on-2, create local 2-on-1s instead of crowding the puck.
Players away from the puck move into open ice and remain available.
Both sides communicate through the whistle and transition immediately.
Recovering players sprint to useful support or coverage positions as the drill expands to 5-on-5.

title: Yellow Attack Timing - V2
description: A two-player wall-retrieval timing drill. One player chips the puck along the boards while the retriever shoulder-checks, pulls it off the wall and finds a supporting teammate arriving either into the slot for a quick release or behind the net for a redirect option.
coaching_points: Shoulder-check before arriving at the puck.
Pull the puck off the wall with the head up and protect it from pressure.
The support player times the route and communicates early.
Use deception on the retrieval and finish with a quick, prepared release.

title: Shot Into Gap Up 1 v 1
description: One player shoots, then immediately gaps up to defend a second player attacking from the blue line. The rep becomes a tight-area 1-on-1 focused on matching speed, protecting the middle and driving the puck toward the net.
coaching_points: Defender closes space under control and matches the attacker's speed.
Keep inside position and angle the puck carrier toward the boards.
Use stick-on-puck and body position instead of reaching.
Offense keeps feet moving, protects the puck and attacks middle ice when it opens.

title: Nobles 2 V 2 + 2 Teammates Transition Game
description: A 2-on-2 battle becomes a 4-on-2 once the team in possession connects with its two support players along the boards. Possession changes immediately flip the support and attacking roles.
coaching_points: Win the first puck and find support quickly.
Support players move the puck back into useful space instead of holding it.
Offense uses switches, give-and-goes and quick-release shots.
Defenders protect the middle, keep sticks in lanes and transition the puck out quickly.

title: Nobles 2 v 2 Transition Game
description: Two teams play 2-on-2 in-zone while the defending team has two teammates waiting along the boards. A defensive possession becomes offense only after the puck is moved to those outlets, creating a continuous transition game.
coaching_points: Defenders keep the puck outside and block the middle with active sticks.
On a turnover, move the puck to the outlets immediately.
New attackers enter with pace and create width.
Offense attacks the net quickly before the defense can fully reset.

title: Larionov 5 V 3 Alternating Warm-Up Drill
description: Five attackers keep possession against three defenders in a confined area. The drill is built as a warm-up that forces constant scanning, support movement, deception and quick puck decisions.
coaching_points: Puck carriers use cutbacks, pace changes and deception to create lanes.
Players without the puck move into open support and present sticks early.
Avoid passing back to the same player when using a pass-count scoring rule.
Defenders stay connected and use active sticks to take away the middle.

title: Add-On Game
description: The game begins 2-on-2. A team can add another attacker by connecting with the first teammate in line and receiving a return pass, so possession and support can progressively create an advantage.
coaching_points: Compete to gain the first clean possession.
After winning the puck, identify the next available support player immediately.
Support away from pressure instead of standing behind defenders.
Defenders keep sticks in lanes and force the attack outside.

title: Net Drive & Angle Drill
description: An attacker loops through the neutral-zone cones and drives back toward the net while a defender takes a shorter route to establish inside position and angle the rush toward the wall.
coaching_points: Defender stays patient, takes back ice and protects the middle.
Steer with the stick, then close body-on-body when the lane is controlled.
Attacker changes speed, protects the puck and drives through the defender's hands.
Do not drift willingly into the corner; keep a scoring-route mindset.

title: Continuous 1 on 1 Puck Retrieval Drill
description: Players alternate corner retrievals while a trailing player provides controlled pressure along the wall. The puck carrier creates separation with body position, gets off the wall and attacks the net before the next retrieval begins.
coaching_points: Retrieve with awareness of the pressure arriving from behind.
Establish body position before exposing the puck.
Use contact and an escape turn to separate from the defender.
Accelerate off the wall and attack the net immediately after creating space.

title: Puck Race to 1 v 1
description: Two players race from the goal line to a loose puck on the dot. The winner becomes the puck protector while the other player defends, creating an immediate possession battle inside the circle.
coaching_points: Win position before reaching for the puck.
Puck winner gets the body between pressure and the puck.
Defender closes through the body rather than reaching from behind.
Progress from no-stick or upside-down-stick defending to a fully live 1-on-1.

title: 1 v 1 Circle (Stick vs. No Stick)
description: A puck carrier works inside a faceoff circle against a defender who initially has no stick. The constraint teaches body positioning, puck protection and contact before progressing to a normal live 1-on-1.
coaching_points: Puck carrier uses body position, deception and speed changes to protect possession.
Defender angles first and closes through the body instead of chasing the puck.
Avoid turning the back into pressure or exposing the puck through the middle.
Progress to an upside-down stick, then both players with normal sticks.

title: 4 Corner Possession Game - Offensive Advantage
description: Two teams play around back-to-back nets with two offensive support players stationed in corner areas. The extra options create give-and-go opportunities, point support, net-front movement and rapid possession changes.
coaching_points: Use the corner support players to escape pressure and attack a new lane.
Move after every pass and arrive at the net with purpose.
Defenders protect inside ice, box out and clear rebounds quickly.
Communicate constantly because the reversed nets create changing threats on both sides.

title: Soft Catch While Attacking Up & Downhill
description: A continuous wall-retrieval skill drill that works the soft catch while attacking in both directions. The player lets a rimmed puck travel across the body, turns with momentum off the wall and immediately attacks the net before continuing to the opposite side for the second repetition.
coaching_points: Start under control and increase speed once the timing is clean.
Stay slightly off the wall so both escape directions remain available.
Let the puck travel across the body before cushioning the catch.
Carry momentum out of the catch and transition directly into the next play or shot.

title: 2 V 1 Quick Strike Game
description: Two simultaneous half-zone areas create quick 2-on-1 attacks. When the defender wins the puck and moves it across to teammates on the opposite side, the next group immediately activates for a new 2-on-1.
coaching_points: Play with quick passes and quick-release shots.
Players away from the puck must become clear outlets and present their sticks.
Defenders scan early so a takeaway turns into an immediate transition pass.
Optional progression allows a joining defender and tracking forward to create a 3-on-2.

title: Sticks In Lanes Game
description: Six offensive players surround a confined scoring area against two defenders. The offense must move the puck through the middle before shooting while the defenders work to eliminate lanes with active sticks and quick stops and starts.
coaching_points: Offense plans the next play before receiving the puck.
Use deception to move defensive sticks and open seams.
Defenders keep sticks on the ice and stay inside passing lanes.
Shrink the space or reduce the offensive numbers to increase difficulty.

title: Rondo Circle Passing to 2 on 1
description: Players maintain possession around the center circle against two defenders. When the defenders steal the puck, they immediately attack together 2-on-1 against the player responsible for the turnover.
coaching_points: Scan the defenders and open space before the puck arrives.
Present a target with the stick on the ice and move after passing.
Use body and eye deception to disguise passes.
On the turnover, both new attackers transition instantly while the new defender recovers through the middle.

title: Cycle to Backcheck Drill
description: Three forwards cycle against two defenders in one end. On the whistle, a new forward line attacks 3-on-2 up ice while the original cycling forwards backcheck and the original defenders join the rush, building toward a full 5-on-5 transition.
coaching_points: Cycle with possession and create a scoring chance before the transition whistle.
New attackers leave with pace and width on the 3-on-2.
Previous attackers reload hard through the middle as backcheckers.
Defensemen recognize the transition and join the rush under control.

title: 1 on 1, 2 on 2, 3 on 3 Battle Drill
description: The drill builds from a 1-on-1 battle to 2-on-2 and then 3-on-3 below the tops of the circles. Offense protects possession and creates scoring chances while defenders work man-on-man coverage, communication and low-zone positioning.
coaching_points: Offense protects the puck first and attacks when a lane opens.
Defenders stay connected to assignments and protect inside ice.
Communicate as each new player joins the battle.
Keep the play below the tops of the circles so the pressure stays tight.

title: Toronto 4 Shot Warm-Up
description: A four-shot full-ice warm-up that gives skaters and goalies four different reads: a downhill dot-lane shot, a weak-side seam shot, a stretch-pass attack, and a final blue-line walk with layered net-front traffic.
coaching_points: Drive the shooting lanes with pace and receive passes in stride.
Time the stretch route so the puck arrives with speed.
Keep net-front players layered and available for screens and rebounds.
On the final shot, walk the blue line to improve the lane before release.

title: Datsyuk Shooting
description: A quick-release shooting station where the shooter receives a pass, attacks the first obstacle with purpose, pulls the puck inside the next obstacle, and releases the shot while staying in stride.
coaching_points: Attack the first obstacle with speed instead of drifting into it.
Use the eyes and upper body to sell a fake before pulling the puck inside.
Keep the feet moving through the release.
Shift body weight through the shot and finish toward the target.

title: NEHDA 2 Puck
description: Players work a two-puck passing and edgework pattern that progresses from facing up ice through both turns to using deception, cutbacks and mohawks while protecting the puck.
coaching_points: Pass with pace and communicate before the puck arrives.
Keep the chest and toe caps facing up ice through the first progression.
Use head and eye deception before cutting back.
Carry the puck away from pressure through the mohawk to protect possession.

title: Decision Time 2 on 1
description: Two attackers use a sharp cut and drop pass to create a 2-on-1 read against a coach or defender. The puck carrier must scan the pressure and decide whether to pass or keep the puck for the shot.
coaching_points: Make sharp lateral cuts so the drop pass is delivered on a useful angle.
Place the drop pass on the receiver's forehand.
Read the defender before deciding pass versus shot.
Both attackers finish at the net for rebounds.

title: Gretzky 2 vs. 2 Game
description: Two teams play 2-on-2 between back-to-back nets while each side has support players stationed behind its attacking net. The support players stay below the goal line and create give-and-go options, changing the attack angle around the net.
coaching_points: Pass and immediately move into new space for a return option.
Support players scan before receiving and use the net as protection.
Defenders keep heads on a swivel and sticks in passing lanes.
Attack quickly when a give-and-go creates separation.

title: Angle Regroup 2 vs. 1
description: A defenseman receives a cross-ice puck under angling pressure while a second forward works to become the outlet. After the breakout, both forwards swing low, regroup and attack back up ice 2-on-1.
coaching_points: The first forward angles on a route that takes away the easy middle pass.
The outlet forward presents a clear stick and moves into available space.
The defenseman scans pressure before deciding pass versus board chip.
Regroup with speed and attack the final 2-on-1 with width.

title: 2 vs. 2 No Sticks Game
description: Two attackers play live against two defenders who have no sticks. The constraint forces defenders to use skating, body position and inside leverage while the offense works give-and-goes and movement into open space.
coaching_points: Defenders protect inside ice with feet and body position instead of reaching.
Offense moves the puck quickly and jumps into open space after passing.
Communicate on both sides of the puck.
Rotate roles so every player experiences offense and defense.

title: Fullback Puck Possession
description: A puck carrier uses two nets as traffic and protection while a pursuing defender tries to close the route. The puck carrier reads the defender, stays tight to the nets and uses controlled cutbacks to maintain possession.
coaching_points: Keep the head up and track pressure with peripheral vision.
Stay tight to the nets so they remove the defender's direct attack lane.
Use tight turns and controlled cutbacks instead of drifting into open ice.
Protect the puck before trying to attack or escape.

title: 3 vs 3 Picket Fences
description: Three attackers forecheck against three defenders in-zone. The offense tries to create a turnover and score, while the defenders must regain possession and skate the puck with control through one of two gates near the top of the circles.
coaching_points: Defenders use support and deception instead of throwing the puck away.
Attackers stay relentless on the forecheck and recover loose pucks quickly.
Scan before possession changes so the next play is already identified.
Support underneath the puck and communicate through the exit.

title: Speed 2 on 2 Gap Up Drill
description: Two forwards work through multiple neutral-zone regroups before attacking two defensemen 2-on-2. The sequence develops support, D-to-D puck movement and the defenders' ability to retake ice and establish a tight gap before the rush.
coaching_points: Forwards stay connected and provide useful support through each regroup.
Defense moves the puck laterally before advancing it.
Defenders retake ice early and match the attackers' speed.
Force the rush outside or into a dump before the blue line.

title: Iron Cross Stick on Puck
description: A defender starts on the faceoff dot and explodes to four puck locations around the circle. Each touch is followed by a quick backward transition and pivot before accelerating to the next puck.
coaching_points: Arrive with a strong stick directly on the puck.
Transition backward immediately after each touch.
Pivot efficiently without crossing up the feet.
Explode out of every turn and finish the final sprint through the goal line.

title: Half Ice (Full Length) Stretch Pass Series
description: A full-length station series run on one half of the rink. Players progress from a direct breakout-style pass to an indirect wall pass, then attack the far end for a shot before retrieving the next puck and continuing the pattern.
coaching_points: Time the receiving route so the player skates into the pass instead of waiting for it.
Present the forehand and communicate before the puck is moved.
On the wall-pass progression, lead the receiver into space so they do not have to look back.
Finish every rush at the net and add a backchecker when the timing is clean.

title: Continuous 1 on 1 Backchecking Drill
description: Players alternate between attacking and backchecking in a continuous full-ice 1-on-1 chase. After the backchecker recovers through the net-front area, that player immediately becomes the next attacker going the opposite direction.
coaching_points: Backcheck all the way through the dangerous middle lane and net-front area.
Attack with pace and force the recovering player to work through the middle.
Transition instantly from defense to offense when the next puck is released.
Keep the repetitions continuous so effort and recovery habits stay game-like.

title: Bing Bang Bong 2 v 1
description: Continuous full-ice passing flow that builds into a 2-on-1. The sequence starts with puck movement through the neutral zone, then progresses from a short-pass variation to a long-pass variation and finally a defenseman activation option that creates a 3-on-1.
coaching_points: Keep the puck moving while skating instead of standing to pass.
Match the timing of the neutral-zone exchanges so the attack stays onside.
Defensemen should gap quickly when they become the defender.
In the activation progression, the joining defenseman must arrive with speed and good spacing.

title: Pens 3 Shot
description: Three-shot offensive-zone sequence. A forward attacks for the first shot, retrieves a second puck for another quick chance, then moves a third puck low-to-high to a defenseman for a point shot and rebound opportunity before the next repetition begins.
coaching_points: Keep the forward moving between shots instead of resetting.
Defensemen should get the puck off the stick quickly and shoot for a useful rebound.
Attack rebounds with the stick available and maintain net-front timing.
Communicate on the low-to-high exchange.

title: Wooley Up
description: Continuous timing drill built around defenseman puck movement, a neutral-zone escape and a stretch pass. The rush finishes with a shot, then players follow the play for rebounds before a low-to-high puck activates the defenseman for a second shot.
coaching_points: Defensemen should move their feet before passing.
Forwards need to time their routes so the stretch option stays onside.
Use loud communication and present the stick as a target.
After the first shot, transition immediately into the low-to-high second-shot sequence.

title: Power Play Flank Shooting
description: Power-play shooting progression using a bumper, a high player and a flank attacker. The puck moves through the bumper to the top, the top player walks the line and then feeds the flank attacker, who uses the bumper as a screen or token defender before cutting into a shot.
coaching_points: Catch and release the puck quickly on each exchange.
The high player should move laterally with pace before making the seam pass.
The flank attacker climbs into space before receiving the puck.
Use the bumper to create traffic and force a game-like shooting lane.

title: Fimmer Rimmer
description: Two-shot wall-retrieval drill. The player first picks up a rim, moves off the wall into better ice and attacks the net. After the first shot, the player climbs into the high slot and receives a seam pass for a second catch-and-release shot.
coaching_points: Meet the rim with speed and control.
Get off the wall immediately after the retrieval instead of staying outside.
On the second shot, arrive in the high slot ready to shoot without extra stickhandles.
Use the progression to reinforce power-play flank habits and quick releases.

title: 2 on 2 Down Low Rim
description: Two defenders start in front while offensive players are positioned on the half walls. One attacker rims the puck to a teammate, who controls it and attacks with support. The defenders pivot around their cones, close the play and defend the rush; after the rep, the offensive players transition into the next defensive pair.
coaching_points: Receive the rim under control and get the puck off the wall quickly.
Attackers should support underneath and create a quick 2-on-2 attack.
Defenders establish inside position before engaging the puck.
Transition immediately between offense and defense to keep the drill continuous.

title: Picking Up Rims with Front Pressure
description: A player loops from the blue line to collect a rim while scanning pressure arriving from the front. The puck carrier reads the forechecker, chooses the middle or wall escape and attacks the net. In the progression, the player who completed the first retrieval becomes the defender on the next rim.
coaching_points: Shoulder-check before arriving at the puck.
Use body position to protect the puck from front pressure.
Keep the hands away from the body so the puck can move across the body when needed.
Read the pressure early and accelerate into the available escape lane.

title: Picking Up Rims with Back Pressure
category: Wall Retrieval / Back Pressure / Puck Protection
description: A coach or player rims the puck from the corner while two players start near the blue line. The first player retrieves the rim, gets off the wall and attacks the net while the second player applies back pressure. Pressure can begin controlled and increase as players improve.
coaching_points: Look over the shoulder early to identify pressure.
Use the body to seal the puck from the backchecker.
Create separation with speed immediately after the retrieval.
Keep the hands free and the puck away from the pressure side.

title: 3 v 2 with Angling Backchecker Continuous
description: A 3-on-2 rush starts up ice. As the rush crosses center, the next two defenders prepare at the far blue line. On the second whistle, the highest forward from the original attack becomes an angling backchecker while the next group attacks, creating a continuous transition sequence.
coaching_points: The backchecker should read the puck carrier, keep the stick in the passing lane and angle the play outside.
Attackers should move the puck away from pressure and maintain width.
Enter with possession when space is available; chip into space only when the pressure dictates it.
Defenders gap early so they are set before the rush reaches the zone.

title: 1-3-1 Mad Attacker
category: Power Play / Penalty Kill / Half Ice
description: A staged pressure game for a 1-3-1 power play. The power-play unit starts in structure and retrieves a dump-in while one designated penalty killer attacks the puck everywhere. Coaches progressively add more attackers as the unit learns to retrieve, support and make simple plays under pressure.
coaching_points: Outnumber pressure on loose pucks before settling into formation.
Use short support options instead of forcing passes through pressure.
Penalty killers attack with an active stick and constant pressure.
Add pressure progressively so the power-play unit must solve increasingly difficult reads.

title: Swedish 2 on 0 Half Ice
description: Two-player half-ice passing warm-up. The first player begins backward with the puck, exchanges passes with a partner and then escapes into the zone while the second player drives the net. The puck carrier can shoot, create a tip or rebound, or pass across.
coaching_points: Pass in stride and keep both players moving.
Time the net drive so the second attacker arrives as a scoring option.
The puck carrier should read the goalie and choose shot, tip, rebound or pass.
Keep the drill flowing as a warm-up rather than slowing to set up each rep.

title: Transition Pull Outside - Defense Skills
description: Defense skill drill for retrieving a loose puck while moving back toward the defensive end. The player explodes to the puck, pivots up ice quickly, pulls the puck laterally to the outside and finishes with a hard forehand pass to the next player.
coaching_points: Retrieve with the feet moving through the puck.
Get shoulders and eyes up ice immediately after possession.
Use one strong lateral pull rather than several extra stickhandles.
Finish with a firm forehand pass.

title: Hit The Tire With 1 Goalie Game
description: Three-on-three small-area game played around a tire or cone in the middle of the zone. One goalie protects the target while both teams can attack it after gaining possession, creating constant changes of direction and quick offensive-to-defensive transitions.
coaching_points: Offense should support the puck and shoot quickly after passes while the goalie is moving.
Defenders keep sticks in lanes and angle attackers away from the middle.
The goalie reads play from every direction and works edges around the target.
Keep shifts short and highly competitive.

title: DV3 Warm Up
description: Three-version continuous full-ice warm-up built around defense-to-defense puck movement and timed forward routes. The progressions move from D-to-D to wall, to a middle option, and finally to a hinge before the puck is advanced to a forward for a shot.
coaching_points: Defensemen move the puck crisply and support the next option.
Forwards time their routes so they arrive as the passing lane opens.
Keep sticks on the ice and communicate throughout the sequence.
Maintain pace through all three versions.

title: Admirals 2 Shot
description: Two-part warm-up. In the first sequence a forward and defenseman exchange passes down ice before the defenseman escapes and hits the forward through the middle for the attack. The second sequence moves a puck to the point for a walk-and-shoot opportunity with traffic at the net.
coaching_points: Pass and receive while moving.
Defensemen use a purposeful escape before advancing the puck.
Forwards time the middle route and create net-front traffic after the rush.
Point shots should arrive through traffic with players ready for tips and rebounds.

title: SD Thomas 1 v 1
description: One-on-one battle in a compact corner area with the net moved away from the boards. The coach chips a puck into play and the two players compete for possession; whoever owns the puck attacks while the other player defends and tries to create a turnover.
coaching_points: The puck carrier uses the body to shield the puck and attack space.
The defender stays stick-on-puck and uses body position to create a turnover.
Transition immediately from defense to offense when possession changes.
Keep the battle active instead of allowing the puck carrier to stall along the wall.

title: Out Of The Corner
description: Down-low puck-protection drill that starts with the offensive player collecting a puck near the corner and attacking off the wall against pressure. The defender begins with controlled resistance and can progress to a live one-on-one battle.
coaching_points: The attacker initiates contact, protects the puck and works off the wall.
Cut the hands across the body as the route turns toward the net.
Defenders keep the stick down and angle the attacker away from scoring ice.
Increase pressure gradually as players master the puck-protection technique.

title: Off-Side Game
description: Cross-ice three-on-three game with a center-ice offsides line. Before a team can attack, it must regroup in its own half and then enter the attacking half onside. An offsides play immediately creates a turnover.
coaching_points: Support underneath the puck during the regroup.
Attackers time their routes through the center line instead of racing ahead of the puck.
Defenders keep sticks in lanes and angle play outside.
Use the rule to reinforce possession and controlled entries.

title: Black vs White Stick Tape Keep Away
description: Keep-away game where teams are identified by stick-tape color rather than jersey color. A point is earned for completing a tape-to-tape pass to a teammate with the same tape color, forcing players to scan and identify teammates before moving the puck.
coaching_points: Scan constantly to identify teammates by stick tape.
Get open quickly when your team has possession.
Protect the puck with the body until a passing lane opens.
Move the puck tape-to-tape instead of throwing it into space blindly.

title: 3 vs. 3 Handball Game
description: Three-on-three handball game played without sticks or pucks. Players use a ball and must move it quickly, creating constant give-and-go situations, support reads and off-puck movement.
coaching_points: Move the ball quickly instead of holding it.
Support the ball carrier by getting open immediately.
Use give-and-go movement after every pass.
Keep shifts short and competitive.

title: Battery Hockey Figure 8 Shooting Drill
description: Six-shot shooting progression with passers on both sides. The shooter begins with stationary catch-and-release shots, progresses to pivots around a cone for quick shots, then finishes with controlled turns and additional catch-and-release attempts.
coaching_points: Keep the stick on the ice to give the passer a clear target.
Receive and release quickly with the hands away from the body.
Stay facing the passer through pivots and controlled turns.
Rotate shooters and passers so the drill stays continuous.

title: Skilled Passing to 1 on 1 Battle Drill
description: Two players begin with a skilled passing sequence through the neutral zone, race to finish a backdoor chance, then immediately compete in a live 1-on-1 battle after the coach sends a new puck to the corner.
coaching_points: Execute the drop pass and obstacle pass with pace and control.
Attack the backdoor with timing and a stick available for the finish.
Transition immediately from the scoring chance into the 1-on-1 battle.
Compete through the puck and finish the battle at the net.

title: Neutral Zone 3 vs. 3 Game
category: 3 vs 3 / Neutral Zone / Small Area Game
description: A neutral-zone 3-on-3 game with each team supported by an outlet on its blue line. New pucks enter quickly after goals, saves or pucks leaving the area, creating constant turnovers, transition reads and support decisions.
coaching_points: Keep the head up and scan before receiving or pressuring the puck.
Keep sticks on the ice for passing targets and defensive lanes.
Communicate through every turnover and new-puck situation.
Move into open space immediately when supporting away from the puck.

title: Continuous In Zone 2 vs. 2 Game
description: A continuous in-zone 2-on-2 where the attacking pair becomes the next defending pair. The defenders effectively double shift, forcing strong positioning, communication and puck decisions while tired.
coaching_points: Defenders stay connected, keep sticks down and protect the middle under fatigue.
Hold and protect the puck until a useful play is available.
Communicate verbally and non-verbally with the partner.
Transition immediately when the rep changes from offense to defense.

title: Finnish 5 Puck - Rotating Zones
category: Warm Up / Puck Skills / Third Ice
description: Five-player groups rotate through three zones in short sets. The outside zones cycle through edgework, puckhandling, passing and keep-away activities while the middle zone provides stationary passing and recovery.
coaching_points: Stay active and creative in the working zones while keeping the head up.
Use strong inside edges and clean transitions before adding speed.
Players without the puck stay ready, communicate and create passing options.
Keep each set short so the rotations maintain tempo.

title: High Tempo 2 vs. 2 to Net
description: A fast 2-on-2 game where the forwards can attack either net while the defenders protect both. If the defense wins the puck, it scores by completing four consecutive passes, creating immediate transition and communication demands.
coaching_points: Attack with pace as soon as the coach starts the puck.
Communicate so the defenders sort the backward-skating and backchecking roles.
Keep the head up and use deception to change the point of attack.
Protect possession and make quick decisions as the available space shrinks.

title: 4 vs. 2 No Stickhandle Game
description: A half-ice 4-on-2 possession game split into two sides. The four offensive players must move the puck without stickhandling while two defenders pressure and take away lanes. On a turnover, possession is transferred to the teammates on the opposite side.
coaching_points: Move the puck immediately instead of holding or stickhandling it.
Players without the puck constantly create new passing lanes.
Defenders keep sticks on the ice and pressure with good angles.
React quickly to turnovers and support the new puck carrier.

title: Corner Puck Protection
description: A corner retrieval and puck-protection drill. The player chips the puck into the corner, shoulder-checks before retrieval, pulls the puck off the wall and uses tight turns to protect it before driving out toward the net.
coaching_points: Scan before arriving at the puck.
Keep the puck protected along the wall before escaping pressure.
Use a strong stance and tight control turns.
Progress from technical reps to shadow pressure and live 1-on-1 pressure.

title: 6 Cone Skills Series
description: A six-cone skill-development series that progresses through hard and soft direction changes, tight turns, figure-eight patterns, pivots and deceptive shuffle movements.
coaching_points: Maintain an athletic stance through every change of direction.
Keep the head and shoulders square while the feet work underneath.
Execute every pattern to both sides.
Build clean edge control before adding maximum speed.

title: Around the World
description: A full-ice puck-control competition. Players begin from both ends with pucks, travel around the nets toward the far end while neutral-zone defenders try to knock pucks away, creating a head-up awareness challenge.
coaching_points: Keep the head up while carrying the puck through traffic.
Protect the puck with body position when defenders close.
Change speed and direction instead of skating predictable lines.
Defenders angle and attack the puck without losing awareness of traffic.

title: Three Gates 1 vs 1 vs 1
description: Three players compete for one puck and score by carrying the puck through one of the designated tire gates. A player cannot score through the same gate twice in a row, forcing puck protection, awareness and changes of direction.
coaching_points: Protect the puck with the body and keep the head up.
Use deception and changes of direction to find an open gate.
Defenders angle the puck carrier toward dead areas.
Compete through possession changes instead of stopping after losing the puck.

title: 1 vs 1 vs 1 - Sixth Ice Station
category: 1 vs 1 / Sixth Ice / Small Area Game
description: Three players each defend one mini net while trying to score on either of the other two. New pucks are added after goals and the game runs in short competitive shifts.
coaching_points: Keep the head up because threats can come from two opponents.
Protect your own net while recognizing the best attacking option.
Transition immediately between offense and defense.
Use short shifts to maintain pace and compete level.

title: Corner Tires 1 vs 1 Multiple Games 1/6 Ice Station
description: Multiple 1-on-1 games run simultaneously in a sixth-ice space. Each player attacks the opponent's tire target while defending their own, creating repeated puck-protection and battle situations.
coaching_points: Compete hard for inside body position.
Protect the puck before attacking the tire.
Keep the head up because multiple games may be active nearby.
Use 60- to 90-second rounds to maintain intensity.

title: D 3 Cone Agility Drill
description: A three-cone defense skill progression that layers footwork, puck control and passing. Players work pivots, transitions and edge control around the cones before adding puck and passing components.
coaching_points: Make pivots smooth and controlled.
Use the outside edge to explode into backward skating.
Stay low through every transition.
Use one hand when appropriate going backward and two hands when attacking forward.

title: Back to Back 3 vs 3
description: A 3-on-3 small-area game with two nets positioned back to back. One player from each team serves as a point option while the other players battle around the nets. Goals created from point shots, screens or tips can be weighted for extra value.
coaching_points: Defenders box out and control sticks around the net.
Offensive players fight for sightlines and keep sticks available.
Point players keep shots low and on net.
Use the point player to create screens, tips and second-chance opportunities.

title: 3 on 2 Corner Passer Cross Ice Game
category: 3 vs 2 / Cross Ice Small Area Game
description: A cross-ice 3-on-3 variation where one player from each team becomes a corner passer below the goal line, leaving a live 2-on-2 in the middle. Teams must use the corner passer and receive the puck back before they can score.
coaching_points: Defenders stay on the defensive side of the puck.
Transition quickly after turnovers.
Players without the puck move immediately to create options.
Corner passers pre-scan and move the puck quickly.

title: Gates, Tires, Triangles Station
description: A random obstacle-course station using gates, tires and stick triangles. Players perform full turns around tires, figure-eights through gates and puck-control moves through or under obstacles.
coaching_points: Keep the head up while navigating the obstacles.
Use tight turns and controlled edges around tires.
Keep the puck close enough to recover after every move.
Encourage creativity while maintaining control.

title: 1 vs 1 Bump and Drive to net
description: The attacker works through a passing and transition sequence before receiving the final puck and attacking a defender to the net. The rep emphasizes puck protection, skating through contact and defensive angling.
coaching_points: Attackers keep their feet moving through pressure.
Keep the body between the defender and puck.
Win the outside shoulder before cutting inside when space opens.
Defenders angle toward the outside and maintain stick position.

title: 1 vs 1 vs 1 with Mini Nets
description: Three mini nets are arranged in a triangle and one player protects each net. Every player can score on either opponent net while defending their own, creating constant offense-to-defense decisions.
coaching_points: Scan before attacking because two scoring options are available.
Protect your own net without becoming stationary.
Use deception and quick changes of direction.
Transition instantly after goals, steals and loose pucks.

title: Paint Scoring
description: A rapid scoring station built around three pucks and multiple finishes. The player works around an obstacle and completes a sequence of backhand, catch-and-release and forehand scoring actions.
coaching_points: Prepare the hands before each puck arrives.
Release shots quickly instead of overhandling.
Stay balanced while changing the shooting angle.
Finish each puck before moving immediately to the next.

title: Tricky Icky - Puck in Triangle
description: A tight-turn puck-protection progression using a triangle setup. Players first learn the skating pattern, then add a puck and work on protecting it through tight changes of direction.
coaching_points: Lead the turn with the inside leg.
Trust the outside edge of the inside skate.
Keep the hands close enough to the blade for control in tight space.
Use body position to take away the defender's path to the puck.

title: Finders Keepers - Puck Protection Drill
description: Players compete for fewer pucks than there are skaters and try to maintain possession until the whistle. The activity forces awareness, puck protection, stealing and movement toward open ice.
coaching_points: Play with the head up and identify open ice.
Use the body to protect possession from pressure.
Look for opportunities to steal without losing awareness.
Keep moving instead of protecting the puck in one spot.

title: Chase the Rabbit Series - With Pucks
description: Paired players complete four chase progressions that increase in difficulty. The rabbit changes speed and direction while the chaser mirrors the route; later progressions add pucks and backward skating for both players.
coaching_points: Keep the head up and maintain awareness of other pairs.
Use quick stops, starts and changes of direction.
Mirror the rabbit closely while maintaining puck control.
Use the advanced backward-with-puck progression only when players are ready.

title: Forwards / Backwards Chase - Puck Control Activity
description: Players work in pairs inside a defined space. One player skates backward and changes direction while the puck carrier skates forward and tries to remain in front while controlling the puck, forcing both players to maintain awareness.
coaching_points: Both players keep their heads up because multiple pairs are active.
The backward skater changes speed and direction to create separation.
The puck carrier stays controlled while matching the partner's movement.
Switch roles after short 45- to 60-second rounds.

title: 5 Pass 2 on 1
description: A high-tempo full-ice passing sequence that uses five passes before developing into a live 2-on-1. Forwards exchange a drop pass and cross-ice passes through the neutral zone while the defense activates from the opposite end.
coaching_points: Call for every pass and present a clear target.
Drop the puck to the receiving player's forehand.
Forwards stay below the puck and time their routes so they can skate into passes.
On the 2-on-1, the defender protects the middle and forces the puck carrier outside.

title: Finders Keepers - Station
category: Puck Protection / Small Area Game / Station
description: A competitive possession station where players race for fewer pucks than there are skaters. After each short round, players without a puck are eliminated or complete an exercise until one puck and two players remain for the championship round.
coaching_points: Attack open ice after gaining possession.
Use body position to protect the puck from pressure.
Keep the head up to locate loose pucks and pressure.
Use short rounds to keep the game fast and competitive.

title: Forehand Shooting Fundamentals #3
description: A forehand shooting progression where the player takes two strides, transitions backward to receive a pass, controls the puck backward around a pad and finishes with a forehand shot after clearing the obstacle.
coaching_points: Keep the puck in shooting position while skating backward.
Pull the puck toward the back of the stance before release.
Use a strong weight transfer through the shot.
Finish with weight on the foot closest to the net.

title: Forehand Shooting Fundamentals #2
description: A basic forehand shooting station where players collect a puck near the top of the circle, skate around a pad while keeping the puck on the forehand, and shoot immediately after clearing the obstacle.
coaching_points: Keep the puck in shooting position around the pad.
Keep the puck toward the back of the stance.
Transfer weight toward the net through the shot.
Use the inside edges to stay balanced through the turn.

title: Forehand Shooting Fundamentals #1
description: A youth forehand shooting station that places a pad in front of the net so the player must pull the puck slightly into the body, around the pad and directly into the shooting motion.
coaching_points: Pull the puck slightly into the body.
Transfer weight through the shot.
Keep the head over the puck and avoid leaning backward.
Shoot low and hard while driving the motion toward the net.

title: 5 Cone 2 Shot Station Drill
description: A five-cone station where the player carries a puck through tight turns, shoots shortly after the final cone, stops at the net for a rebound, then presents a target for a coach pass and a second catch-and-release shot.
coaching_points: Use tight control turns and protect the puck around the cones.
Keep a closed blade and control the puck through the pattern.
Shoot shortly after clearing the final cone and stop at the net.
Present a strong target and use a firm bottom hand on the catch-and-release.

title: Quarter Ice Angle 1 vs 1
description: A quarter-ice 1-on-1 station. The offensive player slaloms through cones and attacks the net while the defender rounds a separate cone and times the route to angle the puck carrier toward the boards.
coaching_points: The defender keeps the stick on the ice.
Use stick position and body angle to discourage the cutback to the middle.
Match the puck carrier's speed before closing.
Finish the angle through the hands into the wall.

title: Three Sided Box Retrieval Station
description: A two-shot retrieval station using three barriers to form a box. The player retrieves a coach chip, transitions backward out of the box, transitions forward for a shot, circles a tire backward, then repeats the retrieval and finishes with a second shot.
coaching_points: Retrieve the puck with control and transition backward immediately.
Keep the feet active through backward-to-forward transitions.
Exit the box before accelerating into the shot.
Recover quickly after the first shot and be ready for the second retrieval.

title: Stick Check Take Away Drill (Studio Rink)
description: Players skate around the net, approach a stationary coach from behind on a proper angle, lift or tap through the coach's stick to steal the puck, then counter quickly for a shot.
coaching_points: Approach from a useful angle with the stick on the ice.
Use a strong bottom hand when getting under the opponent's stick.
Use a quick controlled tap to separate stick from puck.
Protect the recovered puck with the body before attacking the net.

title: Horseshoe Re-Group One Goalie - #1 (D to D to Center)
description: A full-ice one-goalie flow drill combining a backcheck, shot, neutral-zone regroup and a second attack. The forward receives from the coach, moves the puck D-to-D, swings through the neutral zone for the return pass and attacks the net.
coaching_points: Backcheck with urgency on the opening race.
Defense moves the puck quickly D-to-D while maintaining width.
The regrouping forward times the swing to arrive with speed.
Finish the attack at the net and hunt the rebound.

title: Continuous Pass & Shoot Station
description: A continuous passing-and-shooting station. A player carries down for a shot, stops at the net, retrieves a loose puck and passes to the next player moving the other direction. The pattern alternates continuously.
coaching_points: Pass and receive while moving.
Stop at the net after every shot and be ready for rebounds.
Explode with the first three strides to retrieve the next puck.
Present a clear target and keep the drill flowing without pauses.

title: D to D to F3
description: The forward starts the puck from the half wall to the strong-side defense. The defense moves it quickly D-to-D across the blue line, then finds F3 arriving in the high slot for the third pass and shot.
coaching_points: Move the puck D-to-D quickly before the defense can reset.
The receiving defenseman works outside the dots to widen the coverage.
F3 times the route into the high slot instead of arriving early.
Follow the shot and create a screen for the next repetition.

title: Gretzky 3 on 3
description: A cross-ice 3-on-3 game with one designated Gretzky positioned behind each opponent's net. After a change of possession, the team must use its Gretzky before it can attack the net.
coaching_points: Use the Gretzky to create give-and-go and net-front options.
Move immediately after passing instead of watching the puck.
Support below the goal line when pressure closes on the Gretzky.
Keep shifts short and transition hard on possession changes.

title: Five Puck Scoring Race - Half Ice
description: Two teams race to score five pucks in a half-ice setup. A player attacks one puck at a time; a goal allows the next teammate to go after the skater returns to the blue line, while a miss must be retrieved and reset first.
coaching_points: Attack the puck and net at game speed.
Finish the scoring chance before racing back to release the next player.
On a miss, recover and reset the puck quickly.
Keep the race competitive while maintaining safe spacing.

title: Four Shot Half Ice Shooting Drill
description: A half-ice four-shot sequence combining wall puck protection, a slot shot, a pass-and-return shot, and two defense-oriented point-shot patterns with backward transitions and D-to-D puck movement.
coaching_points: Keep the feet moving through the wall turns and shooting actions.
Use quick catch-and-release mechanics in the slot.
Defense transitions backward with the head up and presents a target.
Move D-to-D pucks quickly and get shots through traffic.

title: Continuous 2 on 1 with Backchecker
description: A continuous full-ice 2-on-1 where the coach directs the transition, the defense retakes ice, and the F2 from the previous rush becomes the backchecker against the next attack. The defense can optionally join to create a 3-on-2.
