coaching_points: Forwards react immediately to the coach's transition signal.
Strong-side support opens up while weak-side support stays available.
Defense retakes as much ice as possible before setting the gap.
The backchecker communicates with the defender and identifies the weak-side threat.

title: Neutral Zone Puck Skills #1
description: A three-part neutral-zone skill station combining large puck-control movements, wall puck protection against pressure and a quick-hands stickhandling pattern.
coaching_points: Use both hands and cradle the puck with controlled wrist action.
Stay balanced on the inside edges through large puck movements.
Use the body and wall to protect the puck from pressure.
Finish with quick hands while keeping a stable skating base.

title: Full Ice Skills Series - 1 Goalie
category: Full Ice / One Goalie / Skill Development
description: A full-ice skill series designed for practices with one goalie. Players work through a tire or cone skill pattern down one side, pass to a coach in the opposite corner, support through the slot for a return pass, then push the puck with one hand while working a full forward stride before finishing with a shot.
coaching_points: Support the puck through the slot and present a clear target for the return pass.
Stay low with full extension and full recovery during the forward stride.
Push the puck instead of over-stickhandling when building speed.
Keep the puck close to the blade and slightly outside the body when working the backhand side.

title: The Greatest Drill in the World
description: A cross-ice 3-on-3 game with two coaches or designated players stationed as outlets along the outside of the playing area. The team in possession can use either outlet, effectively creating a temporary 5-on-3 advantage and encouraging quick puck movement and give-and-go support.
coaching_points: Move the puck quickly and use the outside outlets before pressure collapses.
Move immediately after passing to create the next support option.
Communicate constantly and recognize local 2-on-1 opportunities.
Protect the puck under pressure and transition quickly after turnovers.

title: Neutral Zone Passing Station #1
description: A neutral-zone passing station that can be run as three lanes or two longer lanes. Two players pass between each cone set, switch sides at the end with a forehand drop pass, then continue passing through the cones on the return route.
coaching_points: Deliver firm forehand and backhand passes with a clear target.
Receive with soft hands and prepare the puck immediately for the next pass.
Time the side switch so the drop pass lands on the partner's forehand.
Alternate sides on each repetition so players work both forehand and backhand receptions.

title: Five Puck Scoring Race
description: A full-ice relay scoring race. Two teams start from the benches with five pucks placed across each blue line. One player at a time attacks a puck on a breakaway; a goal allows the next teammate to go after the skater returns to the blue line, while a miss must be retrieved and reset before the next player can leave.
coaching_points: Attack the puck and net at game speed.
Finish the scoring chance before racing back to release the next player.
On a miss, retrieve and reset the puck quickly.
Keep the race competitive while maintaining safe spacing between players.

title: Savy's Continuous Breakout Drill with Forecheckers
description: A continuous breakout drill with three designated forecheckers available. The coach controls the pressure by releasing one, two or all three forecheckers against the next breakout group, creating progressively harder breakout reads under live pressure.
coaching_points: Breakout players communicate early and support underneath the puck.
Defense retrieves with the head up and identifies the first available outlet.
Forecheckers pressure with purpose and take away time, space and passing lanes.
Vary the number of released forecheckers so the breakout group must read changing pressure.

title: 2-1 Low/2-1 Long
description: A two-part 2-on-1 progression. The first rep starts with a coach rim and a low 2-on-1, followed by a point shot with net-front traffic. The forwards then transition the other direction for a full-ice 2-on-1 against the opposite defenseman.
coaching_points: Handle the rim cleanly and create width before attacking the low 2-on-1.
Drive the net after the first attack and establish useful screen or rebound position.
Defense gets the second puck to the net quickly through traffic.
On the long 2-on-1, attack with speed and force the defender to make a decision.

title: 2 Shot Rim/Players adding pressure
description: A two-shot rim and pressure drill. Players retrieve coach rims and attack a stationary pressure player for the first shot, then curl low, receive a cross-ice pass, protect the puck around pressure near the red line and attack a second pressure player for another shot.
coaching_points: Shoulder-check before arriving at the rim and get the puck off the wall under control.
Attack the pressure player's feet and use body position to protect the puck.
Accelerate after escaping pressure instead of gliding into the shot.
Rotate through the pressure role so players learn both sides of the contact.

title: Wall to Saucer Pass 6 Shooter (2-1)
description: A multi-shot saucer-passing progression. The wall player receives from the coach and makes saucer passes over stick obstacles to teammates for shots, then works around the obstacles for another shot. The progression finishes with two forwards attacking a defender 2-on-1.
coaching_points: Keep saucer passes flat and land them beyond the obstacle.
Receivers present a target and prepare for a quick release.
Move the feet immediately after each pass to stay involved in the sequence.
Finish the progression by attacking the 2-on-1 with width and pace.

title: Puck Protect to 2-1
description: A puck-protection battle transitions into a 2-on-1. One player protects the puck between the blue line and wall while a partner applies pressure. On the whistle, the puck protector attacks for a quick shot, then becomes the defender against the next two-player rush.
coaching_points: Use hips and body position to keep the defender away from the puck.
Explode out of the protection area when the whistle sounds.
The new defender retakes ice quickly and establishes inside position.
The two attackers use width and a clear passing lane on the 2-on-1.

title: BO Stretch to 2-1
description: A breakout-to-rush progression. Two forwards work around the faceoff dot while the defense gaps up. After the puck is sent deep, the defender retrieves and hits a forward stretching to the far blue line. The second forward supports through the middle and the pair attacks the opposite defender 2-on-1.
coaching_points: The retrieving defender gets the head up early and delivers the stretch pass on time.
The supporting forward stays underneath the puck and arrives with speed.
Use the wall, middle or bump option based on the defender's position.
Attack the 2-on-1 with pace and keep the passing lane available.

title: Double RG to 2-1
description: Two forwards leave the red line with a puck and complete two consecutive one-touch regroups with defensemen on opposite sides of the neutral zone. After the second regroup they re-attack the original defender in a live 2-on-1.
coaching_points: Forwards stay available underneath the puck and time their swings with speed.
Defense presents a clean target and moves the puck one-touch when possible.
Communicate through both regroups so spacing stays connected.
After the second regroup, attack the 2-on-1 immediately before the defender can reset.

title: 2F, 1D Shooting Warm-Up
description: A continuous shooting warm-up using two forwards and one defenseman. The defender backpedals, receives from the opposite defense line and feeds forwards down the wall for shots, then follows the play to receive a final puck for a net-front shooting sequence.
coaching_points: Defense keeps the feet moving while receiving and moving the puck.
Forwards time wall routes to receive passes with speed.
Use the coach as passive pressure and shoot around the screen.
Finish with both forwards creating useful net-front presence.

title: 2-1 Entry/2-1 Down Low
description: Two attackers exchange one-touch passes with a coach before entering against a defender for a 2-on-1. After the initial rush, the coach places a second puck into a corner and the same players continue in a live down-low 2-on-1.
coaching_points: The puck carrier scans before entry and reads shot versus pass.
The off-puck forward creates width and keeps a passing lane available.
The defender protects the middle and lets the goalie handle the outside shot.
On the second puck, transition immediately into down-low support and coverage.

title: 2-1 Wall Battle to 2-2
description: A wall retrieval and battle develops into a quick 2-on-1, then transitions on a second whistle into a live 2-on-2. Players tag designated lines before entering each phase, forcing fast changes between support, pressure and rush defense.
coaching_points: Retrieve the rim with the head up and protect it along the wall.
The supporting forward gets inside and available quickly.
After the second whistle, transition immediately instead of watching the first play finish.
Defenders communicate and sort the 2-on-2 before the attackers gain speed.

title: Puck Protection to 2-1
description: Players begin with a puck-protection battle along the neutral-zone wall. On the second whistle a third player joins as support, the offensive pair regroups back toward the line and re-attacks the former pressure player in a 2-on-1.
coaching_points: Keep hips and body between pressure and the puck.
Support arrives underneath the puck with a clear passing target.
The pressure player transitions quickly into gap control when the play turns.
Attack the resulting 2-on-1 with width and communication.

title: J-Drill Progression #3 (2-1)
description: Players line up at the hash marks. The first player curls inside the opposite blue line without a puck, receives a pass from the next player, and the passer joins to create a 2-on-1 against a third player who has skated up ice to establish gap.
coaching_points: The curling forward scans, communicates and presents a target.
The passer delivers a flat pass then accelerates into support.
The defender gets up ice before setting the gap instead of backing in early.
Attackers communicate shot and pass options while the defender protects the middle.

title: Rim to scissor, 2 D shots to 3-2
description: A layered progression beginning with a forward rim retrieval and scissor exchange, followed by two defense point shots from opposite sides. A final coach pass sends the three forwards up ice against two defensemen in a full-ice 3-on-2.
coaching_points: The first forward retrieves under control and uses the scissor to create separation.
The high forward stays available in soft ice while the low forward attacks the net.
Defense gets both point shots through quickly after the rim.
On the final 3-on-2, fill three lanes and transition with speed.

title: 2-1 Forwards Swinging, RG D 2 shots
description: A defenseman retrieves a spotted puck while two forwards swing off the blue lines to gain speed. The forwards break out, regroup with a far defenseman and re-attack the original defender 2-on-1. The regroup defenseman follows and finishes with two point shots through the forwards.
coaching_points: Forwards time their swings so they receive the breakout pass with speed.
Keep the regroup connected and attack immediately after the return pass.
The original defender establishes gap early for the 2-on-1.
After the rush, forwards create screens and tip options for the two point shots.

title: 3 -n 2v1's (2 low, 1 high)
description: Three separate 2-on-1 situations are staged in one zone: two low in the corners and one high near the blue line. The coach rims or spots a new puck on each whistle and players compete for several seconds before immediately moving to the next 2-on-1.
coaching_points: Attackers create a quick passing lane rather than overhandling.
Defenders protect the middle and keep sticks in useful lanes.
React to each whistle immediately and locate the new puck.
Use short competitive windows so every rep stays intense.

title: Lateral Passing Progress to 2-1
description: A lateral passing and shooting progression that finishes in a 2-on-1. Two players exchange passes while moving across the ice, create quick one-touch shooting chances at the far end, then the first shooter transitions to defense as the other two players attack back 2-on-1.
coaching_points: Pass laterally while moving and keep the puck out in front of the receiver.
Time the curl so the middle player arrives available for the next pass.
Use one-touch passes when the lane is clean and shoot without overhandling.
The first shooter transitions quickly to establish gap for the returning 2-on-1.

title: 2 on 1 to 4 on 2
description: A continuous rush progression from Wes Wolfe. Two forwards begin with a cross-and-drop 2-on-1. After that rush, a third forward activates and the original defender joins the attack to create a four-player rush against two new defenders. The next whistle starts a new 2-on-1 with a backchecker.
coaching_points: On the 4-on-2, play positionless and fill open lanes instead of skating fixed routes.
Players without the puck stay available with sticks on the ice.
Defenders protect passing lanes, angle outside and communicate through the rush.
Transition immediately on each whistle so the drill remains continuous.

title: 4X 2v1's from centre
description: Four lines work simultaneously from center ice. One variation sends a puck carrier around a cone against a defender for a 1-on-1; the paired variation sends two attackers around the cone against a defender for a 2-on-1.
coaching_points: Attackers accelerate around the cone and attack before the defender settles.
The second attacker creates width and stays available for a pass.
Defenders get up ice, transition and establish a tight gap.
Run all four lines with awareness so traffic remains safe and organized.

title: 3 Man Pass G-F Exchange to 2-1
description: Two forwards and a defenseman complete a three-player passing sequence to the far blue line, then the forwards rim the puck to the goalie. The goalie handles the rim and moves it back to the forwards for a breakout before they attack the gapped-up defenseman 2-on-1.
coaching_points: Keep the three-player passing sequence crisp while everyone moves with pace.
The goalie gets out early, controls the rim and makes a useful breakout play.
Forwards support the goalie and exit with speed.
The defender establishes gap early and protects the middle on the 2-on-1.

title: Union Small Area Scoring Game
description: A creative 3-on-3 small-area game from Topher Scott where both teams are allowed to score on either net. The unusual net setup forces players to scan, create time and space, and recognize scoring opportunities from changing directions.
coaching_points: Keep the head up because both nets are live scoring options.
Players without the puck create space and present clear passing targets.
Use sticks on the ice both to request passes and remove lanes defensively.
Defenders close time and space without overcommitting to one net.

title: USA 2 VS. 2 Drill
description: A continuous competitive 2-on-2 from Coach Scott Moser. Two forwards carry through the center circle and attack two defenders. The defenders work forward-skating gap and angling; when they win possession they pass to the next forwards, while the original attackers transition to defense.
coaching_points: Defenders communicate, close gap skating forward and angle the attack toward the boards.
Keep defensive sticks on the ice and prevent cutbacks into the middle.
Offensive players keep their heads up and support each other through the entry.
After possession changes, transition immediately into the next defensive role.

title: Continuous 2 on 2 to 4 on 2
description: A continuous 2-on-2 progression from Joel Beal. Two forwards break out against two defenders. On the second whistle, two additional defensemen activate at the far blue line to create a 4-on-2 with point shots and net-front traffic. The next whistle launches a new 2-on-2 the other direction.
coaching_points: Forwards create strong breakout angles and support underneath the puck.
On entry, create local 2-on-1s and avoid turnovers at the blue line.
During the 4-on-2, forwards get to the net for tips and rebounds.
Defenders maintain gap on the rush and box out when the point players activate.

title: 2 vs. 3 Cross Drop Drill
description: A cross-and-drop rush drill from Topher Scott. Two forwards cross at the start and drop the puck before attacking three defenders. The high defending forward works on angling while the defensemen hold the line, forcing the attackers to enter with possession and create a scoring chance.
coaching_points: The puck carrier shows poise and looks to enter with possession instead of automatically dumping.
The second attacker supports underneath and remains available.
The high defender angles with the stick in a useful lane.
Defensemen step up together and protect the middle of the ice.

title: Dig, Pass & Shoot!
description: A wall retrieval and quick-shot sequence. The first player digs the puck off the boards under control and moves it to a teammate in the slot, who catches and releases quickly for a shot.
coaching_points: Get the puck off the wall cleanly with the head up.
Deliver a firm pass to the receiver's shooting area.
The shooter prepares the hands before the puck arrives.
Release quickly instead of settling the puck for an extra stickhandle.

title: Puck Elevation Rebound Drill
description: A close-range scoring drill that simulates dead pucks and rebounds around the crease. Players work on getting underneath the puck and elevating it quickly over sticks or a goalie's pad.
coaching_points: Keep the hands away from the body so the blade can work underneath the puck.
Pull the top hand back while pushing the bottom hand forward.
Get the puck elevated quickly without a long wind-up.
Finish rebounds immediately instead of drifting away from the crease.

title: Net Awareness Shooting - Pass, Spin & Shoot
description: A net-awareness shooting sequence where the shooter passes through two teammates, receives the puck back, spins and shoots. Repetitions are performed spinning both toward and away from the net.
coaching_points: Use peripheral vision to stay aware of the net through the spin.
Prepare the hands before the return pass arrives.
Keep the hands away from the body for a quick release.
Work both turning directions so the player can shoot from either side.

title: Feed Or Lead
description: A passing and timing drill where the first player makes a tight turn along the boards, exchanges the puck with a teammate, then jumps around an obstacle into open ice. The passer must decide whether to feed the player directly or lead them into space for the shot.
coaching_points: Use verbal and non-verbal communication before the pass.
Jump to open ice immediately after the exchange.
The passer reads the receiver's route and chooses feed versus lead.
Catch the puck in a shooting position and release quickly.

title: Underhandle Defense Passing
description: Five defensemen work through a retrieval and passing sequence. A coach rims or spots a puck into the corner, the retriever gets onto the puck's hip and moves it efficiently through the passing group, and the final defenseman finishes with a shot.
coaching_points: Retrieve with the head up and move the puck before pressure can arrive.
Do not overhandle or dust the puck.
Every defenseman takes at least two hard strides after moving the puck.
Deliver hard tape-to-tape passes and finish the sequence with a shot through traffic.

title: Position Over Possession Circle
description: Two players race from opposite hash marks toward a puck placed on the faceoff dot. The goal is to win inside body position before possession; the winner protects the puck inside the circle while the opponent tries to regain it or force it out.
coaching_points: Win body position before reaching for the puck.
Use leverage, balance and a low center of gravity.
Protect the puck with the hips and shoulders once possession is established.
Keep repetitions short and competitive.

title: 2v2 Shooting Board
category: 2 vs 2 / Net Front / Small Area Game
description: Two players from each team battle around the net while a designated shooting-board player waits near the top of the circle. After every turnover, the team gaining possession must first move the puck to its shooting board before attacking the net.
coaching_points: Defenders protect the middle and cut off passing lanes.
Battle for net-front position and box out away from the puck.
Offensive players create screens, tips and deflection lanes.
Recover loose pucks quickly and move possession to the shooting board before re-attacking.

title: 2vs2 + Player Behind the Net
description: A 2-on-2 small-area game with one support player from each team stationed behind the net. Before a team can score, it must complete a pass to its support player below the goal line, creating movement and down-low support reads.
coaching_points: Work into open ice to become a scoring threat.
Lose the defender and find soft areas when the puck goes below the goal line.
Transition immediately between attack and recovery after turnovers.
Maintain puck support through movement and quick exchanges.

title: 4Check 1 on 1 Angling
description: Two players first race to a puck on the faceoff dot and battle inside the circle for possession. On the second whistle, the puck carrier attacks around the top cone while the player without the puck stays forward-facing and angles the attacker toward the outside.
coaching_points: Use hips, legs and body leverage to win and protect possession.
Control the middle and shield the puck before trying to escape.
The defender keeps an active stick and takes away the cutback.
Maintain forward skating and controlled edges while angling the attacker.

title: Basic Cross Over Skating Station
description: A basic crossover skating station using one faceoff circle. Players complete two laps around the circle, focusing on crossover mechanics, then stop back at the blue line. The direction alternates each repetition and pucks can be added after the skating pattern is established.
coaching_points: Stay low through the crossover and push with both inside and outside edges.
Cross the outside skate completely over without standing up.
Alternate directions so both sides develop equally.
Add a puck only after the skating mechanics remain clean.

title: Quick Coach 2 on 1 with Backcheck
description: Two forwards skate toward the coach, transition backward while facing the puck, then transition forward as the coach passes to one of them for a rush. A defender sprints toward center and gaps up. A backchecker can be added behind the coach to increase urgency and pressure the weak-side attacker.
coaching_points: Forwards transition without losing sight of the puck and attack with speed.
The defender reads which forward receives the pass and establishes inside position.
The backchecker tracks the weak-side attacker first.
Communicate so the defender and backchecker sort the rush without duplicating coverage.

title: 2 vs. 2 Stop & Starts
description: Four players perform stop-and-start skating between the blue and red lines, then race toward the far end. The coach sends the puck to one side, and all four players must immediately read possession and sort themselves into two attackers and two defenders.
coaching_points: Face the coach on every stop so the play stays in view.
Accelerate hard out of each stop and compete for possession.
Weak-side players read the puck winner before choosing offense or defense.
Transition immediately instead of waiting for the rush roles to become obvious.

title: Swedish Transition Series #2
description: A Swedish transition progression where the defense makes the neutral-zone pass, jumps into open ice to receive the puck back and leads a three-player rush into the zone. F1 drives the net while F2 trails into the high slot and provides defensive replacement awareness.
coaching_points: Defense follows the pass into open ice instead of remaining stationary.
F1 drives hard through the middle to push back coverage.
F2 trails into the high slot and stays aware of defensive responsibility.
Keep the passing sequence moving so the rush enters with speed.

title: Neutral Zone Support 3 on 1 - #2
description: A neutral-zone support progression where the defenseman activates from the top of the circles, receives from F1, improves the passing angle and returns the puck. F2 times support through the middle while F1 drives the net, giving F2 both a backdoor option and a high-trailer option.
coaching_points: The defenseman moves the feet before and after receiving so the passing angle improves.
F2 times the support route instead of arriving early and becoming stationary.
F1 drives hard to the net with the stick available.
Read the backdoor option first, then use the high trailer if the lane is taken away.

title: 2 - 0 Drive
description: Two players leave together and skate around their cones. The coach chooses one player to receive the puck. The puck carrier gains the offensive blue line while the partner stays onside, drives the far post and receives a cross-ice pass for the finish.
coaching_points: Gain the blue line with control before forcing the cross-ice pass.
The weak-side player stays onside and drives the far post at full speed.
Keep the stick on the ice and present a clear target.
Pass through the available seam instead of sending the puck behind the receiver.

title: 2 on 0 Escape
description: The coach passes to either forward. The receiver attacks the blue line and uses an escape just inside the zone while the partner drives the far post. After the first scoring chance, the far-side player retrieves a second puck in the corner and finds the original shooter in the slot.
coaching_points: Attack the blue line with speed before using the escape.
The off-puck forward drives through the far-post lane and keeps the stick available.
After the first shot, transition immediately to the second puck.
The original shooter reloads into open slot ice instead of standing at the net.

title: Neutral Zone Attack with Speed #2
description: A speed-entry skill drill. The forward attacks through the neutral zone, works around the cone as a defender reference, protects the puck through the turn and drives hard to the net for a finish.
coaching_points: Carry speed through the neutral zone before making the move.
Use body position to shield the puck around the defender cone.
Keep the feet moving after the move instead of gliding.
Drive directly into a scoring area and finish the rep at the net.

title: Neutral Zone Turnover 2 on 2
description: Two defensemen begin in an offensive transition sequence through the neutral zone. On the whistle the forwards immediately attack them 2-on-2, forcing the defense to shift from offense to defense, recover its gap and defend the blue line.
coaching_points: Defense transitions from offense to defense immediately on the whistle.
Retake ice before settling into the backward gap.
Defenders communicate and try to stand the rush up at the blue line.
Forwards attack with pace, width and support before the gap is established.

title: 4 on 2 D-Zone Coverage
description: Two puck carriers work behind the net while two offensive forwards operate in front against two defenders. The players behind the net move the puck back and forth looking for an opening while the defenders track both puck and threats in front.
coaching_points: Defenders keep heels oriented toward the net and maintain inside position.
Check over the shoulder constantly so both puck and player locations are known.
Use active sticks to take away passes into the slot.
Offensive players change position and timing rather than standing in front.

title: Quick Transition 2 on 1
description: D1 skates to the blue line, receives a pass from F1, walks toward the middle and shoots. F1 and F2 work around the net, receive a pass from the next forward in line and immediately transition up ice against D1 in a live 2-on-1.
coaching_points: The defenseman gets the first shot through quickly and then transitions immediately to defend.
Forwards move around the net with purpose and receive the transition pass in motion.
Attack the 2-on-1 before the defenseman can reset the gap.
Keep the off-puck forward available as a real passing threat.

title: Transition Passing Sequence #2
description: The second variation in a transition passing series adds an extra pass. The player moves the puck to the opposite line, receives it back, makes another pass and then transitions toward the boards to continue the flow.
coaching_points: Move the puck quickly and receive with soft hands.
Transition the feet immediately after passing rather than watching the puck.
Keep spacing between lines so passes stay flat and direct.
Increase pace only when the passing sequence remains clean.

title: Strip & Transition to Low-High Shot
description: A full-ice transition warm-up that begins with a forward being stripped of the puck, moves through a defense-to-forward transition pass into a 2-on-0 rush, and finishes with a low-to-high pass for a point shot with traffic at the net.
coaching_points: Defense protects the inside lane and wins the strip with body position before moving the puck.
Make the transition pass crisp so the forwards can attack with speed.
Forwards communicate, support each other through the rush and arrive at the net with purpose.
Finish the sequence with a clean low-to-high pass, a quick point shot and a screen or deflection.

title: Transition Series #1
description: A full-ice transition passing and shooting sequence. The defenseman explodes backward, receives a puck from the coach and quickly moves it to the wall. The forward receives in motion and attacks for a shot while the defenseman recovers and repeats the pattern to the opposite side.
coaching_points: Defense transitions the feet quickly and handles the puck only as long as needed.
Deliver a firm, accurate outlet pass to a moving target.
Forwards receive facing up ice with the feet moving.
Attack the shot with speed and hunt the rebound before exiting the rep.

title: Neutral Zone Over-speed Transition
description: Two players work a neutral-zone overspeed sequence. One builds speed on a looping route while the puck carrier transitions from forward to backward and back to forward before making a flat pass. The receiver attacks the offensive blue line with lateral speed and finishes in the middle.
coaching_points: Build maximum controlled speed through the neutral zone.
Keep the feet moving while handling the puck through each transition.
Make the pass flat and on time so the receiver can stay in stride.
Attack the blue line with lateral crossover movement, then drive into a scoring lane.

title: Bruins Transition Drill
description: A two-player neutral-zone transition drill built around timing, backward-to-forward skating and a return pass. The first player carries through the middle, moves the puck to the transitioning partner, then receives it back while attacking the blue line with speed before cutting inside to shoot.
coaching_points: Time both routes so the puck carrier and support player arrive together.
Transition backward and forward without losing speed.
Return the puck flat and early enough for the receiver to attack the blue line in stride.
Use lateral movement at the line and finish by driving into the middle.

title: 3 v 1 Wall Play
category: 3 vs 1 / Wall Play / Small Area Games
description: Three attackers play against one defender in a tight-area possession game with a goalie. The offensive group uses quick puck movement, including options from behind the net and off the wall, while the defender works to disrupt passing lanes and protect the middle.
coaching_points: Defender keeps the stick active and works to take away the most dangerous passing lane.
Offense moves the puck quickly instead of holding it under pressure.
Use rims, banks and behind-the-net support to change the defender's angle.
Keep players moving so the 3-on-1 advantage creates new passing and scoring lanes.

title: 1 vs 1 Fox and Hound
description: Two players race around separate cones after the coach sends a puck off the boards. Both players compete to win possession and turn the race into a live 1-on-1 scoring chance.
coaching_points: Keep the feet moving through the puck instead of reaching for it.
Win inside ice after gaining possession.
Protect the puck with the body while driving toward a scoring lane.
Compete through the finish instead of ending the rep at first contact.

title: 2 vs. 2 Finnish Buffet Game
description: A continuous full-ice 2-on-2 game that repeatedly moves players from offense to defense and back into transition. Possession must advance through a neutral-zone support player before the next attack develops.
coaching_points: Defenders communicate switches and manage gap in a large space.
The puck carrier reads whether the attack is 1-on-1, 2-on-1 or 2-on-2 before forcing a play.
The off-puck attacker works to create a support lane and an odd-player advantage.
Transition immediately when possession changes and change hard when the game calls for it.

title: Full Ice Overspeed Skating Progression #2
description: Players leave from opposite corners, use quick crossovers around the circles, then change gears down the length of the ice. The route alternates controlled full strides with a short maximum-foot-speed segment.
coaching_points: Use quick feet through the crossover sections without losing body control.
At controlled speed, emphasize long and powerful full strides.
Increase foot speed sharply through the overspeed segment.
Maintain posture and edge control while changing gears.

title: Michigan Neutral Zone Timing Drill
description: A three-player neutral-zone timing sequence built around a defenseman receiving while moving backward, using an escape, and connecting the forwards through a timed regroup. The entry finishes with a delay and a late defenseman joining the attack.
coaching_points: Defense calls for the puck and controls it while moving instead of stopping the feet.
Forwards time support routes so they receive with speed and separation.
Use the one-touch wall connection to keep the regroup moving.
Net drive creates room for the delay pass to the late defenseman.

title: Four Lines Overspeed Shooting #1
description: Players sprint to the blue line, use tight high-tempo crossovers through the neutral zone, then support across the middle for a pass. They receive in motion, attack wide with speed and finish with a shot before hunting the next rebound.
coaching_points: Make the neutral-zone crossovers tight and fast.
Support the puck through the middle and call for the pass.
Receive in stride and keep the feet moving through the shot.
Stop at the net and hunt the next rebound.

title: Four Lines Overspeed Shooting #3
description: A passing progression in the four-line overspeed series. The skater follows the same high-tempo route, receives a pass after the first turn, moves the puck back to the original line, then supports through the middle to receive it again before attacking up ice.
coaching_points: Keep the feet moving through both turns and every puck touch.
Move the puck quickly after the first reception.
Support through the middle instead of drifting away from the play.
Call for the return pass and attack the zone with speed.

title: Chip and Chase Angle Checking Drill
description: A full-ice angling and checking progression that starts with a quick give-and-go shot, then turns into a chip-and-chase race. The puck carrier attacks the far cone and offensive zone while the checker works from the back shoulder to angle the play outside.
coaching_points: Checker matches the puck carrier's speed before applying pressure.
Stay on the back shoulder to remove the cutback to the middle.
Puck carrier protects the puck and attacks the blue line with speed.
At minimum, force the rush outside and deny a quality middle-lane scoring chance.

title: Double Chip Flow Drill
description: A high-tempo full-ice flow drill using two chip passes. P1 carries up ice, P2 swings through the slot for the first chip, and P3 times a neutral-zone route for the second chip. P2 then drives the net while P3 attacks wide and feeds the finish.
coaching_points: Time each swing so the receiver skates into the chip instead of waiting for it.
Keep both chip passes playable and into space.
After making the second chip, drive the net hard.
Attack wide with speed, read the delay and deliver a hard pass to the net driver.

title: Half Horse Shoe Chip
description: Two diagonal players go at the same time in a four-line flow. The puck carrier crosses the neutral zone and passes to the opposite line. The receiver steps inside for a better wall-chip angle, the original passer collects the chip with speed, and the second player drives the far post for the return pass.
coaching_points: Open up early to receive the cross-ice pass.
Step inside before chipping so the puck comes off the wall at a useful angle.
The original passer retrieves the chip at speed and attacks the zone.
The supporting player sprints to the far post with the stick available.

title: Half Horse Shoe Give & Go
description: Four lines are set along the boards with diagonal groups alternating. The puck carrier moves up the wall, curls toward the middle around the neutral-zone dot, makes a quick give-and-go with the next player in line and then attacks the net for a shot.
coaching_points: Carry with speed before curling into the middle.
Present the stick and make the give-and-go quickly.
Return the puck into the skater's path rather than behind them.
Keep the feet moving through the catch and shot.

title: The U Transition Drill
description: A four-line passing sequence shaped by a large U route. The first player moves the puck across the ice, then skates up and across the red line before opening up for a return pass and attacking the net. Opposite pairs alternate each repetition.
coaching_points: Move the first passes quickly so the skating route stays on time.
Open the hips and stick to the puck while completing the U-shaped route.
Receive the return pass in motion.
Alternate sides so both directions and both passing sequences are trained.

title: Quick Gap 1 on 1
description: A full-ice 1-on-1 designed to force the defender into a tighter gap. The forward transitions toward the wall to receive a pass while the defender moves from center ice, reaches the dot and transitions backward to meet the rush.
coaching_points: Defense closes space early instead of surrendering the blue line.
Forward receives the puck while moving and attacks with pace.
Defender transitions backward with the chest and stick aligned to the rush.
Keep each side on its half of the ice until center to avoid traffic.

title: Shoot and Shadow 1 vs. 1
description: A two-end 1-on-1 progression that begins with the defense receiving while transitioning backward and walking the puck to the middle for a shot. The forward hunts the rebound, becomes a breakout outlet and then attacks up ice while the defender recovers to establish gap.
coaching_points: Defense controls the first pass while moving and gets the shot through.
Forward follows the pass, hunts the rebound and then reloads inside the dots as an outlet.
Receive the breakout pass flat and in stride to create separation.
Defense pivots and recovers quickly enough to keep the rush outside.

title: Warm Up Delay
description: A four-line timing drill through the neutral zone. The outside skater cuts into the middle for a timed pass, enters the offensive zone and uses an escape toward the boards to buy time for the passer to join the attack for a return pass and shot.
coaching_points: Time the first pass so it reaches the receiver in the middle with speed.
Enter under control before using the escape move.
The supporting player joins immediately after the pass instead of watching the play.
Use the delay to create space, then deliver the return pass into a shooting lane.

title: Long Stretch Flow Drill
description: A full-ice flow warm-up that alternates outside-lane shots with a middle-ice support route. After shooting, the player swings back through the middle, receives a pass from the line and one-touches the puck into space for the next skater before the sequence continues.
coaching_points: Attack the first shot with speed and continue skating after the release.
Swing through the middle with the stick available as a passing target.
Use a soft one-touch pass into space so the next player can skate onto it.
Maintain spacing and timing so both ends can run continuously without congestion.

title: Four Lines Flow #3
description: Opposite lines go together in a four-line passing flow. The first player moves the puck to the line directly across, loops around the center circle, receives it back and then moves it to the next support option before continuing into the attack.
coaching_points: Pass early enough for the skating route to stay continuous.
Circle with speed and keep the stick presented for the return pass.
Move the puck immediately after receiving instead of overhandling.
Keep both sides synchronized so the drill flows cleanly through center ice.

title: Shadow Recovery Drill
description: Forwards build speed around the faceoff circle and receive a pass in stride through the neutral zone. Defensemen begin backward, transition forward to shadow the rush, then recover and pivot to maintain a tight outside gap as the forward attacks the net.
coaching_points: Forwards accelerate through the circle and receive the pass without breaking stride.
Defense transitions forward aggressively enough to match the rush.
Recover with quick feet and pivot before the attacker can gain the middle.
Keep the forward outside the dots while maintaining stick and body position.

title: Transition Pivot Hockey Races
description: Two players race through a sequence of forward skating, backward pivots and recovery turns before opening up around the center-ice cone and sprinting for a loose puck. The competitive format forces quick feet and clean forward-to-backward transitions.
coaching_points: Get fully across the blue line before each backward transition.
Open the hips cleanly and avoid unnecessary crossover steps on the final pivot.
Explode out of every transition instead of gliding.
Compete through the puck and continue the play to the net.

title: Three Zone Transition Pivots with Pucks
description: Players carry a puck through a full-ice three-zone skating pattern. In each zone they crossover into a circle, transition backward, pivot forward again and maintain puck control before finishing the final zone by cutting into the middle for a shot.
coaching_points: Keep the puck under control through every crossover and pivot.
Transition backward without standing up or losing speed.
Push the pace while preserving clean edge work and puck control.
Finish by attacking laterally through the slot with the head up.

title: Full Ice Overspeed Skating Progression Drill #4
description: Players use a large offensive-zone crossover circle to build speed, then accelerate down the ice using repeated pairs of lateral crossovers in each direction. The progression emphasizes cross-under power, full extension and quick lateral movement at speed.
coaching_points: Generate power from the cross-under instead of simply stepping over.
Use full extension through each stride while building speed around the circle.
Keep the crossover pairs quick and explosive down the length of the ice.
Stay balanced and athletic while changing lateral direction.

title: Full Ice Overspeed Skating Progression #1
description: Players leave opposite corners and skate an extended full-ice figure pattern around multiple circles. The goal is maximum controlled foot speed through the turns while maintaining sound crossover and cross-under technique.
coaching_points: Move the feet as quickly as possible without sacrificing edge quality.
Use powerful cross-under pushes through every circle.
Keep the head up when routes intersect near center ice.
Maintain speed through the turns rather than coasting between circles.

title: Four Lines Flow #1
description: The first drill in a four-line flow series. Opposite lines start together, exchange a quick give-and-go across the neutral-zone dots, and then the original puck carrier attacks the zone for a long shot while the passer feeds the next repetition.
coaching_points: Start both sides together so the timing remains consistent.
Make the give-and-go flat and quick.
Attack the zone immediately after the return pass.
Keep the drill moving by feeding the next player as soon as the first sequence clears.

title: 4 Lines Below the Puck Zone Rush
description: A four-line timing progression that develops a three-player zone entry. Players exchange passes across the neutral zone, repeatedly swing underneath the puck for support, then head-man the puck so three forwards enter with width and controlled spacing.
coaching_points: Stay below the puck while timing every support route.
Keep the early passes more lateral than vertical to preserve spacing.
Head-man the puck when the lead forward has created separation.
Enter as a connected three-player unit with a middle lane and weak-side width.

title: 1 on 1 Recovery Drill
description: A recovery-focused one-on-one. The defender first skates to the neutral-zone dot and transitions toward the middle while the forward waits to attack. Once released, the forward drives outside and the defender must recover toward the near post, re-establish inside position and defend the rush.
coaching_points: Defense recovers toward the post instead of chasing from the outside.
Pivot and sprint before re-engaging the puck carrier.
Forward keeps the feet moving and drives the far-post lane.
Defender protects inside ice and forces the play away from the middle.

title: 2 Dot Overspeed Skating Drill
description: A full-ice overspeed skating route that weaves players around the faceoff dots from one end to the other. The emphasis is sustained foot speed through repeated turns rather than coasting between patterns.
coaching_points: Keep the feet moving continuously through the entire route.
Use clean edge work and crossover mechanics around each dot.
Push the pace above normal comfort while staying under control.
Keep the head up as players travel through the middle of the rink.

title: Extended Chip & Chase
description: A long continuous repetition combining a give-and-go shot, a chip-and-chase race, back pressure, a second rush and a net drive. The sequence forces both players to skate hard over a large area while generating multiple shots and recovery situations.
coaching_points: Make the opening give-and-go quickly and stop at the net after the shot.
Chip the puck into playable space and apply real pressure from behind.
Puck carrier protects the puck while attacking through the far cone and blue line.
Finish the final rush with width, a hard outside shot and a committed net drive.

title: Short Track Flim Flom
description: A high-tempo overspeed drill with two skaters leaving together. The lead player races to the far blue line for a shot while the trailing player applies pressure, then the trailing player continues through a four-dot crossover route, receives a pass at speed and attacks the opposite end.
coaching_points: Both players explode immediately and create real chase pressure.
Maintain speed through the neutral-zone crossover pattern.
Swing deep enough to receive the pass facing up ice rather than looking backward.
Receive in stride, make a move inside the blue line and shoot with the feet moving.

title: Brittish Bulldog - Full Ice
category: Puck Control / Warm Up / Full Ice
description: Players start on the goal line with a puck or ringette and try to cross the ice while several bulldogs remain between the blue lines and attempt to steal possession. The activity develops heads-up puck control, awareness and evasive movement in traffic.
coaching_points: Keep the head up while carrying through traffic.
Change speed and direction instead of skating a predictable straight line.
Protect the puck with the body when pressure arrives.
Bulldogs stay inside the neutral-zone boundaries.

title: Torpedo - Full Ice
description: A full-ice skating game where players cross from goal line to goal line while coaches stationed along the neutral-zone boards slide or send cones across the ice as torpedoes. Players use awareness, agility and quick direction changes to avoid being hit.
coaching_points: Skate with the head up and scan both sides of the rink.
Use quick lateral cuts and speed changes to avoid the torpedoes.
Keep sticks safely off the playing surface for this activity.
Coaches keep all torpedoes low and controlled.

title: Sharks & Minnows - Full Ice
description: Players skate from one goal line to the other while the sharks remain between the blue lines and try to tag them. A progression adds two power turns inside the neutral zone, forcing players to read pressure and choose the safer direction before escaping.
coaching_points: Keep the head up and read where the sharks are before entering the neutral zone.
Change speed and direction to create separation.
On the power-turn variation, choose the turn direction based on pressure.
Accelerate immediately out of each turn.

title: Bank Robbers
category: Puck Control / Warm Up / Full Ice
description: Players begin on the goal line and enter the neutral zone to retrieve loose pucks while a small group of police tries to tag them. Successful players carry recovered pucks out of the neutral zone and place them in the far net.
coaching_points: Scan before entering the neutral zone and identify open pucks.
Use deception and changes of direction to avoid the police.
Control the puck immediately after retrieval and exit the pressure area.
Keep the activity fast and competitive while maintaining awareness of other skaters.

title: Brittish Bulldog with Control Turns
category: Puck Control / Control Turns / Full Ice
description: A full-ice Brittish Bulldog variation where puck carriers must complete two control turns inside the neutral zone while avoiding the bulldogs and protecting possession.
coaching_points: Keep the head up before entering the neutral zone.
Read pressure and choose the control-turn direction that creates the most space.
Protect the puck through both turns instead of exposing it to the defender.
Accelerate out of the second turn and escape the neutral zone.

title: Superman Relay Races (Full Ice)
description: Teams race full ice using borders. Each skater takes a run, dives onto the border in a superman position and slides it forward, then gets up and returns to tag the next teammate until the border reaches the far goal line.
coaching_points: Organize teams with similar numbers and ability.
Skate hard into the dive while keeping the activity controlled and safe.
Get back to the line quickly so the next teammate can go.
Keep the relay competitive and continuous.

title: Four Lines 1 on 1
description: A four-line 1-on-1 progression that connects a defense transition, a neutral-zone support pass and a live rush. The defender controls the puck while moving backward, moves it to the far support line and then becomes the defender on the next attack.
coaching_points: Defense controls the puck while moving backward and creates a clean passing angle.
The forward times the neutral-zone swing to receive with speed and separation.
Do not get ahead of the support pass and lose usable space.
Defenders close gap early and challenge the rush near the blue line.

title: Two Step Off the Wall 1 on 1
description: An in-zone 1-on-1 progression with two stages. First, the forward works off the wall against a recovering defender for a coach pass. Then both players compete for a loose puck along the wall and the forward can cycle it to the coach for a return chance at the net.
coaching_points: Forward wins the race to usable ice and attacks back toward the net.
Defense stays on the defensive side and maintains inside position.
On the battle rep, compete through the loose puck instead of reaching.
Eliminate the attacker's stick and deny the return pass from the coach.

title: Bonus 1 on 1
description: A corner battle begins 1-on-1. The player who wins possession and completes a pass back to their own line earns a teammate, immediately turning the play into a 2-on-1 attack.
coaching_points: Compete for body position before reaching for the puck.
After winning possession, protect it long enough to find the support pass.
The bonus player joins immediately and creates width.
The player who loses possession transitions quickly into the defender.

title: D to D Up Half Ice 1 vs 1
description: Two players work a defense-to-defense passing sequence with a coach at center ice. After the D-to-D exchange, one player transitions up ice for a return pass from the coach while the partner gaps up and defends the resulting 1-on-1.
coaching_points: Show a clear forehand target on every D-to-D pass.
Receiving defense moves away from pressure to improve the passing angle.
Transition forward immediately after the second pass.
The defending player retakes as much ice as possible before the 1-on-1 begins.

title: Tight Space 1 on 1
description: Forward and defender each skate a figure-eight route around staggered cones while carrying pucks. The defender returns their puck to line as the routes finish and then defends the attacking player in a tight-space 1-on-1.
coaching_points: Exit the figure eight with the feet moving and attack immediately.
Offense protects the puck and reads whether to drive the back shoulder or shoot through the defender.
Defense closes time and space early.
Use good stick position and keep the attacker outside.

title: Breakout Gap control 1 on 1
description: A demanding full-ice defense drill. The defender retrieves around the net, gets inside the dots, squares up before making the breakout pass and then must manage speed and gap against the same forward attacking back at them.
coaching_points: Retrieve inside the dots and square the shoulders up ice before passing.
Make the breakout pass from a position that preserves defensive balance.
Match the attacker's speed while retaking ice.
Aim to make the defensive play at or before the blue line.

title: Breakout Pass 1 on 1
description: A compact breakout-to-1-on-1 station. The defender retrieves a coach dump beside the net, skates behind the goal and moves the puck to a forward opening along the wall. The forward then circles the cone and attacks the same defender.
coaching_points: Defender shoulder-checks and retrieves with control.
Forward gets low and opens to the puck along the wall.
Make the breakout pass to the forward's tape and into usable space.
After the pass, the defender closes the gap and keeps the rush outside.

title: 2 on 1 - 2 on 2 Full Ice Regroup
description: A full-ice flow drill that starts with a forward give-and-go and criss-cross, moves into a regroup with the defense, and finishes with either a 2-on-1 or 2-on-2 rush depending on the variation.
coaching_points: Forwards exchange the first passes while keeping speed through the criss-cross.
Use the defense as a true regroup option instead of forcing the puck vertically.
Support the puck after the regroup and attack with spacing.
Defense steps up quickly after the pass to close the gap.

title: 2 on 1 with Backchecker
description: A full-ice 2-on-1 with pressure from a backchecker. The defense establishes gap while two forwards swing into the rush. The backchecker releases when the coach passes and tracks the weak-side forward to remove the backdoor option.
coaching_points: Forwards move their feet and drive hard to the net.
Weak-side forward keeps the stick available while attacking the far post.
Backchecker identifies the non-puck carrier and works to get defensive-side position.
Defense communicates with the backchecker and keeps the puck carrier from crossing the middle.

title: Defense Read 2 on 1
description: Two forwards sprint around cones and receive a coach pass while a defender steps out, transitions away from the pass and plays the rush. The drill isolates the defender's read between denying the passing lane and controlling the puck carrier's path.
coaching_points: Defense protects the middle first and keeps the stick in the passing lane.
Do not overplay the pass and give the puck carrier a free lane to the net.
Force the shot from an angle the goalie can handle.
Forwards attack with speed and make the defender choose.

title: Cross Ice 2 on 1
description: A one-zone 2-on-1 that alternates teams. Two attackers use different routes around the net and cone to time their rush while the opposing defender loops around the far net and meets them in a live 2-on-1.
coaching_points: Time both offensive routes so the attackers arrive together.
The second forward gets even with the puck carrier before the rush develops.
Defender establishes inside position and protects the passing lane.
Play through the rep until a goal, save, turnover or clear.

title: Panda 2 on 1 with Backcheck
description: A one-goalie full-ice transition drill. D1 retrieves a puck behind the net and outlets to one of two swinging forwards, who attack D2 in a 2-on-1. A third forward can add light forecheck pressure on the retrieval and then backcheck to the open attacker, turning the rush into a 3-player defensive read.
coaching_points: D1 protects the puck behind the net and delivers a crisp tape-to-tape outlet.
The two attackers swing with timing and communicate before entering the rush.
D2 and the backchecker communicate responsibility early.
Backchecker identifies the open attacker and works to regain defensive-side position.

title: Toronto 3 on 2
description: A continuous 3-on-2 rush and down-low cycle progression. A forward passes to a defenseman, who transitions the puck to the opposite forward line for a 3-on-2. A second puck is rimmed to create a 3-on-2 below the tops of the circles, and the sequence transitions back the other direction on the next whistle.
coaching_points: Forwards fill separate rush lanes and keep sticks available.
Defenders protect middle ice, use active sticks and angle the attack outside.
After the rim, offensive players move to open ice and support the puck below the dots.
Transition immediately on the next whistle so the drill stays continuous and fast.

title: 3 zone 3 puck
description: A full-ice team possession game divided into three zones. Each team places players in the defensive, neutral and offensive zones, and players must stay in their assigned zone while passing the puck forward to teammates. The coach can add extra pucks until as many as three are in play.
coaching_points: Puck carriers scan early and find the next available teammate.
Players without the puck move constantly into open passing lanes.
Use both verbal and non-verbal communication across zones.
When additional pucks enter, keep awareness high and continue supporting teammates.

title: 3 v 3 Pass Through The Cones
description: A competitive small-area possession game where teams score by completing passes through cone gates. Players cannot use the same gate twice in a row, forcing constant movement, support and awareness.
coaching_points: Defenders keep sticks on the ice and close passing lanes.
Forwards move to open ice and present clear passing targets.
Move the puck quickly instead of holding it under pressure.
Scan before receiving so the next option is already identified.

title: Picking Up Rims with No Pressure
description: A rim-retrieval skill drill. A player skates around a cone, shoulder-checks, collects a puck rimmed along the wall, gets off the boards and attacks the net for a shot.
coaching_points: Shoulder-check before the puck arrives.
Use strong hand position to control the rim cleanly.
Get the puck off the wall immediately after collection.
Drive toward the net with pace and shoot from a scoring area.

title: Gretzky Coffey Game
category: 3 vs 3 / Puck Support / Small Area Game
description: A one-zone game where one team activates offense through a stationary Gretzky behind the goal line while the other activates through a Coffey at the blue line. Three players per team compete in the middle and must use their designated support player before attacking.
coaching_points: Middle players pass and immediately move to open ice.
Gretzky scans before receiving and uses the net as protection.
Coffey uses deception and looks for shots when traffic is present.
Defenders keep heads on a swivel and sticks in passing lanes.

title: 2 vs 2 with Point Shot - Box Out
description: Two forwards battle two defenders down low while two offensive defensemen work the blue line. The attackers try to win possession and move the puck to the point for a D-to-D shot while the defenders box out and clear the goalie's sightline.
coaching_points: Compete for possession before forcing the puck to the point.
Point players move the puck D-to-D to improve the shooting lane.
Shoot for tips and rebound-producing areas.
Defenders establish inside position, lift sticks and give the goalie a clean view.

title: Poker 2 V 2 Game
category: 2 vs 2 / Two Puck / Small Area Game
description: A high-risk, high-reward two-puck game. Two players from each team enter with a puck and can choose to attack, defend or switch roles at any time while trying to score on the opposing net.
coaching_points: Communicate a plan immediately and keep communicating as roles change.
Keep the head up to track both pucks and all four players.
Use an active stick even while transitioning between offense and defense.
Make quick decisions about when to attack and when to protect your own net.

title: Pass Through The Circle Game
description: A possession game around a faceoff circle. Four attackers keep the puck away from two defenders and score a point by completing a pass through any part of the circle.
coaching_points: Attackers keep the head up and jump to open ice as outlets.
Use eyes and body deception before passing.
Defenders keep sticks down and protect the circle before chasing.
Think about the next pass before the puck arrives.

title: Escape The Circle
description: One puck carrier starts inside a circle surrounded by stationary players who may move their sticks but not their feet. The puck carrier must use deception, scanning and tight-area puck skills to escape the circle with possession.
coaching_points: Keep the head up and scan for open seams.
Use deception with the hands, eyes and body.
Change direction and pace to create an exit lane.
Maintain full puck control through the escape.

title: Griffs Entry Skills
description: A zone-entry skill sequence. The player passes to the far blue-line line, posts through the neutral zone, receives the puck back and attacks a coach while using entry moves such as a mohawk with cut hands or a mohawk delay.
coaching_points: Build speed before the return pass arrives.
Use the mohawk to keep the chest and eyes toward the play.
Move the hands away from pressure when attacking the coach.
Change the shooting angle and stop at the net after the finish.

title: Summerside Drill
description: A two-part full-ice transition drill. Defensemen retrieve and move pucks while forwards time neutral-zone support routes. The progression adds a D-to-D exchange before the defense hits a forward in stride for an attack.
coaching_points: Defense scans before retrieval and uses deception on the turn up ice.
Get hips facing up ice quickly before making the outlet.
Forwards time the route so they are usable neutral-zone outlets.
After the shot, forwards stop at the net before returning to line.

title: 4 V 2 Two Touch Game
description: Back-to-back nets divide two simultaneous 4-on-2 games. The four attackers are limited to two touches while trying to score, and defenders who win the puck move it to their four teammates on the opposite side.
coaching_points: Players without the puck must move early to support a teammate limited to two touches.
Scan before receiving so the next play is ready immediately.
Defenders keep sticks in lanes and pressure aggressively when the puck carrier runs out of options.
Keep passes firm and playable.

title: 2 vs 2 Corner Battle Tag Up
description: A 2-on-2 corner battle around a net placed near the faceoff dot and facing the corner. If the defending team wins possession, it must tag up at the red line before it can attack the net.
coaching_points: Get low and strong over the skates during battles.
Use the body to protect possession.
Communicate continuously with the partner.
Defenders keep sticks down; attackers without the puck jump to open support space.

title: Double Goals Game
description: A competitive game with two nets and two cone or tire gates. Teams can score by completing a pass through a gate or by scoring on a goalie, giving players multiple scoring options and forcing constant scanning.
coaching_points: Keep the head up to recognize both gate and net scoring options.
Communicate and move to open ice off the puck.
Defenders protect both the gates and the dangerous net-front areas.
Keep sticks on the ice as both passing targets and defensive tools.

title: Rondo Circle Keep Away
description: Three to eight passers form around a circle with one or more defenders inside. The outside players keep possession while the defender tries to intercept, with the player responsible for a turnover rotating into the middle.
coaching_points: Passers keep the head up and see both teammates and defender.
Use deception by looking one way and passing another.
Defenders keep sticks down to remove passing lanes.
Move the puck quickly and vary passing techniques as skill improves.

title: Protect The Puck Warm-Up (Individual & Team)
category: Puck Protection / Keep Away / Warm Up
description: A two-part competitive warm-up. Players first battle individually over a limited number of pucks, then combine into teams for keep-away with fewer pucks than players.
coaching_points: With possession, protect the puck with the body and skate to open space.
Without a puck, compete with the stick on the ice to win one back.
In the team phase, use give-and-go support instead of holding the puck.
Scan constantly because multiple battles and pucks can develop at once.

title: The Chaos Weave
description: A full-ice awareness drill with multiple players and pucks moving through the neutral zone at once. Players weave through traffic while controlling or exchanging pucks and then attack the net.
coaching_points: Keep the head up because multiple routes and pucks cross simultaneously.
Communicate before passing and receive with soft hands.
Maintain control through traffic instead of rushing the puck touch.
Increase complexity only when the group can preserve spacing and awareness.

title: NEHDA 3 Puck
description: A three-player passing progression built around three stationary pucks. Players exchange ten continuous passes while the primary skater works footwork and body orientation; later progressions finish with a shot or shot-pass deflection.
coaching_points: Prioritize passing quality and clear communication.
Primary skater keeps toe caps and chest oriented in-zone as much as possible.
Underhandle receptions—backhand receive to forehand pass with minimal dribbling.
Shoot with purpose instead of merely finishing the pattern.

title: Cross-Ice Situational Game
description: A cross-ice situational game that starts 1-on-1 and can change instantly when the coach activates extra forwards or defenders. The evolving numbers force players to recognize and react to changing advantages.
coaching_points: First defender takes an angle that denies the middle.
All players keep the head up because the situation can change at any moment.
Newly activated players enter immediately and communicate their role.
Attackers recognize numerical advantages before forcing a play.

title: 6 vs. 3 Alley Game
description: Six attackers surround a central alley occupied by three defenders. The offense must move the puck across the alley before shooting while the defenders angle, disrupt lanes and try to keep the puck to one side.
coaching_points: Defenders eliminate time and space with body position and stick.
Keep sticks in passing lanes and pressure when a clean opportunity appears.
Offense uses deception and scans before moving the puck.
Off-puck attackers move out of blocked lanes to become passing options.

title: Split Ice Full Length Backcheck Game
description: A continuous full-length backcheck competition run on each half of the rink. One player attacks with a puck while a second chases from behind. After the backchecker reaches the designated release point, they collect a coach pass and immediately become the next attacker while a new player tracks them the other way.
coaching_points: Puck carriers push the puck with speed instead of over-stickhandling.
Backcheckers move the feet until the shoulders are even rather than reaching from behind.
Transition immediately from the completed backcheck into the next attack.
Keep each group on its half of the rink so both sides can run continuously.

title: Horseshoe Regroup One Goalie #2 (Hinge)
description: A one-goalie horseshoe regroup variation that adds a hinge between the defensemen. F2 moves the puck to D1, D1 sends it outside to D2, D2 hinges it back to D1 in the middle, and D1 finds F2 timing the opposite side for the attack.
coaching_points: Defensemen move their feet to improve the angle before every pass.
D2 gets outside the dots before hinging the puck back to the middle.
F2 times the swing so the final pass is received with speed.
Keep the sequence crisp and connected instead of allowing stationary puck touches.

title: Drop Pass Angle 1 on 1 Drill
description: A half-ice angling progression. The defenseman starts with the puck, strides into the zone, cuts toward the middle and leaves a drop pass for the forward. The forward attacks outside while the defender recovers and angles the rush away from the middle.
coaching_points: The forward attacks with speed immediately after collecting the drop pass.
The defender closes from inside-out and maintains a strong stick position.
Take away the middle lane and force the attacker outside the dots.
Finish the defensive rep by limiting the forward to a poor-angle shot.

title: Neutral Zone Puck Skills #2
description: A neutral-zone puck-control progression built around stationary pucks and wall protection. The player pushes the puck beyond a forehand-side puck, toe-pulls it back, moves it to the backhand around the next obstacle and continues through the pattern before using the wall-protection portion of the station.
coaching_points: Keep the hands away from the body so the toe pull can cover more space.
Move the puck forehand-to-backhand cleanly around each stationary puck.
Protect the puck with the body when working along the wall.
Add an extra controlled stickhandle between obstacles once the base pattern is clean.

title: Horseshoe Re-Group Drill
description: A high-tempo horseshoe flow with two players leaving each corner. One attacks for an initial shot and then reloads to the net while the second swings through the neutral zone, regroups D-to-D and receives the puck back for a wide-angle shot designed to create a rebound.
coaching_points: First shooter follows the shot, stops at the net and reloads for the rebound.
Second forward times the neutral-zone swing instead of arriving early.
Defense moves the puck D-to-D quickly and returns it to the moving forward.
Shoot for a playable rebound with the net-front player arriving on time.

title: Transition, Protect & Shoot
description: A two-variation transition drill where the defense receives while moving backward and advances the puck to a forward entering with speed. The forward protects the puck against passive pressure, gets inside the dots and shoots to create a rebound for the defenseman driving the far post.
coaching_points: Defense transitions quickly and creates a clean outlet angle.
Forward receives in motion and keeps the body between pressure and puck.
Attack inside the dots before releasing the shot.
Shoot for the far pad when the defenseman is arriving for the rebound.

title: Four Cone Neutral Zone Drill
description: A multi-action neutral-zone drill built around four cones. Defense retrieves and outlets under pressure while two forwards create support and a net drive; simultaneously another forward attacks the opposite direction against a defender recovering gap for a live 1-on-1.
coaching_points: Defense retrieves on the forehand and prepares to move the puck quickly.
Support forward times the neutral-zone swing and stays available for a direct or bank pass.
Backchecker works to stay defensive-side of the net-driving forward.
Recovering defense retakes as much ice as possible before the opposite 1-on-1.

title: Quick Hinge Warm Up Hockey Drill
description: A high-tempo flow warm-up built around a quick defensive hinge. The puck moves outside on the first D-to-D pass, back to the middle on the second, and then to a forward timing a neutral-zone support route before attacking the blue line for a long shot.
coaching_points: First defensive pass moves the puck outside.
Second defenseman hinges the puck back toward the middle.
Forward times support so the final pass is not a vertical stationary pass.
Attack the blue line with speed and finish with a long shot on net.

title: Split Passing Game
description: A small-area passing game played around a rectangular box. Two offensive teams occupy opposite sides and work together to pass through the box while defenders inside try to intercept. Offense scores by connecting through the box; defense scores by taking passes away.
coaching_points: Move immediately after passing to create a new lane.
Use minimal stickhandling and move the puck before pressure closes.
Defenders stop and start with active sticks instead of circling.
Receivers show a clear target and stay available on opposite sides.

title: Transition Sequence 1 on 1 to 2 on 1
description: The sequence begins with a down-low 1-on-1 battle. On the whistle that puck dies, a new puck is placed in the neutral zone and the high defenseman retrieves it to transition with two forwards into a 2-on-1. The transitioning defenseman can also join to create a 3-on-1 variation.
coaching_points: Compete through the initial 1-on-1 and protect possession until the whistle.
React instantly to the new puck and transition up ice.
Forwards attack the 2-on-1 with width and pace.
If the defense joins, recognize the new numerical advantage without slowing the attack.

title: Sabre O-zone Escape Drill
description: A full-ice touch-and-escape progression. A player receives a long pass, attacks controlled stick pressure from a coach, escapes toward the wall and then finds a supporting teammate through the middle for a shot. The shooter stays at the net to begin the next repetition.
coaching_points: Make the long pass tape-to-tape and receive it with the feet moving.
Attack pressure before using the escape instead of turning away too early.
Accelerate immediately after the escape to create separation.
Support through the middle with timing so the passing lane stays available.

title: Four Wise Men Warm Up
description: Four players are active at once in a full-ice warm-up. The first skater receives a pass while moving down the wall, attacks the blue line inside-out and shoots from the outside lane. The passer then swings low across the opposite blue line, receives a flat pass and takes the second shot while the first shooter hunts the rebound.
coaching_points: Receive every pass under control and with the feet moving.
Attack the blue line with speed before shooting from the outside lane.
The second shooter swings low enough to receive a flat pass.
The first shooter immediately hunts the rebound and arrives at the net for the second shot.

title: Transition Chip 2 on 0
description: A full-ice 2-on-0 transition drill built around a soft chip off the boards. The puck moves from the corner line to support through the middle, then to a player who opens to the outside and chips the puck into space. The weak-side player times the entry to retrieve the chip with speed while the chipper drives the slot for a return pass.
coaching_points: Create separation from the wall before making the chip.
Chip the puck softly enough that the receiver can skate onto it.
The weak-side player times the entry and retrieves with speed.
After the chip, drive immediately to the slot and present the stick for the return pass.

title: Full Ice Overspeed Skating Progression #3
description: Players leave from opposite corners, use quick crossovers around the top of one circle and bottom of the next, then continue down the ice with three crossovers toward the middle followed by three back toward the outside.
coaching_points: Move the feet as fast as possible through the circle work.
Complete a full three crossovers in each lateral direction.
Create power from the outside edge of the skate crossing underneath.
Stay balanced and keep speed through the entire full-ice route.

title: Swedish Transition Series #1
description: A defense-to-forward transition sequence focused on gaining the middle and timing neutral-zone support. D1 receives while moving backward, gets between the cones and finds F2 in stride; F1 fills underneath, while F2 attacks wide and looks for F1 arriving high.
coaching_points: Defense receives the puck while moving and faces up ice through the transition.
Gain the middle before making the next pass.
F2 times the neutral-zone route so the puck arrives in stride.
After the pass, D1 follows the play and transitions backward as if possession has changed.

title: Full Ice Overspeed Skating Progression #2 with Pucks
description: The puck-carrying variation of the full-ice overspeed progression. Two players build speed through the route, then one attacks wide for a moving shot while the other cuts to the middle on the inside edge for a high-slot finish.
coaching_points: Do not let puck handling slow the skating cadence.
Push the puck into space instead of overhandling it.
The outside player shoots with the feet moving from the wide lane.
The second player gains the middle on the inside edge and finishes from the high slot.

title: Full Ice Overspeed Transitions
description: Players start backward, transition forward at the top of the first circle, skate forward to the bottom of the next circle, then transition back to backward skating and use C-cuts down the rest of the ice.
coaching_points: Stay low and balanced on the balls of the feet.
Open the hips cleanly before accelerating forward.
When transitioning backward, keep the chest square to the end boards.
Use as few unnecessary crossovers as possible before settling into strong backward C-cuts.

title: Stretch and Go Flow
description: Four corner lines run a staggered full-ice warm-up. P1 advances up the wall and finds P2 swinging through the middle. P2 enters wide, delays below the dots and returns the puck to P1 arriving in the high slot for a quick shot.
