coaching_points: Time the middle swing so the pass is received in motion.
Enter the offensive zone wide and stay under control below the dots.
Present a clear high-slot target after making the first pass.
Receive and release the final shot as quickly as possible.

title: Avalanche Flow Drill
description: A continuous full-ice passing and timing drill with multiple shots. Players exchange short passes, transition through the corners, create horizontal passing angles through the middle and finish the sequence by joining a 2-on-0 rush at the opposite end.
coaching_points: Create horizontal passing angles instead of relying on long vertical passes.
Forwards face up ice quickly after transitioning through the corner.
Defense gains the middle while controlling the puck before moving it.
Time the final support so the two-player rush attacks with speed.

title: Lulea 2 v 0 Neutral Zone Warm Up
description: A neutral-zone warm-up built around manipulating passive pressure and finding passing lanes. Two forwards work the puck through players stationed on the blue lines, then join for a 2-on-0 rush with a coach providing passive resistance.
coaching_points: Players without the puck move to create a clear passing lane.
Puck carriers use lateral movement to manipulate the passive defender.
Join the 2-on-0 with a strong middle-lane drive and wide support.
Goalie warm-up shots should come from outside the dots with attention to rebound control.

title: Double Swing Full Ice Flow Drill
description: A higher-level full-ice flow drill built around three consecutive passes. P1 shoots and continues into the corner, P2 leaves a puck and turns inside for a return pass, then P3 swings outside to receive the next pass before attacking the opposite net.
coaching_points: Keep all three passes crisp and on time.
After shooting, continue immediately into the next support role.
Turn toward the puck and present the stick before receiving.
Once timing is clean, run the sequence from both ends to increase pace.

title: 2 on 0 Continuous Chip Flow
description: A continuous 2-on-0 flow with a neutral-zone chip. P1 moves the puck across to P2, P2 attacks the coach and chips the puck off the wall to a swinging P3, then drives hard to the net while P3 enters wide and shoots for a rebound.
coaching_points: P2 attacks the coach before placing a controlled chip into space.
P3 calls for the chip and times the swing to receive it with speed.
After chipping, P2 drives directly to the net and hunts the rebound.
Keep the sequence continuous by rotating the original puck carrier into the next support role.

title: 4 Lines - Series 4
description: A four-line warm-up variation that requires players to track where the next pass comes from and where their next support route goes. The receiver in neutral ice attacks the blue line with speed and finishes with a moving shot.
coaching_points: Players stay engaged so they know both the next passing target and next receiving lane.
Receive the neutral-zone pass in motion.
Attack the blue line with speed rather than slowing before entry.
Shoot with the feet moving and continue through the play.

title: React and Angle Drill
description: Two players skate to the blue line, make tight turns and return toward center. The coach passes to either player, instantly defining offense and defense. The defender must react and angle the puck carrier away from the middle and toward the outside.
coaching_points: React immediately when the coach identifies the puck carrier.
Defender closes on an angle that removes the middle of the ice.
Keep the feet moving while matching the puck carrier's speed.
Do not allow the attacker to cut back behind the angle.

title: Transition Angling Drill
description: A defensive progression built from a neutral-zone overspeed transition. The defender first angles the supporting puck carrier to force the play toward the wall, then closes on the receiver and works to deny the cutback to the middle before competing to the net.
coaching_points: Move the feet while keeping the stick in the passing lane.
Force the first puck carrier toward the strong-side wall.
Close shoulder-to-shoulder on the receiver and take away the middle.
Finish the repetition by competing all the way to the near post.

title: 2 on 2 Full Ice
description: Two defenders receive the puck at the blue line and create a middle shot before two forwards release into a full-ice 2-on-2. The defense is challenged to manage an intentionally tight gap and stop the rush before clean offensive-zone possession is established.
coaching_points: Defense establishes the gap early instead of backing into the zone.
Force the rush to dump the puck, go offside or lose possession before the blue line.
Forwards attack with speed, width and support.
Defenders communicate and protect inside ice through the rush.

title: 4 Lines - Series 2
description: A progression from Series 1 where the moving player works the puck through each line before it is returned. The sequence forces players to track where the puck is coming from, where it goes next, and maintain timing through the neutral zone.
coaching_points: Know the next pass before the puck arrives.
Use crisp tape-to-tape passes so the pattern stays on time.
Keep the feet moving through every reception.
Communicate and present a clear target to the passer.

title: 4 Lines - Series 3
description: The third four-line progression adds repeated give-and-go exchanges with each line. The moving player must read the pattern while the second player in each line stays engaged because they often receive and return the pass.
coaching_points: Use crisp passes and strong stick presentation.
Keep the pace high with crossovers and active feet.
Use touch passes when the timing allows.
Second players in line stay alert and ready to return the puck.

title: 4 Lines - Series 5
description: A four-line passing progression where the skater passes to the opposite blue-line line, receives it back, returns it again, then continues around center ice expecting another pass from the opposite side before finishing the sequence.
coaching_points: Pay attention to both where the puck is passed and where the return pass will come from.
Make the first give-and-go quickly without stopping the feet.
Continue the route immediately after returning the puck.
Receive the final pass in motion and finish at pace.

title: Swiss Warm Up Passing Drill
description: A continuous full-ice passing warm-up that relies on timing and flat passing angles. Players must stay connected to the puck and avoid getting too far ahead of the play so the next pass can be delivered cleanly.
coaching_points: Give the passer a flat, usable passing angle.
Do not skate ahead of the puck and break the timing.
Receive and move the puck without unnecessary stickhandling.
Maintain continuous flow from both ends.

title: Stretch Pass 3 on 0
description: Three players leave together. F1 loops beyond center and returns toward the coach for a long stretch pass while F2 and F3 pivot to stay facing the puck. F1 can one-touch the puck to either support player, creating a three-player zone entry with a net drive, trailer and multiple finishing options.
coaching_points: F2 and F3 stay open to the puck while timing their routes.
F1 receives the stretch pass in motion and looks to move it quickly.
Enter with width, a hard far-post drive and a high trailer.
Use a one-touch pass when the support timing allows.

title: Cyclone Passing Drill
description: An advanced one-touch passing drill in which the active player circles through the neutral zone, completes give-and-go passes with each line while skating forward, pivots backward for another full passing circuit, then transitions forward and finishes with a shot.
coaching_points: Move the feet continuously through the entire sequence.
Use one-touch passes whenever possible.
Present the stick early and minimize extra stickhandling.
Make clean forward-to-backward and backward-to-forward transitions before the final shot.

title: Big W Warm Up
description: A full-ice passing warm-up with several quick exchanges. P1 banks the puck behind the net to P2, receives it back, works give-and-go passes with P3 and P4 while advancing up ice, then attacks the far blue line for a shot as the next repetition starts from the opposite side.
coaching_points: Passes must be quick and sharp to keep the drill from breaking down.
Move immediately after every pass to become the next support option.
Keep the give-and-go exchanges in stride.
Alternate sides and maintain continuous flow from both ends.

title: Half Ice Angle Drill
description: A half-ice angling and checking drill where the offensive player carries around a center-ice obstacle and attacks the net while the defender takes a speed-matched angle from below the hash marks to keep the puck outside.
coaching_points: Defender takes the angle with speed instead of chasing from behind.
Match the attacker's pace and stay roughly a half-step behind.
Protect the middle and deny the cutback lane.
Offense uses puck protection and edge work to expose a poor angle.

title: 4Check Loose Pucks
description: A forward and defenseman race around separate obstacles toward a loose puck and compete for possession. The defender works for inside body position and an outside angle, while the forward tries to gain inside leverage, win the puck and attack the net.
coaching_points: Establish inside body position before arriving at the puck.
Use hips and shoulders to engage while staying balanced.
Keep the stick active in the opponent's lane.
Win the battle, recover immediately and transition to offense or defense.

title: Belfry Full Ice Angle Drill
description: Players start on opposite blue lines, skate around their assigned cones and react to a coach's wall pass. The player opposite the puck must identify the angling role immediately, then both players compete live 1-on-1 the full length of the ice.
coaching_points: Read the wall pass immediately and identify offense versus defense.
Defender takes ice away on an angle rather than skating directly at the puck carrier.
Match speed and protect the middle lane.
Play the rush live to the far net and compete through the finish.

title: 1 on 1 Angling Drill
description: Two staggered lines create a deliberate puck-retrieval advantage. The lead player retrieves a puck in the corner and tries to advance it up the wall while the trailing player works to angle, separate the puck carrier from possession and turn the play the other way.
coaching_points: If you cannot meet or beat the puck carrier, establish a proper angling route.
Defender closes from inside-out and prevents the cut to the middle.
Use body contact through the hands while maintaining balance.
Puck carrier protects the puck, reads the angle and tries to expose any open lane.

title: Angling Small Area Game
description: A cross-ice game where the team receiving the coach's pass must first skate around its net before attacking. That delay gives the opposing team an angling cue, creating repeated opportunities to close space, force turnovers and transition the other way.
coaching_points: Defenders recognize the angling cue and close space immediately.
Keep tight gaps while removing middle and passing options.
Use the small-area 1-on-1 version first, then progress to 2-on-2 or 3-on-3.
After a turnover, transition quickly to offense instead of stopping the play.

title: 4Check Sticklift and Drive
description: The player drops into the zone, initiates controlled body contact and uses a stick lift on the first pressure point to gain possession. After winning the puck, the player reads a second layer of pressure along the wall, protects possession and attacks the middle for a play on net.
coaching_points: Close the gap quickly with a balanced base.
Use the stick lift to separate the opponent from the puck.
Get the head up immediately after gaining possession.
Absorb the second contact with hips and shoulders while protecting the puck.
Escape pressure and drive the middle with speed.

title: 4Check Hip Flips
description: A wall-play puck-protection drill that teaches players to use their hips, body position and the boards to shield the puck under pressure while staying balanced enough to escape or make the next play.
coaching_points: Use hips and body position to keep the defender on the back side.
Close the hips toward the boards to create a barrier around the puck.
Stay low and balanced with the knees bent.
Keep the head up to read pressure and locate the next option.
Absorb contact without surrendering possession.

title: 4Check Breakout options
description: A breakout progression that starts with body contact down low. The player wins body position, retrieves the puck and moves it to a wall-side teammate, then accelerates up ice to support the breakout and read whether the next option is a give-and-go or a chip under pressure.
coaching_points: Initiate contact from a low, stable base.
Separate the opponent from the puck before retrieving it.
Communicate early with the wall-side teammate.
Accelerate after the pass to become a support option.
Read pressure and choose the give-and-go or chip-out option.

title: 4Check Body Contact Swing
description: The player angles a puck carrier or dummy up the wall, finishes controlled contact to separate the puck, then immediately finds a supporting defenseman. After making the pass, the player drives the slot for a return pass and a quick shot.
coaching_points: Establish a strong angle before initiating contact.
After contact, get the head up and find the next play immediately.
Move the puck quickly to the supporting defenseman.
Drive the slot with purpose after the pass.
Catch and release the return pass quickly.

title: Body Contact Hip Check w/ Breakout
description: The strong-side defenseman closes on a wall-side pressure point with controlled hip or shoulder contact, recovers the loose puck and moves it D-to-D. A center swings low for support, receives the next pass and chips around pressure while the backside defenseman completes the retrieval.
coaching_points: Step into the lane with balance and controlled contact.
Recover the puck quickly with the head up after contact.
Center times the low swing to support the breakout.
Keep every pass crisp and preserve spacing through the sequence.
Backside defense reads and retrieves the chip.

title: Body Contact Catching The Rim
description: A winger receives a rim under pressure and must read the attacker's angle before choosing an escape. Options include protecting and controlling the puck to the inside or using a high chip to relieve pressure and advance the breakout.
coaching_points: Read pressure early with the head up before the rim arrives.
Lead with the inside leg and shoulder to protect the puck.
Choose the escape based on the pressure angle rather than forcing one option.
Execute the chip or inside move with control and purpose.

title: Body contact sidewall with corner attack
description: The player races a pressure point to a loose puck in the corner, establishes body position through controlled contact, wins possession and immediately turns the battle into offense by cutting from the corner to the net for an in-tight finish.
coaching_points: Arrive low and establish inside shoulder position.
Keep the feet moving through contact to win possession.
Transition immediately from the battle to attack mode.
Keep the head up while cutting through traffic to the net.
Finish with pace and accuracy from tight space.

title: Body contact corner pressure
description: F1 retrieves a puck under pressure from behind, uses a controlled reverse hit to absorb contact and protect possession, then moves the puck to F2 behind the net. F1 releases from contact and drives the front for a return pass and quick finish.
coaching_points: Use shoulder position and the wall to stabilize the reverse hit.
Keep the eyes up while initiating and absorbing contact.
Move quickly from contact to puck control and passing.
Drive hard to the net immediately after the pass.
Finish the return pass without unnecessary stickhandling.

title: 1 v 1 Rush to 1 v 1 Puck Retrieval
description: A two-part 1-on-1 progression. The first rep has the defender shadow the puck carrier through a cone route before defending a rush. The same two players then transition into a dumped-puck retrieval where the defender tries to escape the zone and the forechecker angles to win the puck back.
coaching_points: Defender uses footwork and body position first instead of relying on the stick.
Puck carrier attacks with lateral movement and drives toward the middle when available.
On the retrieval, shoulder-check before arriving at the puck and protect it while escaping.
Forechecker closes from a good angle and finishes through the hands to create the turnover.

title: 1 v 1 Stick Battle
description: Partners share one stick and compete in short controlled battles, each trying to knock the other player off balance while maintaining a strong skating base. The drill is used as a contact warm-up and to reinforce posture, balance and leverage.
coaching_points: Stay low with a wide, stable base of support.
Use leg drive and body position rather than twisting the stick.
Keep the battle controlled and immediately reset after either player loses balance.
Use short high-effort repetitions with partners of similar size.

title: Hit Through the Hands
description: Two players move slowly up the wall with the puck carrier staying tight to the boards. The checker skates alongside and repeatedly finishes through the puck carrier's hands, combining body contact with stick pressure to stop forward progress and separate the player from the puck.
coaching_points: Puck carrier stays close enough to the wall to use it safely when absorbing contact.
Checker closes alongside the player before making contact instead of charging from distance.
Finish through the hands to stop forward momentum, not merely into the side of the body.
Combine body contact with stick-on-stick pressure to separate the puck at the same time.

title: Norwegian Flow Drill
description: A continuous full-ice flow run from opposite corners. P1 carries around the net, works give-and-go passes with successive support players while traveling the length of the rink, then receives the final return pass in the slot for a shot before rotating to the opposite line.
coaching_points: Support players stay alert because the last player in each line is part of the passing sequence.
Keep every give-and-go in stride so the puck carrier never has to stop.
Time the final support pass to arrive as the skater enters the slot.
Run both corners together once the group can maintain clean spacing.

title: Scissors Warm Up
description: A one-goalie warm-up built around quick give-and-go passing through center ice. P1 exchanges the puck with P2, then receives a coach pass near the blue line and attacks for a shot. The middle puck continues through the next pair as the drill flows across the ice.
coaching_points: Make the center-ice give-and-go passes quickly and accurately.
Move toward the passing partner rather than waiting stationary.
Open up for the coach pass before reaching the blue line.
Keep only one puck moving through the middle sequence so timing stays clean.

title: Tight Swivel Puck Control
description: Players control a puck through a tight pattern around pucks or cones arranged near a faceoff circle. The route requires repeated tight control turns and quick hip rotation while keeping the puck protected and close to the body.
coaching_points: Start slowly enough to execute clean control turns before increasing speed.
Lead each direction change with the hips and upper body.
Keep the puck protected on the safe side of the body through each turn.
Keep the head up as technique improves and build toward game-speed feet.

title: Retrieval Races
description: Players skate forward around the first cone, transition backward, then pivot toward the corner at the second cone to retrieve a puck. After the retrieval they accelerate out of the corner, attack the slot from the half wall and finish with a shot.
coaching_points: Use a clean forward-to-backward transition around the first cone.
Open the hips on the backward-to-forward pivot instead of crossing over.
Keep the feet moving through the puck retrieval.
Attack the slot immediately after exiting the corner and shoot inside the scoring area.

title: Neutral Zone Puck Control Setup #1
category: Puck Control / Stickhandling / Neutral Zone Station
description: A neutral-zone puck-control station where players first weave through cones using forehand and backhand control, then work control turns around tires and finish with additional control turns around cones. More advanced players can move the puck outside one side of an obstacle while their body travels on the opposite side.
coaching_points: Keep the head up and scan ahead instead of staring at the puck.
Use both forehand and backhand touches through the opening slalom.
Protect the puck with the body around the tires and control turns.
Advanced players separate puck and body around obstacles while maintaining control.

title: COW Hockey's Continuous 2 on 0
description: A continuous two-player passing warm-up. The first pair exchanges the puck with the opposite line, curls outside the dots while facing the puck, receives the return pass, makes one neutral-zone pass and attacks the net 2-on-0. As soon as the return pass is made, the next pair starts in the opposite direction.
coaching_points: Face the puck throughout both curls.
Keep the give-and-go passes flat and on time.
Make the neutral-zone pass while both players stay in motion.
Both attackers stop at the net and finish rebounds before exiting.

title: Four Lines Flow #2
description: The second four-line flow progression. Players swing through the neutral zone and complete a give-and-go with each line before attacking the offensive zone, creating repeated touches while maintaining speed and timing.
coaching_points: Keep the feet moving through every pass and reception.
Present a clear target while swinging through the neutral zone.
Make the give-and-go passes quickly so the route stays connected.
Enter the zone with speed and use the rep to reinforce shooting angles.

title: Outside Loop Passing
description: Two players move down the ice exchanging as many passes as possible. At the far blue line they loop outside: the puck carrier power-turns with control while the support player transitions to remain facing the puck, then both accelerate back up ice.
coaching_points: Pass frequently while skating at pace.
Puck carrier keeps the head up through the outside power turn.
The support player stays open to the puck through the transition.
Accelerate out of the turn instead of coasting back up ice.

title: 2 on 0 Quick Re-Group
description: Two players pass down the ice toward a coach or stationary player near the far blue line. After moving the puck to the coach just beyond center, both forwards swing underneath for support, receive it back and immediately transition into a 2-on-0 attack.
coaching_points: Exchange the puck while both skaters keep moving.
Time the regroup swing underneath the puck rather than getting ahead of it.
Receive the return pass with speed and separation.
Attack the net immediately after the regroup and finish the rebound.

title: Pre-Game Three Lane Transition Shooting
description: Three shooting lanes operate at once. Each skater passes to a stationary player at the red line, skates forward, transitions outside, receives the puck back and carries into the zone for a long shot from a different angle.
coaching_points: Move the feet from the first pass all the way through the shot.
Transition outside while keeping the chest and stick available to the passer.
Receive the return pass in stride.
Use all three lanes so the goalie sees shots from changing angles.

title: 2 on 0 React and Support Drill
description: Two forwards skate toward the coach, who sends a loose puck to one side. The strong-side forward attacks the puck while the weak-side forward stays below it and provides support. The pair then enters the zone, with the puck carrier going wide and the support player driving the high slot for a return pass.
coaching_points: React immediately to which side the coach sends the puck.
Weak-side support stays below the puck instead of getting ahead of the play.
Communicate and use a chip or pass when pressure arrives.
On entry, create width first and then fill the high slot for the return pass.

title: Transition Passing Sequence #3
description: The third variation in the transition passing series. The player works through the passing sequence, attacks the offensive blue line from the inside out, then makes a sharp cut toward the middle after gaining the zone and finishes with a shot.
coaching_points: Keep the passing sequence quick and clean before the entry.
Attack the blue line with the feet moving.
Make the inside-out entry at speed, then cut decisively to the middle.
Shoot in stride and follow the shot for a rebound.

title: Control Turn Puck Control
description: A half-zone station for younger players that develops puck control through three control turns before a shot. Players work around three cones, protecting the puck through each turn, then attack the net to finish.
coaching_points: Lead each control turn with the head and upper body.
Protect the puck on the safe side of the body around every cone.
Keep the feet moving as the player exits each turn.
After the third cone, accelerate into the scoring area and finish the shot.

title: Trinity Puck Control Drill
description: A half-ice puck-control circuit with three simultaneous lines. One line stickhandles creatively through scattered pucks, one performs tight figure-eights and protects around a dummy net, and one works wall protection before exploding into the slot. Each repetition finishes with a shot.
coaching_points: Keep the head up through every puck-control pattern.
Use tight edges and puck protection through the figure-eight station.
Work the wall with the body between pressure and the puck.
On the whistle, explode into the slot and finish quickly instead of coasting.

title: Puck Control Relays
category: Puck Control / Relay Races / Half Ice
description: A half-ice relay setup that trains three puck-control skills: single-shift moves through a line of pucks, protected control turns around cones, and pushing the puck at speed with one hand rather than overhandling it.
coaching_points: Use clean single-shift moves to move the puck outside each obstacle.
Protect the puck and keep the head up through the control-turn section.
Move the puck forehand-to-backhand around cones instead of stickhandling excessively between them.
On the speed section, push the puck into space with one hand and skate through it.

title: Control Obstacle Course Station
description: A skill station combining puck protection, passing, receiving, control turns and shooting. Players weave through cones, exchange a pass with the coach, circle two tires in opposite directions, then make a single-shift move through the final tires and shoot.
coaching_points: Use the body to protect the puck on both forehand and backhand sides of the cones.
Give the coach a firm pass and receive the return pass with the feet moving.
Circle each tire with the body between the obstacle and the puck.
Alternate the direction of the final single-shift move before shooting.

title: D-Zone 1 on 1 Give and GO
description: A defensive-zone 1-on-1 where the forward starts along the wall and can attack or move the puck low to a coach for a give-and-go. The defender angles from inside ice and stays defensive-side of the forward after the low pass instead of following the puck.
coaching_points: Angle the puck carrier up the wall while protecting the middle.
Stay with the offensive player after the puck is moved low.
Maintain inside body position on the route back to the net.
The forward reads whether to attack directly or use the give-and-go.

title: In-Zone 5 Player Pass and Follow
description: Five players are positioned around one zone. P1 passes to P2 and follows the pass into P2's spot; each player repeats the pass-and-follow pattern until the puck reaches P5, who finishes with a shot.
coaching_points: Pass before accelerating into the vacated spot.
Receive with the stick presented and move the puck quickly.
Stop and start hard between positions so the drill serves as a warm-up.
P5 gets the shot away quickly after the final reception.

title: Head Up Circle Passing Drill
description: Two puck carriers skate inside a circle while four to six players remain around the outside. The inside players make as many give-and-go passes as possible, finding available outside players and avoiding the same target twice in a row.
coaching_points: Carry with the head up and scan before passing.
Use different outside targets instead of repeating the same option.
Outside players stay ready with sticks presented.
Keep moving between passes so awareness is trained under motion.

title: Center Circle Tire Skating - Tight Transitions
description: Players weave around four tires near center ice while facing the same direction throughout the pattern. Alternating clockwise and counter-clockwise routes force repeated forward-to-backward and backward-to-forward transitions.
coaching_points: Keep the chest facing the designated direction around every tire.
Transition cleanly rather than adding unnecessary crossover steps.
Alternate the direction around each tire.
Accelerate immediately after every transition.

title: Center Circle Tire Skating - Control Turns
description: Four tires create a neutral-zone control-turn pattern. Players make a tight control turn at each tire and alternate turning direction from one tire to the next.
coaching_points: Enter each tire under control with knees bent.
Use both inside and outside edges through the turn.
Alternate left and right control turns throughout the pattern.
Accelerate immediately after each turn.

title: 2 to 1 Puck Protection Drill
description: Two offensive players each protect a puck inside a faceoff circle while one defender tries to knock both pucks outside the circle. The rep ends when both pucks are removed or the coach stops play.
coaching_points: Use body position and the stick to shield the puck.
Keep the feet moving instead of protecting from a stationary position.
The defender changes targets and attacks exposed pucks.
Rotate roles so every player works both protection and defensive pressure.

title: Four Cone Control Turn Station
description: Four cones create a compact skating station focused on control turns. Players move through each cone in sequence, first turning one direction around every cone and then repeating the pattern in the opposite direction.
coaching_points: Enter each cone under control before initiating the turn.
Keep the knees bent and weight balanced through the edges.
Accelerate out of every control turn.
Train both left and right turns equally.

title: 5 Puck Breakaway Races (Cross-Ice)
description: Two teams race to score five goals. The first player from each team carries a puck around their own net and attacks the opposite net. A goal releases the next teammate immediately; a miss must be retrieved and passed back before the next player can go.
coaching_points: Attack the far net with speed and finish under pressure.
After a miss, retrieve quickly and make a clean pass to the next player.
Every player must route around their own net before attacking.
Keep the competition continuous until one team scores all five.

title: Neutral Zone 2 on 2
category: 2 vs 2 / Neutral Zone / Small Area Game
description: Two players from each team enter the center-circle playing area and compete 2-on-2. Coaches feed new pucks when a goal is scored, the puck is frozen or it leaves play, creating repeated tight-space battles.
coaching_points: Support the puck in a small area instead of isolating into 1-on-1 play.
Defend inside position and communicate switches.
Use quick puck movement to create short 2-on-1 advantages.
Players on the outside can bump loose pucks back into play.

title: Transition Passing Sequence #4
description: The fourth transition-passing progression adds a coach or stationary player at center ice. After receiving the transition pass, the skater completes another quick give-and-go at center before attacking the blue line for an inside cut or outside shot.
coaching_points: Make the center-ice pass and return quickly enough to preserve speed.
Receive every pass while moving.
Read the entry option before reaching the blue line.
Finish with either a hard inside cut or a purposeful outside shot.

title: Transition Control & Outlet Passing
description: A player skates backward between two neutral-zone cones, receives an outlet pass, controls the puck while transitioning forward to the opposite side and moves it back to the wall. The player then returns to the cones and repeats.
coaching_points: Receive the puck under control while skating backward.
Transition toward the opposite side from the passer.
Handle the puck only as much as needed before making the outlet.
Keep the feet moving through every transition and reception.

title: Red River Skating and Passing Drill
description: A half-ice skating and passing sequence using three stationary passers. The active player works up the wall, transitions to face the puck, exchanges passes through the neutral-zone area, pivots forward, then transitions backward into the slot for a final return pass and shot.
coaching_points: Face the puck during every transition.
Make multiple clean passes without slowing the feet.
Pivot forward with possession before moving to the final passer.
Back into the slot under control and receive the final puck in a shooting position.

title: Pass and Move Quick Puck Movement Drill
category: Passing / Quick Puck Movement / Offensive Zone
description: A quick-puck-movement sequence where F1 carries around the net to F2, F2 moves it immediately to the point, and F3 walks the blue line before returning the puck. F2 then sends the puck through the box to F4, who finds F3 arriving in the middle for a one-timer.
coaching_points: Receive every pass ready to move the puck immediately.
Avoid unnecessary stickhandling that slows the sequence.
Point player walks laterally before returning the puck to change the passing lane.
Time the middle drive for the final one-timer.

title: Tic Tac Passing
description: A continuous neutral-zone passing warm-up. The active skater moves the puck through multiple stationary support players, accelerates around the line, receives a return pass before center, then completes another give-and-go before entering for a shot.
coaching_points: Move the puck quickly between support players instead of holding it.
Active skater accelerates through the route and presents the stick early.
Time each return pass so it reaches the skater in stride.
Finish the sequence with a shot, then rotate to the opposite side.

title: Shooting Gallery
description: Four players operate in two pairs inside one zone. Each shooter passes to a partner, receives a one-touch return and immediately shoots off the pass while the opposite pair alternates the next repetition.
coaching_points: Set up on the off-hand side to shorten the release.
Use firm one-touch passes and receive ready to shoot.
Shoot quickly off the return pass without extra stickhandling.
Focus on hard, low shots that hit the net.

title: 3 Player Passing Series Station
description: A three-player passing station with three progressions: one-touch passes while skating toward the target, repeated passing with control turns around the receiver, and passing while transitioning backward and forward so the moving player stays facing the puck.
coaching_points: Use soft hands rather than slapping at one-touch passes.
Keep the stick presented and call for the puck.
Control-turn variations should stay tight around the receiver.
On transition reps, stay facing the puck and pivot cleanly back to forward.

title: Tornado Pivot Passing
description: A defense-focused passing and skating pattern around the center circle. The active player works around the circle, exchanges passes with stationary players and controls the puck while skating backward and transitioning forward.
coaching_points: Make accurate passes to stationary targets.
Call for the puck and present a clear target.
Control the puck while skating backward.
Transition forward cleanly without losing puck control.

title: Tornado Passing Drill #2
description: A more demanding Tornado progression where the active player attempts a pass with every stationary player around the circle. The drill emphasizes rapid puck movement, quick pivots and body control rather than pure skating speed.
coaching_points: Start at a pace that allows every pass to be completed cleanly.
Move the puck quickly from one target to the next.
Use quick controlled pivots around the circle.
Increase skating speed only after passing and body control stay clean.

title: Finders Keepers (Teams) - Passing and Puck Control Drill
category: Passing / Puck Control / Small Area Game
description: Two teams compete to possess more pucks than the opposition. The coach sends an odd number of pucks into the playing area and players use awareness, communication, puck protection and passing to secure possession before the whistle.
coaching_points: Communicate before receiving so the next play is already identified.
Protect the puck when pressured and move it to an open teammate when support is available.
Players without a puck work to surround loose pucks and create support.
Keep the head up because multiple pucks and opponents are active at the same time.

title: 3 Player Station Passing
description: A three-player station built around repeated give-and-go passes. The active player exchanges the puck with both support players while moving through the station and can finish the sequence with a shot.
coaching_points: Give a target and receive with soft hands.
Move immediately after every pass instead of standing still.
Keep the give-and-go passes flat and on time.
Use the progression with one or two exchanges to match the group's level.

title: Shoot, Curl, Pass, Neutral Zone Station
description: Two cross-ice nets create a neutral-zone station. A player carries a puck to the opposite net for a shot, stops at the net, curls to a nearby puck pile and passes across to the first player in the opposite line, who repeats the sequence the other way.
coaching_points: Carry with the head up before shooting.
Stop at the net after every shot.
Curl quickly to the puck pile and make an accurate cross-zone pass.
The receiving player presents a target and attacks the opposite net immediately.

title: Stop and Start 1 vs. 1
description: Two players complete a stop-and-start skating sequence before racing for a loose puck. The winner attacks for a breakaway while the other player chases from behind and defends.
coaching_points: Explode out of every stop instead of standing upright.
Race through the loose puck and gain body position.
The puck winner attacks the net immediately.
The trailing player backchecks through the hands and stick without giving up.

title: Neutral Zone Puck Races #2
description: Two players race through mirrored tight control turns around tires in the neutral zone, then compete for a puck and attack the mini net.
coaching_points: Use tight control turns with the inside skate leading slightly.
Trust the outside edge of the inside skate around each tire.
Rotate the chest and head toward the exit of the turn.
Compete through the puck and transition immediately into the scoring chance.

title: Quarter Ice Obstacle Course #1
description: A quarter-ice obstacle course combining inside-edge work, one-foot step-overs, a full control turn and two-foot jumps before players race back to their line.
coaching_points: Stay balanced through the staggered-cone inside-edge section.
Land each one-foot step-over under control before the next obstacle.
Complete a tight full control turn around the tire.
Use knee bend and two-foot takeoffs over the final barriers.

title: Inside Edges Slalom Relays
description: Players slalom around a row of sticks using the inside edge of the outside skate, transfer weight between feet, complete the turn at the tire and race back to the line.
coaching_points: Use one strong inside edge around each stick.
Transfer weight cleanly from one foot to the other between obstacles.
Keep the chest and eyes directed toward the next turn.
Accelerate out of the final tire turn.

title: Tire Turn Relays - Control Turns
description: Players race straight to a tire, execute a controlled turn around it and accelerate back to the goal line. The setup can be run as quarter-ice or sixth-ice stations.
coaching_points: Trust the outside edge of the inside skate through the turn.
Lead slightly with the inside foot.
Rotate the chest and head toward the direction of travel.
Accelerate out of the turn with full forward strides.

title: Push & Pull Relays
description: Pairs race to a tire and back using two partner-resistance variations: one player pushes a backward-gliding partner, then the pair switches to a pull/chariot variation before changing roles.
coaching_points: The pushing player uses full forward strides instead of short choppy steps.
The backward player stays balanced and helps steer the pair.
In the pull variation, the front skater maintains posture and powerful extension.
Switch roles so both players perform each skating task.

title: Steps and Jumps Over Sticks Relay Races
description: Two relay variations use the same stick-and-tire setup. Players either step over each stick on one foot or use two-foot jumps, then finish with a control turn around the tire and race back.
coaching_points: On step-overs, land and stabilize on one foot before the next obstacle.
On jump reps, take off and land with both feet under the body.
Use a tight control turn around the tire.
Finish every repetition with strong forward strides back to the line.

title: Defensive Pivot Races
description: Two players race through a defensive-skating route. They skate forward to the low cone, transition backward toward the top of the circle, open the hips to pivot forward around the middle cone, then race for a puck in the slot.
coaching_points: Transition backward cleanly around the low cone without losing speed.
Open the hips at the top cone and pivot forward without unnecessary crossovers.
Move the feet faster than is comfortable through the transition.
Race through the loose puck and finish the play at the net.

title: Sweet Heart Relay Scoring Race
description: Two teams race simultaneously. Each player crosses behind their own net, attacks the opposite goalie on a 1-on-0, must score, then returns to the blue line and stops in hockey position before the next teammate can leave.
coaching_points: Keep the head up because players attack in opposite directions.
Attack the goalie with speed and finish the scoring chance.
After scoring, sprint back to the blue line and stop under control.
The next teammate leaves only after the previous player is stopped in position.

title: 3 Puck Break Away Races
description: Two teams compete in a full-ice breakaway race with three pucks. Players attack the goalie repeatedly and the competition continues until the scoring objective is reached, creating a fast conditioning game with repeated finishes.
coaching_points: Go full speed on every repetition.
Attack the goalie under control and finish each breakaway.
Recover quickly for the next puck instead of coasting after a shot.
Use a clear scoring target or time limit to keep the race competitive.

title: Amazing Scoring Race
description: Two teams run alternating breakaways. P1 receives a diagonal pass from P2 and attacks the opposite goalie. A goal releases P2 immediately; after a miss, P1 must retrieve a loose puck and deliver it to P2 before the next player can attack.
coaching_points: Make the opening diagonal pass flat and on time.
Attack the goalie with speed and finish the breakaway.
After a miss, recover the replacement puck immediately.
Keep the race continuous and compete to a goal target or time limit.

title: Neutral Zone Puck Races #1
description: Two players leave opposite lines, skate around one tire, complete a control turn around the second tire, then race for a puck played by the coach. The player who wins possession attacks the mini net.
coaching_points: Stay low and balanced through both tire turns.
Use a tight control turn around the second tire.
Accelerate immediately out of the turn.
Race through the puck and protect inside position before shooting.

title: Neutral Zone Puck Races #3
description: Two players race through a neutral-zone route that adds forward-to-backward and backward-to-forward transitions plus tight control turns. They finish by racing for the puck and attacking the mini net.
coaching_points: Flip the hips quickly when transitioning from forward to backward.
Stay low while skating backward and keep the feet active.
Transition back to forward without drifting wide.
Explode through the final control turn and compete through the puck.

title: Neutral Zone Puck Races #5
description: Two players race through a square of four tires using forward crossovers, complete a full lap, then skate to the far tire for a tight control turn before racing for a puck played into space by the coach.
coaching_points: Use fast, controlled crossovers around the four-tire square.
Keep the head up when the racers cross through the middle.
Stay low through the far control turn and accelerate out of it.
Compete through the puck and attack the net immediately.

title: Neutral Zone Puck Races #6
description: Players race through two sets of forward-to-backward and backward-to-forward transitions, then skate to a far tire, execute a tight control turn and compete for a puck played by the coach.
coaching_points: Transition forward to backward quickly without losing balance.
Keep the feet active while skating backward between tires.
Explode back to forward around each second tire.
Finish with a tight control turn and race through the puck.

title: Quarter Ice Puck Race #3
description: Players race forward to a low tire, transition backward while staying square to the net, skate backward to a higher staggered tire and then transition forward to battle for a puck.
coaching_points: Approach the first tire with speed and transition backward cleanly.
Stay low and balanced while skating backward.
Transition back to forward explosively at the high tire.
Race through the puck and immediately turn possession into offense.

title: Quarter Ice Puck Race #4
description: Players skate forward to a low tire, transition backward, weave through three staggered tires using backward crossovers, then race to a loose puck played by the coach.
coaching_points: Make the forward-to-backward transition tight around the first tire.
Use strong backward crossovers through the staggered tires.
Keep the chest and eyes up while weaving backward.
Transition to the puck quickly and compete through possession.

title: Quarter Ice Puck Race #5
description: Players start forward and use crossovers around the bottom of a four-tire box, transition backward between the far tires, transition forward around the third tire and race for a puck to create a scoring chance.
coaching_points: Keep the head up as the two racers cross near the bottom of the box.
Use powerful crossovers through the first section.
Transition backward smoothly without losing speed.
Explode forward out of the last transition and win the race to the puck.

title: Neutral Zone Puck Races #4
description: Two skaters work through tight control turns around the tire pattern, turn around the far tire, then race for a coach-played puck and attack the mini net.
coaching_points: Use tight control turns in both directions.
Accelerate out of every turn.
Match skaters with similar speed when possible.
Compete through the puck and finish the scoring chance.

title: Open Hips Ladder with Pucks
description: Players move through a stick ladder while opening the hips around each stick and maintaining puck control, alternating the direction of each rotation.
coaching_points: Open the lead foot and hips before entering each turn.
Ride the inside edges through the rotation.
Keep the puck under control while the feet change direction.
Build the skating pattern first, then increase puck-handling speed.

title: Open Hips Ladders Without Pucks
description: Players skate through a stick ladder using open-hip turns around each stick, completing the rotation and alternating direction from one stick to the next.
coaching_points: Open both hips and keep the knees bent through each turn.
Stay on the inside edges while rotating around the stick.
Complete the full circle before moving to the next stick.
Alternate direction to train both sides evenly.

title: 3 Cone Skills Series #3
description: Players make a puck move at the first cone, transition backward while handling the puck to the top of the triangle, then transition forward and continue into the next three-cone setup.
coaching_points: Attack the first cone with speed before making the move.
Keep the puck controlled during the forward-to-backward transition.
Stay low while skating backward.
Explode forward out of the final transition.

title: Heads Up Stickhandling Station
description: Four skaters enter the center circle with pucks at the same time, handle in traffic with their heads up, then exit diagonally on the next whistle as the next group enters.
coaching_points: Keep the head up and scan for other skaters.
Protect the puck while changing direction in traffic.
Use creative puck moves without losing control.
Exit quickly on the whistle so the next group can enter.

title: Neutral Zone 2 on 0 and Puck Control Station
description: Two players pass together toward the net for a 2-on-0 finish, then each retrieves a wall puck, works through the opposite puck-control course and finishes with another shot.
coaching_points: Pass in stride and support underneath the puck.
Finish the first attack with a purposeful shot.
Keep the head up through the puck-control course.
Switch lines so players work both forehand and backhand patterns.

title: Find the Lane Shooting Drill
description: A defenseman works from the point, first shooting from a stationary position and then pulling the puck laterally along the blue line to find a shooting lane before releasing.
coaching_points: Keep the head up while moving laterally.
Keep the puck on the forehand so the shot can be released quickly.
Change the shooting lane before releasing.
Shoot low and through the available lane.

title: Triple Shot Shooting Drill for Defense
description: A defenseman receives a coach pass and shoots after moving along the blue line, receives a second pass for another shot or one-timer, then goes to the net for a third pass and finish.
coaching_points: Receive the first pass in a position to move the puck laterally.
Release the point shot quickly after creating a lane.
Be ready for the second pass and one-timer option.
Finish the repetition by attacking the net for the third puck.

title: Puck Tag
description: Every player handles a puck while several taggers chase. Tagged players freeze and can be released when a teammate controls the puck through the triangle formed by the frozen player's skates and stick.
coaching_points: Keep the head up while handling the puck.
Use quick direction changes to avoid taggers.
Protect the puck while scanning for frozen teammates.
Encourage continuous movement and awareness.

title: Chase the Rabbit Without Pucks - Station
description: Players work in pairs with one skater leading through creative skating patterns around barriers while the second skater mirrors the route, then switch roles after the interval.
coaching_points: The leader should use varied turns, stops, backward skating and direction changes.
The chasing player mirrors the route as closely as possible.
Keep the feet moving and maintain control through tight spaces.
Switch leaders regularly so both players create and react.

title: Net Races
description: Players race around two closely spaced nets using tight turns, acceleration and body positioning. Run left-turn, right-turn, figure-eight or backward variations.
coaching_points: Make tight turns around each net and accelerate out of every turn.
Use body position to create and maintain separation.
Take efficient angles through the race pattern.
Change turn direction and skating variation to train both sides.

title: Body Contact Competitive Contact Cones
description: Two players begin in controlled body contact, then race to a loose puck between the cones. Each player battles for inside position and the winner attacks the net.
coaching_points: Start balanced and strong through controlled shoulder-to-shoulder contact.
Accelerate immediately when the puck becomes live.
Use body position to establish the inside lane to the puck.
Win possession and transition directly into a scoring attack.

title: Soft Chip Warm Up Drill
description: Players work from four lines. The puck carrier passes across, receives a soft chip into the zone with speed, retrieves it on inside edges and finds the second player driving the far post.
coaching_points: Create a good passing angle before making the soft chip.
Time the chip so the attacking player can skate onto the puck with speed.
Use inside edges and control through the retrieval.
Find the far-post player with a firm pass and finish the play.

title: 10 & 2 Edgework Tag
description: Two players work inside the station with one chasing the other. Players can change direction, but must use the 10-and-2 open-hip skating technique throughout the tag game.
coaching_points: Stay low and balanced while opening the hips.
Use clean inside-edge pressure through each 10-and-2 turn.
Change direction quickly without crossing the feet unnecessarily.
Progress by adding a puck or changing the skating roles.

title: Tire Stickhandling Shot
description: Players weave through a tire stickhandling setup, skate around corner tires, pass to a coach for a return pass and finish with a shot.
coaching_points: Keep the head up while navigating the tire pattern.
Use controlled hands around each obstacle.
Make a firm pass to the coach and present the stick for the return.
Receive the return pass in stride and shoot quickly.

title: Cornell Under-Handling With Shot
description: Players move through three cones or tires while keeping the puck on the forehand with minimal stickhandling, then shoot in stride after the final obstacle.
coaching_points: Keep the puck on the forehand side of the blade.
Use deep knee bend through tight turns.
Keep the head up and let the feet move the body around the puck.
Shoot in stride immediately after the final cone.

title: Blue Line Shuffles
description: Defensemen work laterally across the blue line through several progressions: skating only, passing with a partner, and moving laterally into a shot.
coaching_points: Keep the chest and toe caps facing the offensive zone.
Move the feet outside the line while keeping the puck onside.
Scan up ice while controlling or moving the puck.
Finish the final progression with a quick shot through the lane.

title: Single Shift Decision
description: Players attack a tire with the puck while reading the coach. The coach commits to one side and the player performs a single-shift move to the opposite side before shooting.
coaching_points: Approach with the head up and read the coach before making the move.
Sell the fake before shifting the puck.
Move the puck away from pressure in one clean action.
Accelerate out of the move and shoot without extra stickhandling.

title: Be Creative! Puck Skills Station
description: Players work freely through a station filled with cones, tires, sticks and other obstacles, using creative puck-control moves and direction changes during timed intervals.
coaching_points: Keep the head up while moving through traffic.
Use different moves on each repetition.
Mix control turns, shifts, transitions and puck touches with the skates.
Stay active for the full interval rather than waiting for open space.

title: Choose a Gate
description: The coach passes to the player and then occupies one of two gates. The player must read the coach, control the puck through the open gate and finish with a shot.
coaching_points: Receive the pass with the head up.
Scan the coach immediately after receiving the puck.
Attack the open gate without unnecessary stickhandling.
Accelerate through the gate and finish the play with a shot.

title: Skate Cross Station Progression #1
description: Players skate around two cones using control turns in both directions, take strong strides between turns and accelerate with full-length strides after the final cone.
coaching_points: Use proper control-turn body position around each cone.
Take strong strides immediately out of every turn.
Turn in both directions during the station.
Accelerate to full speed after the final cone.

title: Skate Cross Station Progression #2
description: Players work through a tighter multi-cone pattern than Progression #1, using sharp control turns and a few strong strides between each cone before accelerating out of the station.
coaching_points: Stay low and balanced through every control turn.
Lead each turn with the head and shoulders.
Take strong, purposeful strides between cones.
Use full-length strides to accelerate after the final cone.

title: Skate Cross Station Progression #3
description: Players use an even tighter cone layout that forces quicker direction changes and shorter recovery time between turns, then accelerate to top speed after the final cone.
coaching_points: Be ready to turn again immediately after each cone.
Use clean edges and avoid drifting wide.
Take one strong stride when space allows between turns.
Explode out of the last turn with full-length strides.

title: Push Puck and Shoot
description: Players push the puck with one hand while skating the length of the station, then bring the second hand back to the stick and finish with a shot on goal.
coaching_points: Push the puck with one hand until preparing to shoot.
Keep the puck close enough to maintain control at speed.
Keep the head up while skating.
Add speed only after the one-hand puck push is controlled.

title: M & W Control Turns & Shots
description: Players carry a puck through a staggered three-cone pattern using control turns, protect the puck through each change of direction and finish with a shot.
coaching_points: Use proper control turns around each cone.
Keep the body between the cone and the puck.
Maintain puck control through every turn.
Come out of the final turn ready to shoot.

title: Corner Tires 3 vs 3 - 1/3 Ice Station
category: 3 vs 3 / Small Area Game / Third Ice
description: Two teams play 3-on-3 inside one zone. Each team attacks the two tires at the far end and scores by hitting an opponent-side tire with the puck.
coaching_points: Move the puck quickly to change the point of attack.
Use width and support instead of chasing the puck.
Defend both scoring tires with good body position.
Keep shifts short and competitive.

title: 2 vs 2 vs 2 with Mini Nets
description: Three two-player teams compete around three mini nets. Each team protects one net while trying to score on either of the other two nets.
coaching_points: Scan constantly because there are two attacking options.
Support the puck while still protecting your own net.
Attack open space instead of forcing play into pressure.
Use short shifts to keep decision making and pace high.

title: Coach's Call With Mini Nets
description: Two teams line up beside the coach with a net at each end of the station. The coach calls how many players from each team enter, creating changing numerical situations from 1-on-1 through 3-on-3.
coaching_points: React immediately to the numbers called by the coach.
Recognize whether the situation is even-strength or an advantage.
Support the puck and attack open ice.
Keep rounds short so players experience many different numbers.

title: Soccer on Ice - Station
description: Players play soccer on the ice inside a station, using wide cone goals and their skating to move into space, defend, balance and change direction without relying on normal stickhandling.
coaching_points: Encourage constant movement and quick changes of direction.
Use the edges to stay balanced while competing for the ball.
Create width and open space for teammates.
Adjust the game from quarter-ice to sixth-ice based on group size.

title: Border Tag - Station
description: Two players stay within a stick length of a border while one tries to tag the other. Progressions change the skating requirement from forward to backward, transitions and open-hip skating.
coaching_points: Stay close enough to the border that the game remains tight and reactive.
Use quick starts, stops and changes of direction.
Progress from forward skating to backward and transition patterns.
Keep the knees bent and maintain balance through every turn.

title: 3 vs 3 with mini nets - sixth ice station
category: 3 vs 3 / Small Area Game / Sixth Ice
description: Two teams play 3-on-3 in a sixth-ice station using mini nets. A new puck is introduced after a goal and groups rotate after short competitive shifts.
coaching_points: Compete immediately for each new puck.
Support the puck with short passing options.
Use the small space to practice quick decisions and puck protection.
Keep shifts short and high-energy.

title: Coach's Call - Third Ice Station
category: Small Area Game / Variable Numbers / Third Ice
description: Two teams line up at the blue line beside the coach. Before each round the coach calls the number of players entering from each team, dumps in a puck and lets the group compete until a goal or whistle.
coaching_points: Listen for the numbers before jumping into the play.
Identify numerical advantages and disadvantages quickly.
Use puck support and spacing when your team has extra players.
Defend the middle and communicate when outnumbered.

title: Turns & Stops With Shots (Quarter Ice)
description: Players work opposite sides of a quarter-ice station: one side emphasizes two-foot stops at staggered cones, the other control turns. After the cone sequence, players collect a puck and finish with a shot.
coaching_points: Use a complete two-foot stop and stay balanced at each stop cone.
Rotate the head and shoulders through every control turn.
Accelerate out of each stop or turn.
Collect the puck under control and finish with a quick shot.

title: Hand Soccer
description: Players use their hands to move a ball through wide cone goals in a small area. The game forces players to stay low, use their edges and compete for space without relying on their sticks.
coaching_points: Keep a deep knee bend while moving the ball.
Use edges and quick direction changes to create separation.
Move into open space when a teammate controls the ball.
Keep the game continuous and competitive.

title: Freeze Tag
description: Designated taggers chase the other skaters inside the station. Tagged players freeze until a teammate completes the chosen release action, creating a continuous awareness and agility game.
coaching_points: Keep the head up and scan for taggers and open space.
Use quick starts, stops and direction changes.
Stay balanced when dropping to or recovering from the frozen position.
Rotate taggers often to keep the pace high.

title: Tennis Ball Astroids
description: Coaches shoot tennis balls across the station while players skate inside the designated area trying to avoid being hit. Tagged players drop to their knees and can be reactivated by a teammate.
coaching_points: Keep the head up and track threats from both directions.
Use edges and quick changes of direction to avoid tennis balls.
Stay inside the designated playing area.
Encourage players to help re-activate teammates when safe.

title: 2 vs 2 with Regular Nets - Station
description: Two teams play 2-on-2 in a compact station using full-size nets and goalies when available. Short shifts keep every player involved and create repeated puck-protection and support situations.
coaching_points: Compete through possession and protect the puck in tight space.
Support the puck carrier with a short passing option.
Defend the middle and communicate with the goalie.
Use 60-90 second shifts and restart with a new puck.

title: Puck Tag with Ringettes
category: Puck Control / Awareness / Small Area Game
description: Every player controls a ringette while designated taggers chase. Tagged players freeze until a teammate controls a ringette through their legs, forcing constant scanning and puck-control awareness.
coaching_points: Handle the ringette with the head up.
Scan for taggers while identifying frozen teammates.
Use changes of direction to protect possession.
Free teammates only when the passing lane is safe.

title: Toy Finder
category: Small Area Game / Awareness / Puck Collection
description: Three teams compete to collect loose pucks scattered around the station and return them to their team's tire. The round ends when all pucks are collected and the team with the most pucks wins.
coaching_points: Keep the head up while scanning for open pucks.
Use quick starts, stops and direction changes between pickups.
Stay low when collecting and depositing pucks.
Encourage players to find open ice instead of following the crowd.

title: Criss Cross Drop Passing
description: Two players pass into the station, cross through a series of barriers and execute repeated forehand drop passes before the off-puck player drives the net for a final pass.
coaching_points: Make sharp lateral cuts before each drop pass.
Leave the drop pass on the receiver's forehand.
Communicate through every exchange.
Drive the net hard after the final cross.

title: Zone Entry Drives
description: Three forwards rehearse a small-area entry: the puck carrier drives the wall, one player attacks the middle lane and the third stays wide or folds underneath to create a second scoring option.
coaching_points: Drive the middle lane hard to the net.
The third attacker must create time and space rather than crowd the puck.
Read the available passing option before forcing the play.
Vary the entry pattern once the base timing is clean.

title: Last One Out
description: Most players carry pucks while a smaller group of defenders tries to knock them away. A player exits after losing possession, and the last puck carrier remaining wins the round.
coaching_points: Protect the puck with the body and free hand.
Keep the head up to track pressure.
Change speed and direction before defenders arrive.
Defenders should angle rather than chase from behind.

title: 1 vs 1 in a box
description: Two players compete inside a tight bordered area after the coach introduces a puck. The small space creates repeated 50/50 battles, puck-protection decisions and immediate scoring opportunities.
coaching_points: Win body position before reaching for the puck.
Protect possession with hips and shoulders.
Attack the net quickly once separation is created.
Match players by ability so battles stay competitive.

title: Half Ice Six Shooter
description: Three player lines cycle through six quick shooting actions around two nets. Players receive passes, shoot, hunt rebounds and rotate to the next shooting position.
coaching_points: Receive each pass in a shooting-ready position.
Release quickly rather than overhandling.
Stop at the net for rebounds.
Keep the rotation moving so both goalies see a steady shot rhythm.

title: Weave Shots
description: A player weaves through cones while protecting the puck, turns toward the net for a first shot, then loops to the opposite side to receive a coach pass for a second shot.
coaching_points: Use inside edges and keep the puck away from each cone.
Exit the final turn ready to shoot.
Circle out with the head up and present the stick for the coach pass.
Catch and release the second puck quickly.

title: Neutral Zone Three Shot Station
description: A player receives three separate coach passes for three shots, with stops, backward skating and a backward-to-forward transition built between the scoring attempts.
coaching_points: Keep the stick available for each coach pass.
Stop under control before changing direction.
Stay square to the coach while skating backward.
Transition forward around the tire and attack the third shot with speed.

title: Cutting Hands - Partner Pressure
description: Partners work through three puck-protection variations that train players to lead tight turns with the inside leg, cut the hands across the body and keep the puck shielded from pressure.
coaching_points: Lead the turn with the inside leg.
Trust the outside edge of the inside skate.
Keep the stick blade closed through the tight turn.
Use body and hand position to separate the puck from pressure.

title: Forehand Shooting Fundamentals #4
description: Players approach a pad from the off-hand side, keep the puck on the forehand while surrounding the obstacle and arrive on the far side with the puck already in shooting position.
coaching_points: Keep the puck on the forehand around the pad.
Move the puck into shooting position off the back foot.
Keep the head over the puck through the release.
Transfer weight toward the net and stop at the crease.

title: Figure Eight Tire Shots
description: Players skate a figure-eight route around two tires, collect a puck at each side and return to the middle for two quick shots during the same repetition.
coaching_points: Use tight turns around both tires.
Gain control of each puck quickly.
Move the puck to the forehand before shooting.
Shoot with the head up and continue skating through the pattern.

title: Tire Turn Relays - Forwards to Backwards Transition - Station
description: Players skate forward to a tire, transition around it to backward skating and race backward to the goal line. The drill can be run as a technical station or competitive relay.
coaching_points: Flip the hips as the skater reaches the tire.
Push off the outside edge of the inside skate.
Limit the transition to one crossover when possible.
Move immediately into strong backward C-cuts.

title: Tire Turn Relays - Full 360 Control Turns - Quarter Ice
description: Players race straight to a tire, complete a full 360-degree control turn and accelerate back to the goal line, emphasizing edge control and forward-stride power.
coaching_points: Turn the chest and eyes toward the exit.
Trust the outside edge of the inside skate.
Keep the inside skate slightly ahead through the turn.
Accelerate immediately after completing the circle.

title: Iron Cross Passing Drill
description: One player performs an iron-cross skating pattern inside the circle while repeatedly exchanging give-and-go passes with a stationary teammate at the bottom of the circle.
coaching_points: Communicate before every pass.
Keep the stick on the ice as a target.
Use quick stops and explosive starts to move into open space.
Progress to backhand receptions or light pressure when execution is clean.

title: Puck Tag - Stickhandling and Awareness Game
description: Players each handle a puck while two or three taggers try to freeze them. A frozen player forms a triangle with skates and stick and can be released when a teammate stickhandles through that space.
coaching_points: Keep the head up while maintaining puck control.
Use quick changes of direction to escape taggers.
Scan for frozen teammates while protecting the puck.
Keep all players moving and engaged.

title: 3 Cone Skills Series #1
description: Players attack a three-cone setup with the puck, make a single shift at the first cone, then use tight control turns around the remaining cones before repeating the pattern in the opposite direction.
coaching_points: Attack the first cone with speed.
Make the single shift cleanly without overhandling.
Stay low through the control turns.
Accelerate out of each turn while keeping the puck protected.

title: 3 Cone Skills Series #2
description: Players make a single shift at the first cone, enter between the next two cones, then use quick crossovers around the three-cone pattern before repeating from the opposite side.
coaching_points: Keep the puck under control through the first move.
Use quick crossover footwork around the cone pattern.
Keep the head up whenever possible.
Repeat both directions to develop balanced edge control.

title: Half Ice Open Up Shooting
description: Two players leave from the inside hash marks, touch the red line, open their hips toward the wall, call for a pass and receive it while continuing to move before shooting in stride.
coaching_points: Open the hips while keeping momentum.
Call for the puck and present a target.
Keep the feet moving through the catch.
Release the shot in stride.

title: Footwork Shots
description: Two half-ice shooting patterns combine cone footwork with passes from a corner player. One side uses a figure-eight pattern; the other adds forward-to-backward transitions before the shot.
coaching_points: Use sharp footwork around the cones.
Keep the stick available for passes.
Transition smoothly without losing speed.
Shoot immediately after receiving the puck.

title: Dodge Ball - Quarter Ice Station
description: Teams play dodge ball on the ice with tennis balls or foam pucks, repeatedly using passing and shooting motions while skating, reading traffic and avoiding incoming shots.
coaching_points: Keep the head up and scan for incoming balls.
Use controlled shooting and passing mechanics.
Stay mobile and use edges to evade pressure.
Enforce safe stick height throughout the game.

title: Mirror Shoot Out
description: An offensive player shifts laterally between two reference cones while a defender mirrors the movement. The attacker chooses when to call for the puck and then attacks the net on a breakaway.
coaching_points: Change direction with urgency and deception.
Defender mirrors while maintaining a strong stance.
Attacker communicates when ready for the pass.
Transition immediately from lateral movement to attack speed.

title: McGillney Drop, Shoot, Battle
description: Players start from opposite corners, leave their pucks at central obstacles, change direction around the opposite obstacle, pick up the other puck and shoot. They then race to a loose puck for a live battle to the opposite net.
coaching_points: Change direction quickly around the obstacles.
Pick up the exchanged puck cleanly and attack the net.
Stop at the net after the first shot.
Compete immediately for the second puck and recognize offense versus defense.

title: Pass - Pressure - Escape
description: An attacker receives a pass while starting backward, then reads aggressive pressure and uses an escape move and deception to protect the puck, gain the zone and attack the net.
coaching_points: Read which side the pressure is coming from.
Use deception before the escape move.
Protect the puck through the turn.
Accelerate once separation is created.

title: Two Shot Seal and Walk
description: A defense player controls a difficult rim at the blue line, walks laterally to find a shooting lane for the first shot, then transitions around cones and receives another pass for a one-timer.
coaching_points: Handle the rim cleanly with the head up.
Walk the blue line as if searching for a lane.
Transition quickly after the first shot.
Set the feet and stick early for the one-timer.

title: Half Ice Shoot In Stride
description: Players leave from the hash marks, skate toward the red line and opposite passer, call for the puck and receive it while moving, then release the shot in stride before reaching the cone.
coaching_points: Communicate and show a clear stick target.
Keep the feet moving through the reception.
Shoot before the cone without gliding.
Finish at the net for rebounds.

title: Brooksy Utah Mammoth
description: Players race for a loose puck, turn the win into an immediate 2 on 1 with support, then react to a second rimmed puck and continue into a live 2 on 2.
coaching_points: Win body position before the loose puck.
Move the puck to support immediately after possession is won.
Retrieve the rim under pressure with feet moving.
Transition quickly from the first attack into the 2 on 2.

title: Houda Skin
description: A defenseman retrieves a dump while a supporting forward delays the forechecker to create time for the first pass. After the breakout, the two forwards transition back at the defenseman in a 2 on 1.
coaching_points: Scan before retrieval and identify pressure early.
Supporting forward creates time without losing the passing lane.
Make a clean first pass under pressure.
Transition immediately into the 2 on 1 attack.

title: 4Corner puck protection
description: Pairs work from all four corners. On the first whistle they race to a puck and play keepaway inside the circle; on the second whistle the puck carrier attacks the net while the other player defends.
coaching_points: Arrive low and establish inside body position.
Protect the puck on the hip with quick turns.
Accelerate immediately on the second whistle.
Defender takes an efficient angle and protects the middle.

title: 4Check Warmup Progressions
description: A two-part warm-up progression through neutral-zone obstacles. Players first stickhandle through the traffic and shoot, then repeat while using stationary passing options to pass through the obstacles before finishing.
coaching_points: Keep the head up through traffic.
Use controlled puck touches around obstacles.
Deliver crisp passes through sticks and bodies.
Maintain foot speed before finishing with a shot.

title: 2 on 1 Corner Traffic
description: Two forwards and one defender exchange at least four passes around corner obstacles before the forwards attack out of the corner in a live 2 on 1.
coaching_points: Move the puck quickly with purpose.
Maintain spacing around the obstacles.
Do not attack until the required passes are complete.
Explode into the 2 on 1 and read the defender.

title: 4Check Punch Escapes
description: A forward and defender skate up the wall together. The forward uses a hard punch turn to escape controlled pressure, times a pass from the coach, then attacks the net through traffic.
coaching_points: Stay low through the punch turn.
Use hips and shoulders to protect the puck.
Time the escape with the coach's pass.
Attack the net immediately after separation.

title: Stick Battle with Shots
description: The skater approaches an obstacle, executes a stick lift to gain possession, flips the hips to face the net and releases a quick shot through the screen before repeating from the opposite side.
coaching_points: Approach with strong body and stick position.
Lift through the hands with control.
Flip the hips quickly into shooting posture.
Release through traffic without overhandling.

title: Low Rim Pickup with Screens
description: A puck is rimmed around the wall for a retrieval. The player controls it, makes a creative move around the first obstacle, cuts to the net and shoots through a second screen.
coaching_points: Angle the retrieval to maintain puck speed.
Scan before collecting the rim.
Use deception around the first obstacle.
Drive inside and release quickly through the screen.

title: Blue Line Shots with Screens
description: Defensemen walk the blue line while reading traffic and changing their angle to get shots through layered screens to the net.
