coaching_points: Keep the head up while walking the line.
Use lateral footwork to change the lane.
Control the puck close enough for a quick release.
Prioritize getting the puck through traffic.

title: 4Check 1 Zone Passing
description: Two defensemen retrieve a coach dump, execute a D-to-D breakout, carry up ice and work passes through obstacles before finishing the sequence at the net.
coaching_points: Communicate retrieval responsibility early.
Shoulder check before collecting the puck.
Make firm D-to-D passes while moving.
Enter with the head up and find passing lanes through traffic.

title: Blue Line Shot Pass
description: A defenseman receives at the blue line, walks laterally to open a lane and sends a controlled backdoor shot-pass through traffic to a teammate at the far post.
coaching_points: Read the backdoor option before moving the puck.
Use lateral movement and deception to open the lane.
Keep the puck in a quick-release position.
Deliver a firm but redirectable shot-pass.

title: 4Check Moving Shot Blockers
description: A defenseman works the blue line while moving obstacles simulate changing traffic. The player must scan, adjust laterally and release through the safest available shooting lane.
coaching_points: Scan before and during the rep.
Use quick lateral steps to change the lane.
Use deception to shift traffic.
Prioritize getting the puck through over maximum power.

title: O-Zone D to D
description: Defensemen work two offensive-zone patterns designed to maintain control through transitions, move laterally under pressure and create a shot or passing lane from the blue line.
coaching_points: Keep the head up through the transition.
Maintain a strong skating base.
Use deception and quick puck movement.
Choose shots that create rebounds or second chances.

title: 4Check Power Play Options
description: A low player receives from up top for a quick shot, reloads immediately, then receives a second puck and moves it across the zone to a teammate for the next power-play option.
coaching_points: Shoot in stride with a quick release.
Reload immediately after the first shot.
Open the hips on the cross-ice pass.
Lead the target and keep the head up.

title: 4Check 1 Timers
description: Players exchange pucks through traffic and finish with one-timers, emphasizing quick puck movement, shooting through screens and clean preparation for the release.
coaching_points: Use quiet hands and proper weight transfer.
Track the puck while reading the lane.
Pass firmly to the shooting pocket.
Shoot through traffic instead of around it.

title: 4Check Dummy Chaos
description: Multiple players stickhandle inside a faceoff circle while navigating teammates and obstacle dummies, forcing constant awareness and tight-area puck control.
coaching_points: Keep the head up at all times.
Use soft, quick touches in traffic.
Shoulder check and identify open space.
Protect the puck while changing direction.

title: Body contact side wall angling
description: A player takes a controlled angle into sidewall contact, retrieves the loose puck, moves it behind the net, then drives to the crease while the puck goes low-to-high for a shot through traffic.
coaching_points: Take a strong controlled angle into contact.
Keep the head up through the battle.
Move the puck quickly low-to-high.
Establish strong net-front position for screens and tips.

title: Body Contact open ice hit
description: The player works controlled open-ice body contact, immediately recovers possession, advances the puck to a teammate and continues to the net for a screen or tip.
coaching_points: Keep the head up through the middle.
Stay balanced through contact.
Angle through the body rather than reaching.
Recover the puck immediately after contact.

title: Body contact Hip Check
description: The player performs a controlled hip-out around a cone, moves laterally into body contact at the wall, releases from contact, retrieves a loose puck and makes the next pass for a shot.
coaching_points: Stay balanced through the hip-out.
Time the contact under control.
Release cleanly into puck recovery.
Make an accurate pass immediately after contact.

title: Body Contact Low Corner Drive
description: The player drives through light contact in the corner to gain body position and retrieve a puck, moves it to the blue line, then loops open for a return pass and attacks the net.
coaching_points: Stay low and strong through contact.
Keep the feet moving to win position.
Move the puck quickly after retrieval.
Open up for the return pass with speed.

title: Body Contact Low Angle w Shot
description: A player takes a strong corner angle, initiates controlled contact, retrieves the puck and passes high before driving the crease for a screen, tip or rebound on the point shot.
coaching_points: Angle under control before contact.
Stay balanced while retrieving the puck.
Move the puck quickly to the high option.
Drive directly to the net after the pass.

title: Body Contact Puck Protection - Skate Touch
description: Two players begin in body contact. The outside player tries to drive through and reach the puck using only a skate while the inside player protects the puck with body position and stick presence without touching it directly.
coaching_points: Stay low and balanced through contact.
Win inside body position.
Use hips and leverage to shield the puck.
Maintain control rather than reaching or lunging.

title: Body Contact Corner protection - reverse hit
description: A player retrieves a loose puck in the corner, uses a controlled reverse hit against pressure, secures possession and moves the puck to a teammate in the high slot.
coaching_points: Keep the head up before contact.
Stop under control with two feet and leave space from the boards.
Use body position to absorb pressure and secure the puck.
Move the puck quickly after winning possession.

title: Forward-Backward Passing Drill
description: Partners move together while continuously exchanging passes, with one player skating forward and the other backward. At the end of the lane they return with the skating roles reversed.
coaching_points: Pass while both players stay in motion.
Present a clear stick target.
Receive on both forehand and backhand.
Keep the head up and maintain spacing with the partner.

title: Puck Protection With Ringettes
description: Partners battle inside a circle while the offensive player protects a ringette or puck using skating, body position and stick placement against live pressure.
coaching_points: Use the body to shield possession.
Stay low and balanced while changing direction.
Keep possession on the far side from pressure.
Use tight turns and edges instead of reaching.

title: Pass Off Bumper Underhandle With Shot
description: Players bank a puck off a bumper in the slot, collect it in motion and push or pull it around the obstacle in one movement before releasing a quick shot.
coaching_points: Use deception before choosing a side of the bumper.
Underhandle the puck instead of adding extra stickhandles.
Keep the eyes up to read the net.
Release immediately after clearing the obstacle.

title: Brunner Catch And Shoot
description: Players drive toward the net from the blue line, receive a cross-ice pass from the opposite line and catch-and-shoot without breaking stride or adding an extra stickhandle.
coaching_points: Keep the stick on the ice as a target.
Receive the pass in the shooting pocket.
Shoot without breaking stride.
Practice both strong-side and backhand receptions.

title: Wise Drill
description: Forwards and defensemen exchange passes through the neutral zone to create a timed entry, then continue into an offensive-zone sequence that adds net-front presence, a corner puck and a point option.
coaching_points: Time the neutral-zone support to arrive with speed.
Move the puck flat and early through the entry.
Maintain width and layered support.
After the first shot, reload immediately into offensive-zone roles.

title: 4 v 2 Down Low Game
category: 4 vs 2 / Down Low / Small Area Game
description: Two forwards battle two defenders in front while two stationary offensive support players work below the goal line. The offense uses support and quick puck movement to create scoring chances; a progression adds point players.
coaching_points: Create separation without the puck.
Scan before receiving and move the puck quickly.
Defenders protect the middle and maintain body position.
Use the low support players to change the point of attack.

title: 1 V 1 to 2 V 2 Down Low
description: Players compete in a very tight area below the goal line between two opposing nets. The game begins 1 on 1 and progresses to 2 on 2 to emphasize wall work, protection and quick scoring decisions.
coaching_points: Win pucks along the wall with strong body position.
Protect possession using the wall when useful.
Use deception and self-passes in tight space.
Release shots quickly when a scoring window opens.

title: Two Pucks 2 v 2 Circle Battle
description: Two teams of two enter a faceoff circle with two live pucks and may score on either of two opposing nets. Both pucks remain active until they are scored or leave the circle.
coaching_points: Protect the puck in tight traffic.
Communicate constantly with the teammate.
Use quick touches and quick releases.
Track both pucks and both nets before committing.

title: Ring of Fire
description: A 3 on 3 game is played around a faceoff circle with one player from each team inside and the remaining teammates outside. Teams use quick support, passing and shooting to attack either end.
coaching_points: Move the puck quickly.
Get open off the puck and communicate.
Present the stick as a clear passing target.
Defenders keep sticks in lanes and pressure without losing shape.

title: Honey Hole
description: A defenseman receives a sequence of passes at the blue line and works three releases around a net used as traffic: shoot around it, fake behind it, then jump laterally into open ice for the final shot.
coaching_points: Communicate and present the stick for each pass.
Move laterally to clear traffic before shooting.
Pull the puck toward the toes to create a new lane.
Receive and release quickly when jumping into the open lane.

title: Quarter Ice Puck Race #2
description: Two players start between staggered tires, skate a complete figure-eight using tight control turns, then accelerate with crossovers toward the middle and race for a loose puck.
coaching_points: Stay low through each control turn.
Keep the feet moving through the figure-eight.
Explode out of the final turn with crossovers.
Compete through the puck and finish the play.

title: Quarter Ice Puck Race #1
description: Two players skate forward through two tight control turns around staggered tires and then accelerate into the middle to race for a puck played by the coach.
coaching_points: Use tight turns without losing speed.
Accelerate immediately out of each turn.
Keep the head up when entering the race.
Compete through the loose puck and attack the net.

title: Neutral Zone Puck Races #7
description: Players begin skating backward through a tire pattern, transition forward and backward through the course, then turn forward and race for a puck played into open space by the coach.
coaching_points: Start backward with strong first pushes.
Make clean backward-to-forward transitions.
Keep balance and speed around each tire.
Accelerate hard into the final puck race.

title: D-Spinorama
description: Partners move toward each other with one player skating forward and the other backward. They exchange the puck near center, then the receiver uses a spin or escape move before reversing the roles.
coaching_points: Use eyes and stick position to sell the fake.
Practice escape moves to both sides.
Transition backward smoothly after making the pass.
Keep the pass flat and on the receiver's stick.

title: Clean Your Room
description: Two teams stay on opposite halves of a small area and try to clear every puck from their own side by passing pucks along the ice into the opponent's half.
coaching_points: Use proper passing technique instead of lifting pucks.
Retrieve and move pucks continuously.
Scan for open lanes before passing.
Read opponents and look to intercept incoming pucks.

title: Tire Moves
description: Players attack two tires or cones with the puck, make a single shift to the outside at the first obstacle and a single shift to the inside at the second, then finish with a shot on the small net.
coaching_points: Approach each obstacle with speed.
Move the puck outside the defender's reach.
Practice the move to both forehand and backhand sides.
Accelerate out of the second move and shoot quickly.

title: D-Zone D to D
description: A defenseman retrieves a coach dump, shoulder checks and turns up ice before moving the puck D-to-D behind the net. The supporting defenseman receives in motion, advances and can regroup again before adding center support.
coaching_points: Shoulder check before retrieval.
Use deception when turning up ice.
Support below the puck for the D-to-D pass.
Receive with the head up and feet moving.

title: O-Zone Sticklift Regroup
description: A forward rims the puck to the opposite wall. The defenseman pinches, uses a stick lift to gain control, passes to a forward coming through the middle, then the players switch in the high slot and attack a central obstacle.
coaching_points: Arrive at the wall under control.
Use the stick lift to establish clean possession.
Move the puck quickly to middle support.
Time the high-slot switch with speed.

title: Body Contact Boardside Puck Protection
category: Puck Protection / Wall Play / Defensive Zone
description: Players race to a loose puck along the wall while controlled pressure arrives with a dummy. The player uses body position to protect the puck, moves it to a teammate, then circles into space for a return pass.
coaching_points: Get body position between pressure and the puck.
Stay low and balanced through contact.
Secure possession before moving the puck.
Release from the wall and become an immediate passing option.

title: Dodge Ball with Tennis Balls - Third Ice Station
description: Two teams begin on opposite sides of a third-ice station with tennis balls placed through the middle. On the whistle they collect balls and use controlled shooting motions to try to hit opponents.
coaching_points: Use controlled shooting mechanics.
Keep shots low and safe.
Keep the head up while retrieving balls.
Stay active and aware of traffic.

title: 1 vs 1 Multiple games - Third Ice Station
description: Several 1-on-1 games run simultaneously inside the same third-ice area, forcing players to compete for their own puck while constantly reading traffic from the other battles.
coaching_points: Compete hard for possession.
Keep the head up in traffic.
Use body position to protect the puck.
Adjust the number of simultaneous games to the group's age and pace.

title: 3 vs 3 Cross Ice
description: Three players per side play cross-ice with the nets moved toward the faceoff dots, creating additional space behind both nets and encouraging quick puck touches, support and attacks from below the goal line.
coaching_points: Keep shifts short and competitive.
Support the puck on both sides.
Use the space behind the nets.
Move the puck quickly to create scoring chances.

title: Explosive Skating with Tires
description: Forwards accelerate from a standstill, optionally pushing tires for resistance through their first strides, while defensemen explode backward, build speed with C-cuts and pivot to race the forwards to the red line.
coaching_points: Explode through the first three to five strides.
Defensemen use a powerful cross-under into backward C-cuts.
Pivot at speed without crossing the feet inefficiently.
Forwards continue accelerating after releasing the tire.

title: Royal Puck Protection Drill
description: A puck carrier works a figure-eight pattern around two stationary pressure players, using body position and moving feet to protect the puck before attacking out of the turn for a quick shot.
coaching_points: Keep the feet moving while protecting the puck.
Use the body and hips to shield possession.
Attack out of the final turn with speed.
Release quickly and stop at the crease.

title: Umbrella Roll Power Play Drill
description: A forward moves up the wall and pivots backward to receive a pass while the defense shifts laterally along the blue line. The puck goes forward-to-defense and back into the seam for a shot.
coaching_points: Time the pivot so the forward receives while moving.
Defense stays available along the blue line.
Move the puck quickly through the exchange.
Explode into the seam after the return pass.

title: Shooting Warm-Up Progression
description: A full-ice two-part warm-up progression. Players cross and exchange one-touch passes through center before finishing with quick-release shots, then progress to outside-lane entries with seam and backdoor options.
coaching_points: Communicate before each pass.
Keep sticks on the ice as clear targets.
Maintain spacing through the neutral zone.
Use quick, crisp passes and quick-release shots.

title: 4Check body contact corner race
description: A forward angles a dummy away from a loose corner puck, wins body position, retrieves the puck and moves it to support before the sequence finishes with a point shot.
coaching_points: Take a smart angle before initiating contact.
Separate the opponent from the puck, not just the body.
Recover the loose puck immediately.
Move the puck quickly to support and get to the net.

title: Body Contact Angle with Sticklift
description: A player takes a controlled angle to force a puck carrier up the wall, initiates body contact with stick-on-stick detail, separates the player from the puck and immediately attacks the net.
coaching_points: Get in front of the puck carrier before contact.
Use stick-on-stick and body-on-body together.
Keep the head up through contact.
Attack the net immediately after creating the turnover.

title: 4Check Skills Pinch and Attack
description: A defenseman pinches down the wall, lifts through a dummy's stick to win a puck, escapes boardside pressure and drives the net. The progression adds a rim and a slot one-timer.
coaching_points: Seal the wall with strong body and stick position.
Win the puck before making the escape move.
Accelerate immediately after separation.
On the progression, time the slot support for the one-timer.

title: Circle Angling Drill
description: Two players work across a divided faceoff circle. The puck carrier tries to reach the opposite half while the defender uses a controlled angle to steer the carrier away from the middle.
coaching_points: Defender approaches on an angle instead of skating directly at the puck.
Protect the middle and steer toward the boundary.
Use stick-on-stick and body-on-body at the right moment.
Puck carrier keeps feet moving and protects possession.

title: 3 v 3 Change on The Fly
description: A 3-on-3 game rotates continuously from offense to defense to out. The defending team must win possession and make a breakout pass before fresh teammates enter on offense.
coaching_points: Transition immediately when possession changes.
Defenders protect the middle and communicate.
Offense attacks quickly before the defense gets set.
Change cleanly so the game keeps its pace.

title: Redwing Backcheck
description: Two forwards attack a defenseman while a trailing player backchecks through the play. The drill runs from both sides to create repeated 2-on-1 reads under back pressure.
coaching_points: Attack with pace before the backchecker can recover.
Puck carrier reads the defenseman's stick and gap.
Backchecker takes away the most dangerous support option.
Defenseman delays the rush and protects the middle.

title: Hot Wall Corner
description: A live 1-on-1 is played in the corner with teammates stationed outside the area as support. An outside support player must one-time the pass, or the progression requires an extra support pass before the one-timer.
coaching_points: Compete for inside body position in the corner.
Use support instead of forcing low-percentage plays.
Outside players prepare the stick early for the one-timer.
Move immediately after passing to create a new lane.

title: Laker 3 Puck
category: Net Front / Battle / Small Area Game
description: An offensive player behind the net feeds three separate pucks to teammates around the crease. Defenders must clear possession below the goal line or find a coach on the dots before the next puck starts.
coaching_points: Offense battles for inside net-front position.
Defenders box out before hunting the puck.
React immediately when the coach starts the next puck.
Keep sticks available for tips, rebounds and outlet passes.

title: Shadow Defensive Skating, No Crossover Drill
description: Two players mirror each other through a figure-eight pattern around cones while always facing one another. Direction changes are made with backward inside-edge transitions instead of crossovers.
coaching_points: Stay square to the opposing player.
Load the inside edge before changing direction.
Avoid crossing the feet during the defensive transition.
Keep the stick active once the footwork is comfortable.

title: Introduction to Angling
description: A puck is placed into the corner with one player given a head start on retrieval. The trailing player practices taking an angle, steering the puck carrier up the wall and separating body from puck.
coaching_points: Recognize when the puck cannot be beaten directly and take an angle.
Approach through the hands instead of chasing the puck.
Keep body and stick connected through contact.
Puck carrier protects the puck and stays balanced along the wall.

title: USA Step Forward Drill
description: A player on a faceoff dot reacts to controlled contact arriving from either side, stepping forward into the hit rather than waiting stationary. The progression adds sticks and puck control.
coaching_points: Stay light on the skates and react without looking at the coach's signal.
Step forward into contact instead of absorbing it flat-footed.
Lead with the shoulder and keep the head and chest up.
Progress gradually from no stick to stick and puck.

title: Side by Side Checking
description: Partners stand side by side and practice controlled body-contact mechanics from a stationary position before progressing to sticks and then puck control.
coaching_points: Use a wide, balanced base and stay low.
Load the opposite leg and transfer weight through contact.
Lead with the shoulder cap while keeping the head protected.
Progress only as players demonstrate balance and control.

title: Playing in Contact Skills (Part 1, 2, 3)
description: A three-part progression teaches position before possession: cutting off an opponent in a puck race, separating an opponent from the puck defensively, and using contact to protect possession offensively.
coaching_points: Win body position before reaching for the puck.
Cut through the opponent's hands with controlled body position.
Defensively separate the player from the puck.
Offensively keep the defender behind the puck carrier.

title: Puck Protection Weight Shift Moving
category: Puck Protection / Puck Control / Warm Up
description: Players skate slowly down the ice while alternating weight shifts, keeping the puck and stick on one side while leaning the body away to build a strong puck-protection posture.
coaching_points: Keep both skates engaged instead of dragging the outside foot.
Shift roughly 60/40 rather than balancing on one leg.
Lean the body away from the puck side.
Keep the drill controlled until posture is consistent.

title: Isolated Bump & Go
description: Two players skate up the wall together. The offensive player uses controlled body contact to bump the defender, turns back toward the wall, creates separation and attacks the net.
coaching_points: Use controlled contact to create separation.
Keep the feet moving through the bump.
Turn back toward the wall with the puck protected.
Explode away from pressure and attack the net.

title: Puck Protection Weight Shifting (Standing Still)
description: Players rehearse the puck-protection base position while stationary, shifting body weight away from the puck side before repeating the same movement with a puck.
coaching_points: Shift weight away from the puck side.
Keep the inside knee bent and the puck protected behind the leg.
Stay balanced through the lower body instead of dropping the shoulder.
Practice both forehand and backhand protection positions.

title: 2 On 2 Jets
description: The drill begins with a 2 on 2 rush, then immediately becomes a 2 on 2 net-front battle with additional offensive support players around the perimeter moving pucks quickly into scoring areas.
coaching_points: Use timing and tempo on the rush to create separation.
Forwards establish body position and free sticks at the net.
Defenders protect the middle and keep sticks in lanes.
Perimeter players move pucks and shots quickly.

title: Center Circle Tire Skating - Cross-Overs / Transitions
description: Two players work around four tires positioned at center ice, using crossovers plus forward-to-backward and backward-to-forward transitions before accelerating out of the pattern.
coaching_points: Use controlled crossovers around the circle.
Open the hips cleanly into transitions.
Make the backward-to-forward transition without extra crossovers.
Increase speed as footwork improves.

title: Offensive Advantage 3 vs 3
description: A 3 on 3 small-area game split by a center line. All three attackers may enter the offensive half while only two defenders may enter their defensive half, creating a constant 3 on 2 attacking advantage.
coaching_points: Communicate who stays high when possession changes.
Attackers recognize and use the extra player quickly.
Defenders protect the middle and communicate switches.
Anticipate turnovers so the high player is ready to transition.

title: Around The Circle Progression Drill
description: Players start in opposite defensive-zone circles, skate backward around the circle, pivot forward, receive a pass from the next player in line, accelerate through neutral ice, exchange a give-and-go with the coach, then attack the far end for a shot.
coaching_points: Accelerate out of the backward-to-forward pivot.
Receive passes in stride and keep the puck moving.
Use full-speed crossovers through neutral ice.
Finish the rep by attacking the shooting lane with pace.

title: Overload Power Play Drill
description: A half-ice power-play shooting drill built around an overload setup. A forward moves the puck to the point and follows up the wall while the defenseman walks the blue line. The puck returns to the wall for a seam attack and shot; the next repetition adds a low give-and-go before the seam shot.
coaching_points: Defenseman walks the puck inside before returning it to the wall.
Forward receives in a shooting position and attacks the seam with feet moving.
Follow the shot to the crease.
On the second action, use the low give-and-go to create the seam shot.

title: Westminster 3 on 3
category: 3 on 3 / Small Area Game / Half Ice
description: A 3 on 3 game where teams play until a goal. The scoring team stays on the ice, while the losing team is replaced by the players lined up as bumpers at the blue line. The incoming team is the only team allowed to use the bumpers, creating an immediate possession advantage.
coaching_points: Use the available bumpers to create an advantage.
Move the puck quickly and keep the feet moving.
Recognize the transition immediately after a goal.
Support the puck and attack open space.

title: 1 vs 1 with Mini Nets - Multiple Games
category: 1 on 1 / Small Area Game / Mini Nets
description: A mini-net 1 on 1 game that can run in several areas at the same time without goalies. Multiple simultaneous games force players to scan, keep their heads up and compete while navigating traffic around them.
coaching_points: Compete hard for possession.
Keep the head up and scan for surrounding traffic.
Protect the puck in tight space.
Let players solve the 1 on 1 situation rather than over-coaching the rep.

title: Harley Overspeed Progression Drill
description: Players begin in opposite neutral-zone lines, skate around the center circle without a puck, receive a diagonal pass, return the puck to their original line, open up for a return pass, then accelerate down ice for a shot.
coaching_points: Keep the feet moving at overspeed through the circle.
Receive the first pass in stride.
Open the hips and present a target for the return pass.
Accelerate out of the turn and finish with a shot.

title: Low Traffic Shots
description: A shooting drill with multiple traffic-based variations. Players work through each sequence with the puck, create a shooting lane through traffic, finish the shot, and continue to the net for rebounds or tips.
coaching_points: Stay balanced and keep the feet moving through each repetition.
Handle the puck quickly and move directly from reception into the release.
Scan through traffic for open shooting lanes and rebound opportunities.
Follow every shot to the net and be ready for a second chance.
Vary the release to make the reps more game-like.

title: Defenseman Blue Line Walk
description: Defensemen work laterally along the blue line through two progressions, keeping the puck under control while changing the shooting or passing lane through traffic before finishing the play.
coaching_points: Keep a low, balanced stance while moving laterally.
Use quick feet and compact crossovers to stay inside the blue line.
Keep the head up and read the lane through traffic.
Use puck-control deception to create space.
Finish with a quick shot or a pass through the available lane.

title: 4Check Body Contact Angling #1
description: Players start on the goal line without a puck, take an angle into controlled body contact on a dummy, recover a loose puck, make a pass to the blue line, loop around the faceoff-dot cone, receive the return pass, and attack the net for a shot.
coaching_points: Get low before initiating body contact.
Win the board-side lane and wall off the contact target.
Keep the stick on the ice and the hands controlled.
Transition quickly from contact into puck recovery and passing.
Accelerate through the return pass and finish the rep with a shot.

title: Sabre D Shooting Drill
description: A half-ice defense shooting progression. The defenseman receives a pass near the wall, moves backward toward the blue line under pressure, changes the shooting lane around an obstacle, and gets a shot through traffic.
coaching_points: Receive the puck with the head up and establish the blue line.
Use lateral footwork and deception to change the shooting lane.
Keep the puck inside the offensive zone while moving across the line.
Get the shot through traffic quickly.
Attack available space instead of forcing the first lane.

title: Sabre 2v2 Support Game
category: 2 on 2 / Small Area Game / Puck Support
description: A half-ice 2 on 2 game with an outside support player. After gaining possession, the team must use its support option before attacking, forcing quick recognition, puck support and transition.
coaching_points: Win possession before looking to attack.
Find the support player quickly after a turnover.
Support can move laterally to improve the passing lane.
Attack immediately after the support pass.
Defenders communicate and protect the middle.

title: Oswego Passing Station
description: A neutral-zone passing station in which a puck carrier moves around the outside of the setup while exchanging passes with players in the opposite lines. The rep develops multiple receptions and passes while moving.
coaching_points: Make firm tape-to-tape passes.
Keep eyes up and stay connected to the puck.
Present a clear target before each reception.
Use verbal and non-verbal communication.
Run the station in both directions.

title: Castleton Puck Protection Drill
category: Puck Protection / Skill Development / Neutral Zone
description: Players use a give-and-go before attacking a coach as passive pressure, then escape around an obstacle with a mohawk-style turn while keeping the puck protected and moving it to the opposite line.
coaching_points: Use deception before entering the pressure area.
Keep the puck away from the defender's reach.
Stay low and balanced through the escape turn.
Use the mohawk to maintain vision and puck protection.
Finish with an accurate pass to the next player.

title: Sabre Split Ice Attack Drill
description: A full-ice split-ice attack drill run from both sides. Players exchange passes, attack through neutral ice in a 2 on 1, then continue to the net-front area while the next action develops from the blue line.
coaching_points: Move the puck cleanly before entering the rush.
Attack the 2 on 1 with speed and deception.
Use width to force the defender to make a decision.
Finish at the net and stay available for rebounds or screens.
Keep both halves organized and moving at game pace.

title: Trinity Quick Escape Drill
description: A quick-escape read in which the puck carrier receives a pass, feels pressure from one side, turns away from that pressure around an obstacle and attacks the net.
coaching_points: Read which side the pressure is coming from.
Escape away from pressure instead of skating into it.
Protect the puck through the turn.
Accelerate immediately out of the escape.
Finish the rep with a quick shot.

title: Kick Out Warm Up
category: Zone Entry / Passing / Transition / Warm Up
description: A full-ice warm-up with passing, curling support and a kick-out pass to the wall before the receiving player drives toward the middle for a shot. Both players finish at the net.
coaching_points: Pass and receive while moving.
Time the curl so the middle lane stays available.
Lead the kick-out pass to the wall.
Drive the middle with speed after receiving the puck.
Both players follow the play to the net.

title: 3/4 Ice Skating Race
description: Two players race through an obstacle course toward a loose puck. The first player to the puck becomes the attacker while the second player transitions into back pressure, turning the race into a competitive scoring situation.
coaching_points: Explode through the skating course.
Stay under control around the obstacles.
Compete through the loose-puck race.
Winner attacks immediately after gaining possession.
Trailing player transitions into hard back pressure.

title: DSS Turn Pull
description: The puck carrier makes a tight turn around an obstacle, pulls the puck against the direction of momentum to create separation, then cuts the hands and shoots in stride. A mohawk turn can be added as a progression.
coaching_points: Stay tight to the turning obstacle.
Pull the puck away from the pressure side.
Separate the hands from the body when changing the puck angle.
Shoot without breaking stride.
Add the mohawk progression only after the base movement is clean.

title: Stop Drop Roll
description: The drill begins as a controlled breakout. At the coach's whistle, both groups stop and reset their body position, then a new puck is sent into a zone so one group must break out while the other immediately becomes the forecheck.
coaching_points: Execute the initial breakout with proper spacing.
React immediately to the transition whistle.
Identify offense and defense roles quickly on the second puck.
Breakout players communicate and support underneath the puck.
Forecheckers close space with speed and structure.

title: Quarter Ice Obstacle Course #2
description: An advanced quarter-ice obstacle course for younger players that combines forward-to-backward and backward-to-forward transitions, two-foot jumps, crossovers, step-overs and forward stride in a competitive relay format.
coaching_points: Give players a few controlled practice runs before racing.
Stay balanced through every transition and obstacle.
Use clean crossovers around the four-cone square.
Keep spacing between racers so each player can complete the course safely at speed.

title: D-Zone 1 on 1 Give and GO - #2
description: A defensive-zone 1 on 1 that starts with a forward carrying the puck behind the net. The defender engages near the post, stays defensive-side, angles the attacker toward the wall and must remain connected if the forward uses the coach for a low give-and-go.
coaching_points: Defender stays on the defensive side of the attacker.
Angle the puck carrier up the wall and close space.
Forward protects the puck and can use the low give-and-go option.
Defender tracks the forward after the puck is moved instead of chasing the puck.

title: Neutral Zone Six Shooter
description: A neutral-zone station that allows six players to work at once. Three lanes use different skating routes around cones before each player attacks a net for a shot.
coaching_points: Keep the head up through the control turns.
Maintain puck control around each cone.
Stay in the assigned lane to avoid traffic.
Accelerate out of the turn and finish with a shot.

title: Two Tire Shooting Warm Up
description: Two players leave opposite corner lines on each whistle. The puck carrier skates up the wall, exchanges a pass with a coach through the tire area, transitions backward, receives the return pass and attacks for a wide-angle shot while the second player hunts the rebound.
coaching_points: Make the neutral-zone exchange while moving.
Transition backward under control and call for the return pass.
Attack the zone inside-out with pace.
Second player gets to the high slot and hunts the rebound.

title: Four Corner Shooting Warm Up #1
description: A four-line shooting warm-up built for high player volume or half-ice sessions. Four players attack in sequence, with the first two carrying around the top of the circles and the next two using blue-line transition footwork before shooting.
coaching_points: Move the feet through the shot from the corner lines.
Control the puck through the transition at the blue line.
Keep the head up when re-entering the zone.
Hit the net and keep waiting lines clear of missed shots.

title: Murphy's Down Low Drill
description: A down-low retrieval drill. A coach rims a puck along the wall, the forward retrieves and protects it, quickly finds a teammate in the slot for a shot, then drives the net for a rebound before repeating the action from the opposite side.
coaching_points: Retrieve the rim with the body between the puck and pressure.
Get the puck into passing position immediately.
Pass quickly to the available stick in the slot.
After passing, move to the net instead of watching the shot.

title: Spartan Warm up Shooting Drill
description: A half-ice shooting warm-up built around a shot, net drive and quick one-touch passing exchange. The shooter follows the first shot, moves to the corner, exchanges passes with the opposite line and then receives a return pass for the next shot.
coaching_points: Use quick one-touch passes.
Explode off the wall after the exchange.
Receive and release the shot quickly.
Hit the net and stop at the crease for rebounds.

title: Winnipeg Shooting Warm Up
description: A high-repetition half-ice shooting warm-up with three progressions: stop and open to receive a pass, carry into a tight control turn, and transition backward to receive before turning forward for the shot.
coaching_points: Wait until the previous player has released the shot.
Execute each footwork pattern with control.
Receive passes with the head up.
Accelerate out of the transition and finish the shot.

title: Flames O-Zone Give and Gos
description: An offensive-zone give-and-go drill. The player retrieves a rimmed puck, controls it on the wall, moves it to a passer below the goal line and drives the net for the return pass, then repeats from the opposite corner.
coaching_points: Move the feet all the way to the loose puck.
Use the skates to help secure difficult wall rims.
Make firm passes from below the goal line.
Play fast and attack the net immediately after moving the puck.

title: Half Ice Three Lane Control Turn Shooting
description: Three players leave a corner line with pucks and use three separate routes to the blue line. Each performs a control turn and returns through a different shooting lane, then the opposite corner sends the next group.
coaching_points: Keep all three players in their designated lanes.
Maintain puck control through the turn.
Keep the head up as players return toward the net.
Alternate corners after the three shots.

title: Wisconsin Shooting Drill - Part II
description: A three-look shooting progression. The forward attacks off the wall for the first shot, the defense follows with a point shot while the forward hunts the rebound, then the forward completes a low give-and-go and attacks across the top of the crease for the final shot.
coaching_points: Create three distinct shot angles in the sequence.
Forward hunts the rebound on the point shot.
Make the low give-and-go quickly.
Finish the final attack across the top of the crease.

title: Wisconsin Shooting Drill
description: A two-shot warm-up for forwards, defense and goalies. A forward passes to the point, gets the puck back off the wall and attacks the slot for the first shot. The defense then receives a second puck, walks the blue line and shoots while the forward screens and looks for a rebound.
coaching_points: Forward explodes off the wall into the slot after receiving the return pass.
Defense moves the feet while carrying toward the middle.
Forward gets to the net-front area for screens, tips and rebounds.
Keep the drill flowing from alternating corners.

title: High Horse Defensive Skills
description: A half-ice defense skill progression combining transition passing, outlet passes, backward skating and getting off the wall into the middle for a shot. The defense receives multiple passes while changing skating direction around cones.
coaching_points: Receive passes in transition and maintain puck control.
Make clean outlet passes before transitioning backward.
Skate backward with speed while staying balanced.
Open the hips cleanly and get off the wall before shooting.

title: Soft Chip Overlap Possession Hockey Drill
description: A possession entry drill built around a soft chip into space and an overlap. Two players exchange passes in neutral ice, chip the puck into the offensive zone, recover it with speed, overlap below the puck and create a quick scoring chance.
coaching_points: Place the chip softly enough to be recovered around the hash marks.
Recover the puck at full speed and use a tight control turn.
Time the overlap so the second attacker arrives with speed.
Move the puck into scoring space and support the return pass.

title: Offensive Blue Line Drill
description: An offensive-zone defense drill. A forward passes to the point and goes to the net while the defense walks the blue line for a low shot. The sequence then continues with a wall retrieval, drop pass and overlap to create a second scoring chance.
coaching_points: Defense moves the feet and keeps the head up while walking the blue line.
Shoot low through the screen for tips and rebounds.
Forward establishes a strong net-front screen.
Execute the wall drop and overlap with pace.

title: Swiss 3 Shot Transition
description: A three-shot sequence emphasizing defense skills. The defense receives at the point and shoots through a screen, retrieves a loose puck in transition and hits a forward swinging through neutral ice, then receives another puck from the coach for the third shot.
coaching_points: Defense gets off the wall before the point shot.
Forward screens and looks for a redirection.
Surround the retrieval and get the head up quickly.
Time the forward swing so the outlet is available with speed.

title: Protect IT!
description: Two offensive players each protect a puck inside a faceoff circle while a defender tries to knock the pucks outside. After the timed battle, any player still possessing a puck can attack the net for a shot.
coaching_points: Use the body to shield the puck from pressure.
Keep the feet moving in tight space.
Scan for the defender instead of staring at the puck.
Transition immediately from protection to attack on the whistle.

title: 4 Timer Shooting Drill
description: A four-shot slot progression emphasizing quick releases while moving. The shooter attacks through four cone locations, repeatedly staying available to the passer for one-timers or catch-and-release shots while changing skating direction.
coaching_points: Keep the feet moving through every shot.
Stay facing the passer while moving around the cones.
Use a one-timer when possible or a very quick catch-and-release.
Recover immediately after each shot and become available again.

title: Criss Cross Overspeed
description: An overspeed skating pattern run from both corners. Players sprint through a criss-cross route around the circles and neutral-zone dot, pick up a puck near the blue line and attack the net for a shot without slowing their feet.
coaching_points: Move the feet as fast as possible through the entire route.
Use hard crossovers through each turn.
Pick up the puck in stride.
Shoot from the top of the circles while the feet are still moving.

title: Austrian Two Shot Drill
description: A two-shot offensive-zone sequence. The puck moves from the half wall to the blue line and across to the opposite wall for a quick shot, followed by a second point shot with the first shooter remaining at the net for a tip or screen.
coaching_points: Move the puck quickly through the three-player passing sequence.
Shooter explodes off the wall into scoring space.
Follow the first shot to the net.
Use the net-front player as a screen or tip option on the second shot.

title: PK Conditioning
description: A half-ice conditioning drill using six lines at different depths. Players sprint inside-out to assigned wall locations, stop and recover to their starting point, with each line activating in sequence to simulate short penalty-kill effort patterns.
coaching_points: Attack each wall location inside-out.
Stop under control and accelerate immediately back.
Keep each repetition short and explosive.
Maintain work quality across all three repetitions before rotating.

title: Neutral Zone Transition with High Roll
description: A two-player neutral-zone transition drill that emphasizes puck support, passing angles and a high-roll offensive-zone action. The defense and forward exchange passes through neutral ice, attack for a shot, then reconnect on a wall drop and return pass for a second chance.
coaching_points: Support the puck with a useful passing angle in neutral ice.
Exchange passes while both players keep their feet moving.
Forward attacks the blue line with speed for the first shot.
Time the wall drop and high roll so both players finish at the net.

title: Turns and Stops Station
description: A shared-ice station using two mirrored skating routes. One side works power turns around four obstacles while the other works stops and starts; both finish by receiving a pass from the coach for a shot.
coaching_points: Use controlled power turns without drifting wide.
Come to complete stops on the stop-and-start side.
Accelerate out of every change of direction.
Finish by presenting a target and shooting in stride.

title: Quick Shot, Quick Stuff
description: A forward skill drill combining transition passing, a quick give-and-go shot and a second attack from behind the net. The player transitions to receive a pass, moves it to a designated passer for a quick return shot, then retrieves a puck behind the goal line and attacks the crease.
coaching_points: Transition while facing the puck and present a target.
Move the puck quickly to the designated passer.
Release the first shot immediately off the return pass.
Attack the net decisively after retrieving the second puck.

title: Force Up Wall 1 on 1
description: A defensive 1 on 1 beginning below the goal line. The forward carries behind the net and tries to turn the corner for a scoring chance while the defender uses stick position, body angle and inside leverage to force the attacker outside and up the wall.
coaching_points: Defender protects the inside lane first.
Use the stick and skating angle to steer the attacker away from the net.
Stay between the puck carrier and the scoring area.
Forward attacks the far post with speed and protects the puck.

title: 4 Stations #1
description: A four-station practice layout for younger players. The stations combine a scoring relay, continuous passing with backward skating, a tight-area 2 on 2 battle game and a 3 on 3 transition game that requires using the coach before attacking.
coaching_points: Keep station rules simple and rotations short.
Demand good skating posture in the relay and passing station.
Encourage puck battles and creativity in the 2 on 2 station.
In the 3 on 3 game, transition through the coach before attacking.

title: Continuous Reverses
description: A continuous defense drill for practicing reverse breakouts. A defenseman moves the puck to a wall passer, transitions back below the dots to receive it again, carries behind the net and reverses the puck to the next defenseman, who repeats the sequence.
coaching_points: Stay inside the dots while transitioning back for the puck.
Receive the return pass under control.
Communicate the reverse early and clearly.
Pick up the reverse with speed and continue the pattern.

title: Transition Give & Go Below Goal Line
description: A quick give-and-go attack from the wall into an area below the goal line. The forward takes hard strides, transitions backward to receive and return a pass, then pivots forward and curls toward the net to receive the puck near the goal line for a scoring play.
coaching_points: Take hard strides before the transition.
Receive and return the puck quickly.
Explode forward after the give-and-go.
Make one quick move when attacking from below the goal line.

title: Transition Give and Go from Corner
description: A quick passing and footwork drill from the corner. The forward takes three hard strides, transitions backward to receive a pass, immediately gives it back, then explodes into the slot for the return pass and shot.
coaching_points: Face the passer during the backward transition.
Limit the exchange to one touch or one stickhandle.
Explode into the slot after moving the puck.
Receive the return pass in a shooting position.

title: Breakout Weave #1
description: A breakout timing drill that develops into a full-ice 3 on 0 weave. The defense begins with a breakout pass, stays inside the dots as a support option, receives the puck back and finds the second forward before the three players continue up ice in a weave.
coaching_points: Breakout timing is more important than racing up ice.
Defense remains available underneath the puck.
Use horizontal support passes instead of forcing vertical passes.
Carry the spacing and timing into the 3 on 0 weave.

title: The Transition Wheel
description: A continuous defense transition wheel for four to six players. Pairs receive passes while skating backward, support each other across the middle, transition forward to move the puck to a wall option, then reset into backward skating as the sequence moves to the next pair.
coaching_points: Receive passes while skating backward with control.
Create a support angle underneath the puck.
Transition forward without losing puck or body position.
Reset quickly into backward skating when the puck changes sides.

title: Break Out Timing #1
description: A breakout timing drill focused on creating a clean first-pass option. The defense retrieves the puck from behind the net and passes to a forward timing a swing through the slot. After receiving the breakout pass, the forward attacks through neutral ice while the defense follows to support the next pass.
coaching_points: Forwards must time the swing so the defense has a flat passing lane.
Do not get ahead of the puck and force a difficult vertical pass.
Defense retrieves with feet moving and presents the puck up ice.
Continue supporting the play after the first breakout pass.

title: Break Out Timing #2
description: A two-forward breakout timing drill. The forwards time their release to receive flat passes from the defense, continue the rush, then remain around the net while the defense gets a point shot through for a screen, tip or rebound.
coaching_points: Centers and wings stay underneath the puck until the pass is available.
Receive flat passes rather than getting too far ahead of the play.
Defense sets the pace of the breakout.
Finish with net-front presence on the point shot.

title: Break Out Timing #4
description: A breakout timing progression using two defensemen and two forwards. The defense moves the puck off the boards to a partner, then finds either the center or winger while both forwards time their swings. The defense finishes the rep with a D-to-D pass and a low shot from the blue line.
coaching_points: Handle the board pass quickly.
Centers and wings time their routes to stay available for flat passes.
Defense supports the puck after the breakout pass.
Finish with a hard low shot on net.

title: Three Lane Shooting
description: A shooting warm-up run from four lines at the blue line. Shooters alternate between the far outside lane, middle lane and near outside lane so the goalie sees shots from three different angles with enough spacing to reset between attempts.
coaching_points: Keep enough spacing between shots for the goalie to get set.
Shoot from the assigned lane.
Use all three shooting lanes.
Keep the warm-up flowing without stacking shots.

title: Perpetual Forecheck
description: A continuous forecheck and breakout drill. Five defenders begin in defensive-zone formation, three attackers forecheck a coach dump-in, and the defending group works to break the puck out. The groups rotate so the drill continues into the opposite end.
coaching_points: Forecheck with a defined team structure.
Break out under pressure.
Communicate defensive-zone responsibilities.
Transition immediately when the puck exits the zone.

title: Swoop Warm Up
description: A half-ice warm-up with two corner lines. Both players skate into the neutral-zone puck area, collect a puck and use different looping routes back into the zone before shooting, creating staggered shots for the goalie.
coaching_points: Attack the loose puck area with pace.
Keep the head up while choosing a puck and route.
Swoop back into the zone under control.
Stagger the shots so the goalie can reset.

title: Continuous Breakouts - #1
description: A continuous breakout warm-up. The defense carries the puck around the net and hits a forward timing a curl for the breakout pass. After the pass, the defense pivots back to retrieve the next dump-in while the forward attacks the far end for a shot.
coaching_points: Defense retrieves with urgency and stays inside the dots.
Forwards time the curl and face the puck.
Make the breakout pass flat and in stride.
Transition quickly from supporting the rush back into the next retrieval.

title: Continuous Chip Drill
description: A continuous winger breakout drill. The coach rims a puck around the boards, one forward works to control and chip it high off the wall into neutral ice, and a supporting forward times the route to collect the chip and attack the far end.
coaching_points: Get to the wall before the rim arrives.
Gain control and create separation before chipping the puck.
Use the boards to place the puck into safe neutral ice.
Supporting forward times the route to arrive with speed.

title: Double Chip Off Boards
description: A breakout progression with a second chip off the boards to a supporting forward in neutral ice. The player making the chip drives hard to the far post and becomes a scoring option for the supporting player.
coaching_points: Use the boards to move the puck through pressure.
Support the first chip with proper neutral-zone timing.
Drive the far post after moving the puck.
Look to turn the second touch into an immediate attack.

title: Center Timing Drill
description: A full-ice breakout and regroup timing drill. The forward works with two defensive pairs, first timing a defensive-zone breakout pass and then staying available through neutral ice for a regroup pass before attacking back toward the original end.
coaching_points: Forward stays underneath the puck and times each route for a flat pass.
Defense supports partner-to-partner puck movement.
Receive and move the puck while skating.
Progress to a 1 on 1 by having the breakout defenseman gap up.

title: Middle Man - Small Area Game
category: Passing / Neutral Zone / Small Area Games
description: A possession game built around a designated middle player who must stay inside the center circle. After a turnover, the team in possession has to use its Middle Man before it can score, forcing players to create passing lanes and find support through traffic.
coaching_points: Find the Middle Man quickly after a change of possession.
Move away from the puck to create clean passing lanes.
The Middle Man must stay available while also defending the circle.
Keep the puck moving instead of holding it under pressure.

title: Here you go, there you go.
description: A one-touch passing warm-up for groups of four to seven players. One player works in the middle of a circle, calls for a puck, returns it to the same outside player, then turns to a new option and repeats for a timed interval.
coaching_points: Call for the puck before every reception.
Use one-touch passes whenever the skill level allows.
Turn the head and body early to identify the next option.
Keep the passing rhythm high for the full work interval.

title: Pivot,Receive, Shoot
description: A half-ice shooting warm-up that combines forward-to-backward pivoting with receiving a pass in stride. Players skate to a marker, pivot while facing the passer, transition forward at the blue line and receive a pass before attacking for a shot and rebound.
coaching_points: Stay facing the passer through the pivot.
Accelerate forward as the player comes out of the transition.
Receive the pass with the feet moving.
Shoot low from the outside angle and stay at the net for a rebound.

title: Loose Puck Transition 1 on 1
description: A full-ice transition drill that begins with a defenseman retrieving a loose puck while forwards provide inside-out support. The play moves through neutral ice for a shot, then immediately turns into a 1 on 1 in the opposite direction to challenge the defender's recovery and gap.
coaching_points: Forwards support inside-out while facing the puck.
Time the neutral-zone support route instead of getting ahead of the puck.
Defense should move the puck and immediately regain ice.
Treat the second attack as a quick turnover and establish the gap early.

title: Impossible 3 on 2
description: A defensive-zone coverage drill with two defenders protecting against three attackers. Two offensive players work below the goal line while a third tries to get open in the slot, forcing the defenders to communicate, switch responsibilities and protect the most dangerous scoring area.
coaching_points: Protect the slot player as the first defensive priority.
Communicate switches before releasing coverage.
Use stops and starts rather than drifting through the defensive zone.
Challenge a puck carrier below the goal line only when the slot remains protected.

title: Hard Rim One on One
description: A full-ice breakout-to-1-on-1 drill. Defensemen rim pucks hard around the boards, wingers work to move the rim to a curling center, and the center attacks the opposite defenseman while that defender recovers ice and gaps up.
coaching_points: Wingers arrive at the wall ready to handle the hard rim.
Use a direct pass or controlled chip to move the puck to the center.
Centers time the curl so they receive the puck with speed.
Defensemen recover ice quickly and try to hold the blue line.

title: Timing in Transition 1 on 0
description: A transition timing drill that emphasizes defensemen handling the puck while moving. A defenseman transitions backward to receive from a forward, then moves the puck back to that forward as the forward swings through neutral ice and attacks the far end for a shot.
coaching_points: Defensemen receive the puck while keeping their feet moving.
Create a clean passing angle before returning the puck.
Forwards time the swing so the return pass is flat and in stride.
Attack the offensive zone with speed after the regroup.

title: 3 Prong Warm Up
description: A three-part half-ice warm-up that gives the goalie shots from three different routes and angles. Players attack from below the circle, from a moving outside route and from a puck-control move around a tire before finishing with quick shots.
coaching_points: Keep the feet moving through each shooting route.
Get the shot off quickly after clearing the tire.
Keep warm-up shots low and on net so the goalie can track rebounds.
Shoot off both feet and use good lower-body power.

title: Figure Eight Gap Up 1 on 1
description: A full-ice 1 on 1 drill that develops forward overspeed and defensive footwork. The defense passes to the forward and both players skate separate figure-eight patterns before the forward uses a quick give-and-go, exits with speed and attacks the defender down ice.
coaching_points: Forwards keep their feet moving through the entire figure-eight pattern.
Explode out of each turn instead of gliding.
Defense stays facing the forward and exits slightly ahead to read speed and close the gap.
Defender should engage the rush before the offensive blue line.

title: Russian 3 on 3
category: 3 on 3 / Small Area Games / Half Ice
description: A sectional 3 on 3 small-area game designed to create offensive support and defensive-zone coverage habits. Players remain in designated sections while trying to move the puck to teammates in the opposite section or create a scoring chance from their own area.
coaching_points: Offensive players move to open ice and stay available as support options.
Defenders protect dangerous space and avoid overcommitting.
Communicate constantly between the two sections.
Use short, intense shifts and add a second puck as an awareness progression.

title: Round A Round
description: A full-ice flow warm-up built around quick give-and-go passing and a long shot. Players work from four blue-line stations, exchange two quick passes while changing their angle, then curl up the boards and attack the net for a shot.
coaching_points: Make the first return pass immediately after receiving the puck.
Change the passing angle before delivering the second pass.
Keep the feet moving through the curl and transition.
Time the next player so the drill flows continuously without congestion.

title: Iron Cross #1
description: A conditioning and footwork drill performed around a faceoff circle. Players repeatedly stop, start, side-step and skate forward or backward between the center dot, hash marks and top and bottom of the circle while always keeping their body facing forward.
coaching_points: Come to a complete stop at every change of direction.
Stay facing forward during the side-step portions.
Explode immediately out of each stop.
Maintain good knee bend and edge control as fatigue increases.

title: Three Puck Conditioning
description: A high-work-rate half-ice conditioning drill that can run from both ends. A player attacks three separate puck locations in sequence, skating hard between each puck and finishing each repetition with a shot before moving to the next puck.
coaching_points: Use an appropriate work-to-rest ratio so every repetition stays fast.
Sprint to each puck instead of coasting between locations.
Keep the feet moving through each shot.
Use different puck placements to change the skating distance and workload.

title: Christmas Tree Conditioning
description: A demanding conditioning pattern that uses repeated diagonal sprints and stops to form a Christmas-tree path through the rink. Players work progressively farther across the ice before returning through the pattern.
coaching_points: Skate every segment at game-speed intensity.
Make complete stops before changing direction.
Accelerate hard out of each stop.
Use this late in practice because the repeated stops heavily wear the ice.

title: Full Ice 1 on 1
description: A full-ice 1 on 1 progression that begins with a forward passing to a defenseman at the blue line. The defense walks the puck to the middle for a shot, then recovers up ice while the forward receives a puck from the opposite corner and attacks in a full-ice 1 on 1.
coaching_points: Defense gets the first shot through quickly and immediately retakes ice.
Forwards attack with their feet moving.
Defense should establish the gap early instead of backing into the zone.
Challenge the defender to make the play at or before the blue line.

title: Recovery 2 on 2
description: A full-ice recovery drill where defenders begin retreating and must transition forward to recover after being beaten in neutral ice, while backcheckers start from the hash marks and chase the rush. Two forwards attack with urgency before the recovering defenders can re-establish position.
coaching_points: Defenders open the hips directly into a forward recovery stride instead of crossing over.
Sprint to the near post and recover inside position.
Backcheckers work through the middle and get back into the play.
Forwards attack immediately and drive both the puck and the weak-side player toward the net.

title: Defense Elements
description: A defense-specific half-ice station combining breakout passes, blue-line movement, shooting, net-front screens and puck retrievals. Four players rotate through the passing, shooting and screening roles while the primary defenseman retrieves and controls multiple pucks around the net.
coaching_points: Move the first breakout pass quickly and accurately.
Blue-line player walks toward the middle before shooting.
Net-front player establishes a screen or presents the stick for a tip.
Retrieving defenseman keeps the feet moving and controls the puck around both cones.

title: 1 on 0 with Backchecker
description: A continuous full-ice speed and backchecking competition. A player attacks on a 1 on 0 and shoots with the feet moving, then stops and immediately backchecks against the next player, who starts as soon as the shot is taken.
coaching_points: Attack the net at full speed and shoot without gliding.
Stop immediately after the shot and transition into the backcheck.
Backcheck through the middle with urgency.
Use the competitive chase to maintain maximum skating effort.

title: Defensive Figure Eights
description: A defense-focused footwork and passing drill built around figure-eight routes. Defensemen receive passes while moving, turn up ice with their head up, and work on making the next play quickly during a neutral-zone transition.
coaching_points: Keep the feet moving through every turn and transition.
Receive the puck with the head up and scan before turning up ice.
Move the puck to the open option quickly.
Recognize when there is enough space to carry the puck and become part of the rush.

title: Defense Transition into 2-0
description: A defense regroup drill that emphasizes proper support spacing between partners. The defenseman without the puck stays slightly behind and underneath, receives a partner pass, accelerates up ice and then moves the puck to the forwards to initiate a 2 on 0 attack.
coaching_points: Support underneath and slightly behind the puck-carrying defenseman.
Avoid unnecessary full-width lateral passes.
Explode up ice after receiving the D-to-D pass.
Become a threat by carrying, passing, or joining the rush after moving the puck.

title: Dump with Give & Go
description: A defense retrieval and breakout drill focused on backward-to-forward pivots and the first pass. The defenseman retrieves a puck from the corner, gains the far post with feet moving, stays inside the dots when turning up ice and makes a breakout pass before continuing through the play.
coaching_points: Keep the feet moving through the corner retrieval.
Gain the far post before turning up ice.
Stay inside the faceoff dots to create a safe breakout lane.
Make the first pass in stride and continue skating up ice after moving the puck.

title: 2 on 1 Down Low
category: 2 on 1 / Half Ice / Small Area Games
description: A quick down-low 2 on 1 battle where the defender begins at a disadvantage. The defender starts on their knees with their back to the forwards; on the whistle the coach feeds either forward and the three players immediately compete around the net.
coaching_points: Forwards attack immediately before the defender can recover.
Use quick puck movement to create a back-door or net-front chance.
Defender recovers inside-out and protects the middle first.
Keep the puck below the dots and play through contact around the net.

title: 4 on 2 Down Low
description: A down-low overload drill that recreates a power-play scoring situation. One playmaker works from behind or beside the net while three scoring options occupy dangerous areas in front, forcing two defenders to protect multiple passing and shooting threats.
coaching_points: Playmaker scans before receiving and attacks from either side of the net.
Offensive players move to open scoring space instead of standing still.
Use quick passes to force the two defenders to change coverage.
Defenders communicate and protect the most dangerous net-front options first.

title: Re-Group 1 on 1
description: A defense gap-control progression that begins with backward skating, a pass exchange around cones and a regroup. The defender eventually carries toward center, passes to a waiting forward and times the pivot to establish a playable gap for the ensuing 1 on 1.
coaching_points: Keep the feet moving during the backward portion.
Execute the pass exchanges while maintaining body control around the cones.
Defender times the pivot so the gap is established early.
Aim to make the defensive play at or before the blue line.

title: Lateral Yo Yo
description: A two-player passing and footwork drill through a staggered cone pattern. Players move laterally across the neutral zone, keep their heads up and exchange passes between each set of cones before both transition forward for separate shots.
coaching_points: Keep the head up while moving laterally.
Complete at least one pass between every set of cones.
Use active feet instead of gliding through the pattern.
Pivot forward quickly at the far side and finish with controlled shots.

title: One Man Regroup
description: A full-ice regroup drill that works both forward timing and defense gap control. The forward times a curl to stay underneath the puck for a flat pass, while the defense moves the puck and then gets up ice to establish the gap for a 1 on 1.
coaching_points: Forward stays underneath the puck and avoids getting too far ahead of the pass.
Create a flat passing lane instead of a dangerous vertical pass.
Defense moves the puck and immediately retakes ice.
Establish the gap early and make the play at or before the blue line.

title: Sabres Defense Drill
description: A continuous team drill combining net-front defending, breakout execution and backchecking. A forward and defender first battle at the net, then a defenseman retrieves and breaks the puck out to start a rush while the previous forward tracks back to create a 2 on 2.
coaching_points: Defenders battle for inside position at the net.
Breakout defenseman carries with the feet moving and makes a clean first pass.
Backchecking forward transitions immediately when the breakout begins.
Communicate through the rush as the drill flows continuously end to end.

title: Blue Line 1 vs. 1
description: A full-ice 1 on 1 drill that challenges defenders to improve backward skating speed. Forwards swing behind the net to receive passes while defenders skate forward to the wall and then continue backward along the blue line before matching the oncoming attacker.
coaching_points: Defense stays backward instead of turning forward to chase.
Increase backward skating speed while maintaining balance and gap.
Forward receives the pass in motion and attacks with speed.
Defender identifies the attacker early and closes space before the blue line.

title: Escape, Pass, Follow
description: A defense-to-forward passing sequence built around an escape move. The defenseman receives a pass while skating backward, uses an escape to create space, moves the puck across ice to a forward for a long shot, then times a second high-slot pass after the forward retrieves a puck from the corner.
coaching_points: Defense receives the first pass with the feet moving.
Use the escape move to create a better passing lane before moving the puck.
Forward follows the first shot for a rebound before retrieving the next puck.
Defense times the high-slot arrival instead of getting there too early.

title: Backwards Circle Passing
description: An advanced defensive footwork drill where two defensemen circle a pair of cones in opposite directions while always facing each other. They continuously pivot between forward and backward skating and exchange the puck throughout the movement.
coaching_points: Stay facing the partner throughout the entire pattern.
Pass while the feet are moving and the body is transitioning.
Keep the puck in a position where the next pass can be made quickly.
Reverse the skating direction after a timed interval to work both sides.

title: Neutral Zone Give & Go
description: A full-ice defense skating and passing drill. The player receives a pass, pivots around a cone, moves the puck to a coach in the middle, transitions backward near the red line, receives the return pass, pivots forward and finishes with another give-and-go before shooting.
coaching_points: Keep the feet moving throughout the entire sequence.
Stay facing the puck during the backward transition.
Make firm passes and present a target for each return pass.
Accelerate out of the final pivot before attacking the net.

title: Turnover 1 on 1
description: A neutral-zone turnover simulation that quickly becomes a 1 on 1. The defenseman begins by moving into a shot, then receives a puck from the previous forward, advances up ice and makes a cross-ice pass to a timed forward before recovering to defend the rush.
coaching_points: Forward times the route so the cross-ice pass arrives before the red line.
Defense moves the puck and immediately recovers ice.
Defender gets the heels outside the blue line before matching the rush.
Attack the 1 on 1 with speed before the defender can fully reset.

title: Tip Drill into 2 on 2
description: A full-ice 2 on 2 progression that starts with a point shot, screen and tip. After the rebound phase, the two forwards receive a new puck from the corner and attack the two defensemen in transition for a 2 on 2 rush.
coaching_points: Establish a screen and present the stick for the point shot.
Compete for the rebound before transitioning to the rush.
Defense gets up ice quickly to establish the gap.
Try to stand the rush up at or before the blue line.

title: 10 Second 2 on 2 Down Low
category: 2 on 2 / Half Ice / Small Area Games
description: A ten-second down-low 2 on 2 battle. The coach rims a puck into the corner and the two forwards attack while the two defenders protect the net area. The rep ends after a score, a defensive clear, or the timed interval.
coaching_points: Forwards keep their feet moving and use quick turns in the corners.
Protect the puck until a clean net-front option appears.
Defenders recover inside position and protect the middle first.
Keep shifts short and intense so every battle is played at game pace.

title: 1 on 1 Battle Down Low
description: A low-zone 1 on 1 battle where the defender begins from a recovery disadvantage behind the net while the forward starts with a puck along the wall. On the whistle the forward attacks and the defender recovers to protect the net.
coaching_points: Forward attacks immediately and stays below the dots.
Use puck protection and quick changes of direction to create separation.
Defender recovers inside-out and protects the direct lane to the net.
Progress to 2 on 1 or 2 on 2 once players understand the battle concepts.

title: Yo Yo Transition Skating
description: A paired transition skating drill for defensemen. One player skates forward as the rabbit while the partner transitions backward and works to keep the rabbit in front, then the roles reverse as the pattern moves back and forth across the ice.
coaching_points: Transition without crossing the feet unnecessarily.
Keep the chest square to the forward skater.
Adjust the distance between lines to change the gap challenge.
Use short explosive repetitions to train backward speed.

title: Tight Transition 1 on 1
description: A difficult half-ice 1 on 1 that forces the defender to transition quickly from forward skating to backward gap control. The forward and defender skate to the red line, stop, and race back toward the zone, with the forward collecting a puck and attacking immediately.
coaching_points: Defender comes to a complete stop at the red line before transitioning backward.
Keep the attacker to the outside as long as possible.
If beaten, open up and recover hard to the near post.
Forward attacks with speed immediately after collecting the puck.

title: High Slot Give & Gos
description: A high-slot passing and footwork drill. The active player skates figure eights around two cones while always facing the net, receives passes from alternating stationary players and quickly moves the puck to the opposite passer before finishing with a shot.
coaching_points: Stay facing the net throughout every pivot around the cones.
Keep the feet moving instead of gliding between passes.
Control each reception and move the puck to the opposite passer quickly.
Maintain balance and edge control through the figure-eight pattern.

title: 2 on 0 into 1 vs. 1
description: A full-ice transition progression that begins as a 2 on 0 and then immediately turns into a counterattack 1 on 1. After the defense joins the first rush and takes a point shot, a coach feeds a third forward through the slot for a quick full-ice attack against that same defenseman.
coaching_points: Defense must be ready to defend immediately after taking the point shot.
Forward times the counterattack swing through the slot.
Defense recovers ice quickly and establishes the gap early.
Treat the second phase like a turnover and transition without hesitation.

title: 1 on 1 from Center Ice
description: A full-ice 1 on 1 starting from center ice. The defender passes to a forward in the corner, then skates around a cone and pivots from forward to backward while the forward attacks straight down the ice.
coaching_points: Forward cannot leave until the pass is received.
Defender pivots early enough to establish a controlled gap.
Protect the blue line rather than retreating too deep.
Use angle and stick position to steer the attacker outside.

title: 2 on 0 Neutral Zone Swing
description: A neutral-zone transition drill where the defense receives and moves the puck while skating backward, then transitions forward and finds one of two swinging forwards. The forwards attack 2 on 0 while the defense resets for the next repetition.
coaching_points: Defense receives passes with the feet moving.
Make clean D-to-D passes because poor puck movement breaks down the timing.
Second defenseman transitions forward before making the outlet pass.
